dietary_lever_atoms.evidence_limitation: Catalytic capacity does not show that extra dietary magnesium increases regional catecholamine clearance or improves function. COMT isoforms, genotype, SAM availability and tissue homeostasis constrain interpretation; increased clearance is not universally desirable.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Tyrosine
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Tyrosine is the starting material used to make dopamine.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Iron
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Iron helps the enzyme that carries out the first step in making dopamine from tyrosine.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Vitamin B6
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Vitamin B6 is converted into PLP, the active cofactor used in the final step of dopamine synthesis.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4)
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: BH4 helps the enzyme that converts tyrosine into L-DOPA, the first step in making dopamine.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Pair non-haem iron-containing meals with an ascorbic-acid source
system_optimisation_practices.presentation_label: Pair non-haem iron-containing meals with an ascorbic-acid source
system_optimisation_practices.biological_role: Ascorbic acid can counter phytate- and polyphenol-related inhibition and improve non-haem iron absorption at the meal level. Iron is a required cofactor for tyrosine hydroxylase.
system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: Evidence supports improved non-haem iron absorption at the meal level; it does not establish improved iron status or any change in dopamine biology or function.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Use validated phytate-reducing preparation methods for high-phytate cereals
system_optimisation_practices.presentation_label: Use validated phytate-reducing preparation methods for high-phytate cereals
system_optimisation_practices.biological_role: Phytase treatment can reduce phytate inhibition and improve non-haem iron absorption from some cereal matrices. Iron is a required cofactor for tyrosine hydroxylase.
system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: Improved absorption was matrix-dependent and did not consistently translate into better long-term iron status; no dopamine-related outcome was measured.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Short-term selective dietary-fat restriction in adults with obesity under controlled conditions
system_optimisation_practices.presentation_label: Short-term selective dietary-fat restriction in adults with obesity under controlled conditions
system_optimisation_practices.biological_role: Five days of selective isocaloric fat restriction reduced striatal D2/D3 receptor binding potential and food-cue activity in adults with obesity; selective carbohydrate restriction did not produce the same change.
system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: Evidence comes from 17 adults with obesity in a short inpatient experiment; reduced binding potential does not by itself distinguish receptor change from greater endogenous dopamine occupancy.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Short-term very-low-calorie dieting in adults with obesity
system_optimisation_practices.presentation_label: Short-term very-low-calorie dieting in adults with obesity
system_optimisation_practices.biological_role: About ten days of very-low-calorie dieting reduced substantia-nigra D2/D3 receptor binding potential in women with obesity, and regional changes tracked reductions in leptin.
system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: The uncontrolled study involved 15 women with obesity and cannot establish whether the imaging change reflects altered receptor availability or endogenous dopamine occupancy.

lifestyle_priorities.biological_role: Voluntary mild-to-moderate cycling produced a PET signal consistent with dorsal-striatal dopamine release, which was associated with faster Go/No-Go reaction time.
lifestyle_priorities.evidence_limitation: Evidence is limited to a small acute study in healthy adults; the dopamine–performance association was correlational and does not establish chronic or clinical benefit.

lifestyle_priorities.biological_role: One night of total sleep deprivation reduced PET-measured ventral-striatal D2/D3 receptor availability and was associated with lower alertness in healthy adults.
lifestyle_priorities.evidence_limitation: Evidence concerns acute total sleep deprivation in a small healthy sample and does not establish effects of habitual sleep patterns.

candidate_cross_brs_relationships.relationship_scope: One-carbon metabolism and SAM-dependent COMT activity
Catecholamine oxidation, oxidative burden and antioxidant handling
Energetic requirements for synthesis, vesicular handling and neuronal signalling
Metabolic, stress-related and circadian modulation of dopaminergic function

phenome_relationships.rationale: Dopamine contributes to working memory and cognitive control, but the relationship is nonlinear and depends on baseline state and whether prefrontal stability or striatal updating is required {{cite:cools_inverted-u_2011}}. ADHD imaging findings are heterogeneous across dopamine processes, regions and medication histories rather than showing a uniform dopamine deficit {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024,fusar-poli_striatal_2012}}.

Striatal dopamine synthesis capacity and controlled dopaminergic manipulation alter willingness to expend cognitive effort by changing benefit-versus-cost weighting, supporting a direct relationship with effort allocation rather than a general “reward chemical” account {{cite:westbrook_dopamine_2020}}.

Dopamine can influence willingness to sustain cognitive effort, but the strongest assessed human study measured effort choice rather than fatigue or performance decline over time {{cite:westbrook_dopamine_2020}}. Cognitive energy remains a multi-system outcome, and a dopamine-specific fatigue claim is unresolved.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Dopamine synthesis requires distinct substrate and cofactor steps
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Dopamine synthesis proceeds through tyrosine hydroxylase and aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase. Iron and tetrahydrobiopterin support the hydroxylase step, while pyridoxal-5′-phosphate supports decarboxylation{{cite:fanet_tetrahydrobioterin_2021,beard_iron_2003,kennedy_b_2016}}. These biochemical requirements do not show that extra intake increases dopamine in an adequately nourished human brain.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This finding supports tyrosine as the hydroxylase substrate, iron, PLP and vitamin B6 as dietary-requirement atoms, and BH4 as an endogenous biochemical cofactor; none is an intake-responsive dopamine lever.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Neuronal dopamine synthesis depends on separable tyrosine-hydroxylase and aromatic L-amino-acid-decarboxylase reactions with iron, tetrahydrobiopterin and pyridoxal-5′-phosphate requirements; cofactor requirement is not evidence of intake responsiveness.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Biochemical reviews identify tetrahydrobiopterin and iron as requirements for aromatic amino-acid hydroxylation and pyridoxal-5′-phosphate as a catecholamine-synthesis cofactor. Experimental iron deficiency alters striatal and nucleus-accumbens dopamine metabolites in rats, supporting biological sensitivity under deficiency. Together this establishes pathway dependence, not ordinary-diet control of human brain dopamine.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The most direct deficiency evidence is preclinical, and the reviewed sources do not establish common inadequacy in a defined clinical population, responsiveness when baseline status is adequate, or functional benefit mediated by dopamine.

evidence_considered.label: Fanet et al. (2021)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: BH4 is required for aromatic amino-acid hydroxylation and therefore for dopamine synthesis.

assessment.study: Narrative biochemical review of tetrahydrobiopterin and monoamine synthesis pathways.
assessment.population: Mixed mechanistic literature; not a defined dietary intervention population.
assessment.result: Identified BH4 as necessary for aromatic amino-acid hydroxylation and monoamine synthesis.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled intake-response effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports reaction-level requirements and pathway boundaries.
assessment.limitations: Does not establish that increasing dietary intake modifies human brain dopamine or improves function.

evidence_considered.label: Erikson et al. (2000)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary iron deficiency
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Increasing severity of iron deficiency altered locomotor activity and dopamine metabolites in rat striatum and nucleus accumbens.

assessment.study: Controlled rat dietary iron-deficiency experiment with regional dopamine-metabolite and locomotor outcomes.
assessment.population: Laboratory rats under graded iron deficiency.
assessment.result: Iron deficiency changed regional dopamine-metabolite profiles and locomotor activity, with severity-dependent effects.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Directional severity-response; no human-equivalent effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports dopamine-system sensitivity to marked iron deficiency.
assessment.limitations: Animal deficiency model; metabolite concentrations do not directly measure synthesis flux or predict human clinical benefit.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Beard et al. (2003)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews iron-dependent dopamine biology and behavioural consequences of deficiency.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Review-level and predominantly preclinical; it does not add a human intake-to-dopamine estimate.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Kennedy (2016)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews B-vitamin roles in neurochemical synthesis, including vitamin B6 as a cofactor context for dopamine formation.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: General B-vitamin review; it does not isolate aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase or show an intake-to-dopamine response.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Spector (1978)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Shows that B6 vitamers enter the central nervous system and contribute to the brain vitamin B6 pool.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Rabbit transport study; it does not measure dopamine synthesis, release or function.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Dopamine supports cognitive control nonlinearly
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human pharmacology and patient studies show that dopamine effects on working memory and control depend on baseline state, brain region and task. Both insufficient and excessive stimulation can impair performance.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Dopamine is not a single directional cognitive-performance variable; “more dopamine” is not a valid general recommendation.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Dopaminergic modulation of working memory and cognitive control follows baseline-, region- and process-dependent nonlinear relationships rather than a uniformly beneficial direction.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The reviewed human evidence supports an inverted-U framework in which prefrontal stability and striatal flexibility can respond differently to dopaminergic manipulation. Baseline dopamine, receptor context, region and cognitive demand explain why the same manipulation may improve one process or participant while impairing another.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The synthesis integrates pharmacological studies, Parkinson disease withdrawal studies and preclinical evidence. Drug effects may include non-dopaminergic actions and do not establish nutritional modifiability.

evidence_considered.label: Cools & D'Esposito (2011)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: pharmacological dopaminergic manipulation and medication withdrawal
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Dopaminergic effects on working memory and cognitive control varied with baseline dopamine, brain region and stability-versus-flexibility demand, consistent with an inverted-U relationship.

assessment.study: Mechanistic review of experimental animals, healthy-human pharmacology and Parkinson disease medication-withdrawal studies.
assessment.population: Healthy adults and people with Parkinson disease, with supporting animal evidence.
assessment.result: Both low and high dopaminergic stimulation could impair cognition; effects differed between prefrontal stability and striatal flexibility.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled effect estimate; direction depended on baseline and task.
assessment.evidence_summary: Directly rejects a unitary more-is-better dopamine model for cognition.
assessment.limitations: Heterogeneous paradigms and pharmacological exposures; not a dietary intervention synthesis.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Striatal dopamine influences willingness to expend cognitive effort
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In healthy adults, higher striatal dopamine synthesis capacity predicted greater willingness to choose demanding cognitive work, while methylphenidate and sulpiride shifted benefit-versus-cost weighting most in people with lower synthesis capacity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports effort allocation and motivation, not a claim that dopamine simply increases energy or that diet reproduces medication effects.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Striatal dopamine synthesis capacity and controlled dopaminergic manipulation influence cognitive-effort choice by altering benefit-versus-cost weighting.
scientific_findings.synthesis: PET-derived synthesis capacity and a placebo-controlled pharmacology design converged on a baseline-dependent role for dopamine in cognitive motivation. Higher synthesis capacity increased benefit weighting on placebo, and drug effects were larger at lower baseline capacity.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: A modest healthy-adult sample and an effort-choice task do not establish sustained performance, fatigue resistance, clinical benefit or dietary modification. Methylphenidate also affects noradrenaline.

evidence_considered.label: Westbrook et al. (2020)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: methylphenidate, sulpiride and placebo
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Higher striatal dopamine synthesis capacity and dopaminergic drugs increased willingness to expend cognitive effort by strengthening benefit relative to cost weighting.

assessment.study: Within-participant pharmacological study combined with PET measurement of striatal dopamine synthesis capacity and computational modelling of effort choices.
assessment.population: Fifty healthy adults; complete model estimates were available for a smaller subset depending on analysis.
assessment.result: Baseline synthesis capacity predicted cognitive motivation, and methylphenidate and sulpiride increased motivation most at lower baseline capacity.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reported model coefficients and baseline interactions; no general clinical effect size.
assessment.evidence_summary: Provides human mechanistic evidence linking a measured dopamine process to cognitive-effort allocation.
assessment.limitations: Healthy sample, acute drugs, modest size, choice rather than endurance; methylphenidate is not dopamine-selective.

scientific_findings.finding_label: D2-receptor signalling contributes to cognitive flexibility
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human pharmacological evidence supports a role for D2-receptor signalling in set shifting, while broader evidence shows that dopamine effects vary by task, baseline state and frontostriatal locus.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Flexibility and stability can move in opposite directions; receptor engagement is not equivalent to a global dopamine concentration change.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Dopamine, including D2-receptor signalling, contributes to cognitive flexibility and set shifting in a task- and baseline-dependent manner.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A human agonist-antagonist pretreatment experiment provided receptor-specific evidence that D2 signalling contributes to flexibility, while a broader review situated this within frontostriatal and clinical evidence. The combined result supports a functional role without implying uniform enhancement.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Acute pharmacology in healthy volunteers and mixed human/animal review evidence do not quantify everyday dopamine function, nutritional modification or clinical treatment effects.

evidence_considered.label: van der Schaaf et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: bromocriptine with sulpiride pretreatment
evidence_considered.directional_finding: The effect of a dopamine agonist on cognitive flexibility was abolished by D2-antagonist pretreatment, supporting D2-receptor involvement.

assessment.study: Double pharmacological challenge study of task switching in healthy young adults.
assessment.population: Healthy young adult volunteers.
assessment.result: Bromocriptine changed flexibility performance and sulpiride pretreatment blocked the effect.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Task-specific drug interaction; no general cognitive enhancement estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Strengthens receptor-specific attribution for human cognitive flexibility.
assessment.limitations: Acute pharmacology, limited sample, and no dietary or clinical outcome.

evidence_considered.label: Klanker et al. (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human and animal evidence linked striatal dopamine to reversal learning and set shifting, with direction contingent on receptor, baseline state and task.

assessment.study: Narrative review of pharmacological, genetic, patient and animal studies of cognitive flexibility.
assessment.population: Healthy humans, clinical groups and experimental animals.
assessment.result: Supported dopamine involvement but not a single direction across flexibility paradigms.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Provides scope and heterogeneity context around the receptor-specific experiment.
assessment.limitations: Mixed models and designs; review predates newer evidence and does not establish dietary modification.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Aging affects dopamine targets differently
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Across 95 imaging studies, healthy aging was associated with lower dopamine receptor and transporter measures, while synthesis capacity was not significantly lower.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Age-related change is process-specific; receptor or transporter decline must not be restated as global dopamine depletion.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Healthy aging is associated with declines in dopamine receptor and transporter availability but not a significant pooled decline in dopamine synthesis capacity.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The meta-analysis separated receptors, transporters and synthesis measures across PET and SPECT studies. Moderate-to-large negative age associations were found for receptors and transporters, with larger effects for D1-like than D2-like receptors, while synthesis capacity was spared on average.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Cross-sectional imaging cannot establish within-person decline or causal cognitive effects. Ligands and regions varied, and availability measures are not dopamine concentration.

evidence_considered.label: Karrer et al. (2017)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Age was negatively associated with dopamine receptors and transporters but not significantly with synthesis capacity.

assessment.study: Meta-analysis of cross-sectional PET and SPECT studies of distinct dopamine targets.
assessment.population: Ninety-five studies comprising 2,611 healthy adults.
assessment.result: Receptor and transporter measures declined by target-specific amounts with age; synthesis capacity did not show a significant pooled age effect.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Average age reductions across assessed dopamine targets ranged from 3.7% to 14.0% per decade.
assessment.evidence_summary: Directly establishes process-specific age variation and rejects a global decline formulation.
assessment.limitations: Cross-sectional studies, heterogeneous ligands and regions, and no direct mediation test for cognitive decline.

scientific_findings.finding_label: ADHD does not show one uniform dopamine abnormality
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Dopamine biology is relevant to ADHD, but imaging and mechanistic findings differ by dopamine process, brain region, developmental stage, medication exposure and study method. The evidence does not support ADHD as a uniform global dopamine-deficiency disorder.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Medication target engagement supports dopamine relevance but cannot identify a universal baseline lesion or establish nutritional modifiability.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: ADHD-related dopamine findings are heterogeneous across synthesis, release, receptors and transporter measures and do not establish a uniform global dopamine deficit.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A recent broad evaluation found hypo-, hyper- and null findings across human and animal evidence. A transporter meta-analysis found an average group difference but large heterogeneity and a strong relationship with prior psychostimulant exposure. Together these support dopamine as one relevant regulatory domain while making medication history, region, age and measured process essential to interpretation.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Small samples, different tracers and diagnostic groups, medication confounding and cross-sectional designs limit causal interpretation. Transporter binding, synthesis capacity, receptor availability and extracellular release are not interchangeable.

evidence_considered.label: MacDonald et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human and animal findings did not consistently support a generalized hypodopaminergic ADHD state; results varied by process, region, task and population.

assessment.study: Critical review of the dopamine hypothesis across human studies and animal models.
assessment.population: Children and adults with ADHD, healthy comparison groups and ADHD-relevant animal models.
assessment.result: Reported lower, higher and null dopamine-related findings and concluded that a simple global deficiency model is not supported.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled global effect estimate because dopamine processes and methods were heterogeneous.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports dopamine relevance while constraining the direction and universality of the ADHD interpretation.
assessment.limitations: Broad narrative synthesis across heterogeneous methods; many studies were small or medication-confounded.

evidence_considered.label: Fusar-Poli et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Striatal dopamine-transporter density was 14% higher on average in ADHD, but heterogeneity was large and medication exposure materially moderated the result.

assessment.study: Meta-analysis of nine PET and SPECT studies of striatal dopamine-transporter binding.
assessment.population: 169 participants with ADHD and 173 matched controls.
assessment.result: Average transporter density was higher in ADHD, but studies were significantly heterogeneous and medication exposure explained important variation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Approximately 14% higher mean striatal transporter density in the ADHD group.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows a process-specific group difference while demonstrating why medication history cannot be ignored.
assessment.limitations: Small number of imaging studies, heterogeneous tracers and designs, and transporter binding is not dopamine concentration or release.

scientific_findings.finding_label: L-tyrosine did not provide sustained ADHD benefit
scientific_findings.finding_summary: A small open trial in adults with attention deficit disorder reported an initial response to L-tyrosine that disappeared as tolerance developed.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The study does not establish sustained clinical benefit, dopamine target engagement, or a food-based treatment claim.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Open-label L-tyrosine supplementation did not produce a sustained ADHD benefit and did not demonstrate modification of brain dopamine biology.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The trial is retained as non-supportive clinical evidence at the boundary between precursor provision and PM3 signalling. An initial symptom response was not sustained, and no dopamine process was measured.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Very small, uncontrolled, older study with no placebo group, no dopamine biomarker and limited diagnostic comparability to current ADHD definitions.

evidence_considered.label: Reimherr & Ward (1987)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: isolated L-tyrosine supplement
evidence_considered.directional_finding: An initial symptom response in some adults disappeared during continued treatment as tolerance developed.

assessment.study: Open-label L-tyrosine trial without placebo control.
assessment.population: Twelve adults diagnosed with attention deficit disorder.
assessment.result: Initial response was not sustained during continued supplementation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Small uncontrolled sample; no robust comparative effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Does not support sustained L-tyrosine treatment efficacy and provides no evidence of dopamine target engagement.
assessment.limitations: Open label, n=12, older diagnostic framework, no dopamine measurement, and tolerance confounds interpretation.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Meal preparation can improve non-haem iron absorption
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human absorption studies show that ascorbic-acid pairing and phytate degradation can increase non-haem iron absorption from selected meals. This supports iron-delivery practices only; neither study measured brain dopamine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Preparation and pairing can improve iron absorption from a meal. Iron is required by tyrosine hydroxylase, but these studies did not test brain iron delivery, dopamine signalling or cognition.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Ascorbic-acid pairing and validated phytate degradation can increase meal-level non-haem iron absorption in matrix-dependent human studies, but no direct dopamine effect has been demonstrated.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A controlled meal study found that ascorbic acid countered dose-dependent phytate and polyphenol inhibition of non-haem iron absorption. A separate human radioiron study found that complete phytate degradation increased iron absorption from several water-prepared cereal porridges, with smaller or absent effects in some matrices. A later review of 42 human interventions found that most dephytinisation and phytase studies improved short-term iron or zinc bioavailability while identifying limited long-term evidence.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: These studies measured gastrointestinal mineral absorption or bioavailability, not human brain iron delivery, dopamine synthesis, dopamine release or functional benefit. Results depend on meal matrix and baseline status, and no dopamine-specific dose or preparation prescription is established.

evidence_considered.label: Siegenberg et al. (1991)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: ascorbic acid added to phytate- or tannin-containing test meals
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Ascorbic acid prevented dose-dependent inhibition of non-haem iron absorption by phytate and polyphenols under the tested meal conditions.

assessment.study: Controlled human test-meal iron-absorption study.
assessment.population: 199 adult participants across the meal experiments.
assessment.result: Iron absorption fell as phytate or tannic acid increased; ascorbic acid countered this inhibition in a context- and dose-dependent manner.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Thirty milligrams of ascorbic acid overcame inhibition from the tested maize-bran phytate exposure; higher tannic-acid exposure required more ascorbic acid under the experimental conditions.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports same-meal ascorbic-acid pairing as an iron-delivery practice.
assessment.limitations: Test-meal absorption rather than long-term iron status; no brain, dopamine or functional endpoint.

evidence_considered.label: Hurrell et al. (2003)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: phytase-dephytinised cereal porridges
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Complete phytate degradation increased iron absorption from several water-prepared cereal porridges, but effects varied by matrix and were reduced or absent with milk and high-tannin sorghum.

assessment.study: Controlled human radioiron-absorption experiments across nine cereal porridges.
assessment.population: 78 adults distributed across the test-meal comparisons.
assessment.result: Dephytinisation increased absorption from rice, oat, maize, wheat and wheat-soy porridges prepared with water, with matrix-specific exceptions.
assessment.effect_magnitude: For example, wheat-porridge absorption rose from 0.99% to 11.54%; effects ranged from absent to approximately twelve-fold across matrices.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports validated phytate reduction as a matrix-dependent iron-delivery practice.
assessment.limitations: Short-term absorption experiments in adults; infant-style test matrices, no long-term status outcome and no brain or dopamine endpoint.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Chondrou et al. (2024)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Narrative review of 42 human interventions found that most dephytinisation and phytase studies improved iron or zinc bioavailability.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Review-level support with heterogeneous matrices and limited long-term status evidence; it adds no dopamine endpoint.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Acute voluntary exercise releases dorsal-striatal dopamine
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In healthy adults, voluntary mild-to-moderate cycling elicited endogenous dopamine release in dorsal striatum, and the PET signal correlated with faster Go/No-Go reaction time. Peripheral muscle stimulation without voluntary central command did not reproduce the behavioural effect.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports an acute state-dependent exercise relationship, not a chronic exercise prescription, clinical treatment claim or global “more dopamine” model.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Acute voluntary cardiovascular exercise can elicit dorsal-striatal dopamine release in healthy adults, with the measured release associated with faster reaction time.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A human PET experiment measured endogenous dopamine release during mild-to-moderate cycling and related it to Go/No-Go performance. Additional electrical-muscle-stimulation experiments suggested that voluntary central command, rather than peripheral movement alone, was important for the reaction-time effect.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The PET experiment was acute and small, and the dopamine-performance association was correlational. It does not establish mediation, chronic adaptation, optimal exercise dosing, ADHD benefit or clinical efficacy.

evidence_considered.label: Ando et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: acute voluntary mild-to-moderate cardiovascular exercise
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Voluntary cycling elicited endogenous dopamine release in caudate and putamen, and greater release was associated with faster Go/No-Go reaction time.

assessment.study: Human PET exercise experiment with two additional electrical-muscle-stimulation experiments.
assessment.population: Sixteen healthy adults in the PET experiment; 18 and 22 healthy adults in the supporting stimulation experiments.
assessment.result: Dorsal-striatal dopamine release occurred during voluntary exercise and correlated with reaction-time improvement; peripheral stimulation alone did not produce the same behavioural effect.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Study-specific PET and reaction-time associations; no clinical effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Provides direct acute human mechanistic evidence for an exercise–dopamine relationship.
assessment.limitations: Small healthy samples, acute exposure, correlational mediation evidence and no chronic, clinical or dietary comparison.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Acute sleep deprivation downregulates ventral-striatal D2/D3 availability
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In healthy adults, one night of total sleep deprivation reduced ventral-striatal D2/D3 receptor availability and was associated with lower alertness and greater sleepiness. The methylphenidate comparison supported receptor downregulation rather than increased dopamine release.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This identifies an acute sleep-state constraint on receptor signalling; it is not evidence that ordinary sleep extension increases dopamine or improves a clinical condition.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: One night of total sleep deprivation reduces ventral-striatal D2/D3 receptor availability in healthy adults and is associated with reduced alertness.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Within-person PET scans after rested sleep and one night of total sleep deprivation showed lower ventral-striatal D2/D3 receptor availability during deprivation. Methylphenidate-induced dopamine increases did not differ by sleep state, supporting receptor downregulation rather than a deprivation-induced rise in dopamine release.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The experiment was acute, involved a small healthy sample and used receptor availability as an imaging construct. It does not establish effects of normal sleep variation, a sleep intervention, chronic outcomes or clinical benefit.

evidence_considered.label: Volkow et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: one night of total sleep deprivation versus rested sleep
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Sleep deprivation reduced ventral-striatal D2/D3 receptor availability, associated with lower alertness and greater sleepiness, without increasing the methylphenidate-evoked dopamine response.

assessment.study: Within-person [11C]raclopride PET study after rested sleep and total sleep deprivation, each under placebo and methylphenidate conditions.
assessment.population: Twenty healthy adults.
assessment.result: Ventral-striatal receptor availability decreased after deprivation and tracked reduced alertness; pharmacological comparison supported receptor downregulation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Region-specific PET change and behavioural associations; no general clinical effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Provides direct human evidence that acute sleep state constrains a specific dopamine-receptor measure.
assessment.limitations: Small healthy sample, one night of total deprivation, pharmacological probe and no chronic or clinical outcome.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Short restrictive dietary protocols alter dopamine receptor binding in obesity
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Two small human PET studies found lower regional D2/D3 receptor binding potential after short restrictive dietary protocols in adults with obesity. The imaging changes are compatible with altered endogenous dopamine occupancy but do not uniquely identify that mechanism.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports two tightly bounded Dietary & Fasting Protocol relationships for adults with obesity, not general reduced-fat or very-low-calorie diet recommendations.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Short-term selective fat restriction and very-low-calorie dieting can alter regional D2/D3 receptor binding potential in adults with obesity under controlled research conditions.
scientific_findings.synthesis: In a randomized inpatient crossover study, five days of selective isocaloric fat restriction reduced striatal D2/D3 binding potential and food-cue activity, whereas selective carbohydrate restriction did not. In a separate before-and-after study, about ten days of very-low-calorie dieting reduced substantia-nigra D2/D3 binding potential in women with obesity, with regional changes tracking leptin reduction.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Both studies were short and population-specific. D2/D3 binding potential reflects receptor availability and competition from endogenous dopamine, so the imaging result cannot by itself distinguish receptor regulation from altered dopamine occupancy.

evidence_considered.label: Darcey et al. (2023)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: five-day selective isocaloric dietary-fat or carbohydrate restriction
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Selective fat restriction reduced striatal D2/D3 receptor binding potential and food-cue activity; selective carbohydrate restriction did not.

assessment.study: Randomized inpatient crossover study using [18F]fallypride PET and food-cue functional MRI.
assessment.population: Seventeen adults with obesity.
assessment.result: D2/D3 binding potential decreased in bilateral striatal clusters after the reduced-fat diet, with no significant change after carbohydrate restriction.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Significant cluster-level reductions in left putamen and right caudate/putamen; no general clinical effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Directly supports a short, controlled dietary-protocol relationship with a specified dopamine imaging measure.
assessment.limitations: Small obesity-specific sample, five-day exposure and no ability to separate receptor regulation from endogenous dopamine occupancy.

evidence_considered.label: Dunn et al. (2017)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: approximately ten days of very-low-calorie dieting
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Very-low-calorie dieting reduced substantia-nigra D2/D3 receptor binding potential, and regional binding changes were associated with reduced leptin.

assessment.study: Before-and-after [18F]fallypride PET study with metabolic and neuroendocrine measurements.
assessment.population: Fifteen women with obesity.
assessment.result: Substantia-nigra D2/D3 binding potential decreased significantly, with nonsignificant trends in other regions; leptin change predicted regional binding change.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Approximately 3 kg mean weight loss; leptin–binding-potential associations were significant across assessed regions.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports a short-term calorie-restriction relationship with a regional dopamine imaging measure.
assessment.limitations: Uncontrolled, small female sample and no ability to separate receptor regulation from endogenous dopamine occupancy.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Remethylation supplies the methionine/SAM resource used by COMT
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Remethylation can replenish methionine for SAM synthesis; human COMT uses SAM to methylate dopamine.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Remethylation can replenish methionine for SAM synthesis; human COMT uses SAM to methylate dopamine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This establishes the connected biochemical supply route, not a measured dietary effect on regional neural SAM or COMT clearance. BHMT is predominantly hepatic/renal; peripheral methionine contribution, local SAM synthesis, alternative supply and turnover vary by tissue. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint and benefit from extra intake in replete individuals remain unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Verified BRS2 PM1/PM2/PM3 Findings establish folate-dependent remethylation, betaine/BHMT remethylation, choline-to-betaine provision and MAT substrate use. Lotta's recombinant human COMT work establishes the downstream methyl-transfer reaction. These successive reactions support upstream resource provision. They do not directly measure transfer of a dietary donor into regional neural SAM or a change in signalling.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This establishes the connected biochemical supply route, not a measured dietary effect on regional neural SAM or COMT clearance. BHMT is predominantly hepatic/renal; peripheral methionine contribution, local SAM synthesis, alternative supply and turnover vary by tissue. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint and benefit from extra intake in replete individuals remain unresolved.

assessment.population: Human proteins expressed in bacterial and insect-cell systems; not a dietary or in-vivo neural trial.
assessment.result: Measured catecholamine methylation and SAM affinity of both enzyme forms.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Different SAM binding affinities; no dietary intake, brain supply or functional effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes SAM use during catecholamine methylation.
assessment.limitations: Primary abstract inspected; full experimental methods/results not obtained. Does not attribute neural SAM supply or clearance changes to donor intake.

scientific_findings.finding_label: The shared LNAA pool presents tyrosine upstream of catecholamine synthesis
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The reviewed LNAA pool supplies tyrosine upstream of dopamine synthesis.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The reviewed LNAA pool supplies tyrosine upstream of dopamine synthesis.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Ordinary dietary LNAA changes do not establish uniform effects on catecholamine synthesis, regional signalling or benefit. The separately recorded competitive capacity-constraint proposition remains unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis: LAT1 presentation supplies tyrosine used by the local hydroxylase reaction already assessed in PM3-F1. This is the same provision job as PM3-DIT-5, not a second limiting constraint.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Ordinary dietary LNAA changes do not establish uniform effects on catecholamine synthesis, regional signalling or benefit. The separately recorded competitive capacity-constraint proposition remains unresolved.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Phenylalanine replenishes tyrosine upstream of catecholamine synthesis
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Phenylalanine can replenish circulating tyrosine upstream of dopamine synthesis; precursor conversion is not evidence that additional intake increases neuronal output.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Phenylalanine can replenish circulating tyrosine upstream of dopamine synthesis; precursor conversion is not evidence that additional intake increases neuronal output.

This does not establish increased dopamine/noradrenaline output, a limiting intake or benefit from extra phenylalanine. Hydroxylation, renal/hepatic function and LNAA competition matter; high phenylalanine is not interchangeable with tyrosine.

scientific_findings.finding_summary: Riboflavin-deficient rats had lower brain mitochondrial MAO activity measured with tyramine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Riboflavin supplies FMN and FAD formation; FAD sustains monoamine oxidase in dopamine metabolism capacity.

title: Noradrenergic Signalling
mission: Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.
summary: Noradrenaline, also called norepinephrine, helps set arousal, vigilance and executive control so attention can stay engaged. Neurons make it from dopamine, then shape the signal through release, receptors, reuptake and breakdown. This coordination lets alertness follow cognitive demand. Iron, vitamin B6, copper and vitamin C take part in that chemistry.
dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based; adequate protein plus cofactor sufficiency
scientific_findings_intro: Structural and biochemical evidence establishes copper and ascorbate participation in the defining dopamine-to-noradrenaline conversion. [[10]](#pm-ref-10) [[9]](#pm-ref-9) Animal pharmacology and neuronal recordings separately support receptor-dependent prefrontal regulation and firing-pattern responses to attended cues. [[16]](#pm-ref-16) [[18]](#pm-ref-18) These findings support distinct synthesis and signalling processes; they do not establish that changing dietary precursor or cofactor intake changes brain noradrenaline firing or attention.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Noradrenaline helps set arousal and vigilance so attention and executive control can stay engaged {{cite:odonnell_norepinephrine_2012}}. That biological role is not a dietary-treatment claim, and ADHD imaging that varies by dopamine process does not show a uniform noradrenaline deficit or a food-based attention effect {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}.

Noradrenaline can change arousal and effort-related tone, but dopaminergic reward circuitry remains the primary biological driver of Motivation / Drive {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}. The attached sources do not measure motivation after a dietary change, and iron-deficiency reviews are not motivation trials {{cite:beard_iron_2003}}.

Catecholamine systems can sit near reward and incentive-motivation biology, but the attached insulin–dopamine review does not measure noradrenaline signalling or a pleasure outcome after diet {{cite:gruber_impact_2023}}. Dopamine-process heterogeneity in ADHD is not a pleasure-capacity finding for this mechanism {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Noradrenaline supports arousal, vigilance and executive control
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Noradrenaline (norepinephrine) is a neuromodulator that changes how many brain-cell types respond, helping set arousal and vigilance so attention and executive control can stay engaged. That is a signalling role, not a dietary dosing rule.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports the mechanism’s attention and arousal mission. It does not show that changing food intake raises brain noradrenaline or treats ADHD.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Noradrenaline modulates arousal, vigilance and executive-control processes by changing the gain of multiple central-nervous-system cell types rather than acting as a single directional attention chemical.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The attached review treats norepinephrine as a widespread neuromodulator that optimises central-nervous-system performance by acting on several cell types. That account matches the mission of supporting alertness and executive control. It does not measure dietary intake, brain noradrenaline after meals, or a clinical attention outcome.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The source is a mechanistic review, not a human dietary or ADHD trial. It does not isolate receptor subtypes, quantify everyday noradrenaline tone, or show that precursor or cofactor intake changes signalling.

evidence_considered.label: O'Donnell et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Norepinephrine acts as a neuromodulator across multiple central-nervous-system cell types to support optimised performance, including arousal and vigilance-related functions.

assessment.study: Narrative review of norepinephrine as a multi-cell-type neuromodulator.
assessment.population: Mixed experimental and human mechanistic literature; not a dietary intervention sample.
assessment.result: Identified norepinephrine as a gain-setting neuromodulator rather than a single-target attention chemical.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled functional or dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the signalling role this mechanism represents.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; does not demonstrate dietary modification or a clinical attention benefit.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Noradrenaline formation shares catecholamine synthesis requirements
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Noradrenaline is formed from dopamine on the tyrosine-derived catecholamine path. Iron supports tyrosine hydroxylase, and pyridoxal-5′-phosphate (PLP; the active form of vitamin B6) supports decarboxylation toward dopamine. These shared steps are biological requirements, not proof that extra iron or B6 raises brain noradrenaline.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Tyrosine remains the pathway starting material. Circulating amino-acid supply, competitive brain entry and dopamine formation are earlier steps. The later conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline is assessed in the dopamine β-hydroxylase finding.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Noradrenaline formation depends on the shared tyrosine-to-dopamine catecholamine sequence, including iron- and PLP-dependent enzyme steps; cofactor or substrate necessity is not evidence of intake-responsive human brain noradrenaline.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Iron-deficiency review evidence identifies iron as required for tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting step from tyrosine toward dopamine and then noradrenaline. B-vitamin review evidence places PLP in neurochemical decarboxylation, and a transport study shows that B6 vitamers can enter the central nervous system. Together they support shared pathway dependence. They do not show ordinary-diet control of human brain noradrenaline. The later dopamine β-hydroxylase step is assessed separately.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The most direct deficiency discussion is preclinical or developmental. The sources do not establish common inadequacy in a defined clinical population, responsiveness when status is already adequate, or an attention benefit mediated by noradrenaline.

evidence_considered.label: Beard et al. (2003)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary iron deficiency
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Iron deficiency alters developing-brain catecholamine biology, including tyrosine-hydroxylase-dependent synthesis toward dopamine and noradrenaline.

assessment.study: Narrative review of iron deficiency, brain development and neurotransmitter systems.
assessment.population: Mixed human developmental and experimental-animal literature.
assessment.result: Identified iron as required for tyrosine hydroxylase and described catecholamine-system sensitivity under deficiency.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No human intake-to-noradrenaline effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports iron as a shared catecholamine-synthesis cofactor relevant to noradrenaline formation.
assessment.limitations: Predominantly deficiency and developmental evidence; not a human noradrenaline-dosing or attention trial.

evidence_dependency: The later dopamine-to-noradrenaline conversion is assessed in PM4-F4 rather than restated here.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Kennedy (2016)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews B-vitamin roles in neurochemical synthesis, including vitamin B6 as cofactor context for catecholamine formation.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: General B-vitamin review; it does not isolate aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase or show an intake-to-noradrenaline response.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Spector (1978)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Shows that B6 vitamers enter the central nervous system and contribute to the brain vitamin B6 pool.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Rabbit transport study; it does not measure noradrenaline synthesis, release or function.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Dopamine β-hydroxylase converts dopamine to noradrenaline using copper and ascorbate
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Dopamine β-hydroxylase hydroxylates dopamine to noradrenaline inside vesicles. The enzyme needs copper at its active sites and ascorbate as the electron donor that keeps that copper reduced. These are reaction requirements, not proof that extra dietary copper or vitamin C raises brain noradrenaline.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This finding identifies copper and vitamin C (ascorbate) as candidates for dietary assessment. It does not admit an intake-responsive noradrenaline lever or an attention benefit.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline by dopamine β-hydroxylase requires enzyme-bound copper and ascorbate as the electron donor; those biochemical requirements are not evidence of intake-responsive human brain noradrenaline or a functional benefit.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A 2026 catecholamine review identifies dopamine β-hydroxylase as a copper-dependent monooxygenase that uses molecular oxygen and ascorbate to form noradrenaline, and states that this is the only catecholamine-synthesis step with a direct mechanistic ascorbate requirement. The human crystal structure shows two copper ions per subunit and two ascorbate-derived electrons per turnover. Brain-copper and brain-ascorbate reviews place the same cuproenzyme and reductant in central-nervous-system catecholamine chemistry, while noting that circulating copper is not brain copper. Together they establish the defining conversion and its participants. Genetic copper-trafficking disease, animal copper deficiency and high-dose intravenous vitamin C in septic shock are not ordinary-diet evidence.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The synthesis is mechanistic and review-level. It does not show that ordinary dietary copper or vitamin C changes human brain noradrenaline, attention or ADHD when status is already adequate.

evidence_considered.label: Goldstein and Eisenhofer (2026)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Dopamine β-hydroxylase converts dopamine to noradrenaline and requires copper, molecular oxygen and ascorbate as the electron donor that keeps active-site copper reduced.

assessment.study: Integrative review of catecholamine synthesis, storage, release, reuptake and metabolism.
assessment.population: Mixed human physiological, clinical-pathophysiological and experimental literature; not a dietary trial sample.
assessment.result: Identified copper and ascorbate as required participants in the dopamine-to-noradrenaline step and noted that this is the only catecholamine step with a direct ascorbate requirement.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary or functional effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the defining conversion and its cofactor chemistry.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; disease and kinetic examples are not ordinary-diet interventions.

evidence_considered.label: Vendelboe et al. (2016)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human dopamine β-hydroxylase requires two copper ions per subunit and two ascorbate-derived electrons for hydroxylation of dopamine.

assessment.study: Crystal structure of human dopamine β-hydroxylase at 2.9 Å.
assessment.population: Structural biochemistry; not a human dietary sample.
assessment.result: Confirmed two type-2 copper sites per subunit and ascorbate dependence of the monooxygenase class.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Structural, not a dose-response estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Independently supports copper and ascorbate as reaction participants.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Attention relevance is not a dietary or ADHD-treatment finding
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The attached sources support noradrenaline as attention-relevant biology. They do not show that meals, iron or B6 change human noradrenaline signalling, and they do not show a uniform ADHD lesion that diet can correct.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Keep biological relevance separate from dietary modulation and from dopamine-process findings that are not noradrenaline measurements.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Repository evidence supports a translational relationship from noradrenergic signalling to Focus / Attention Stability without establishing dietary modification of noradrenaline or an ADHD treatment effect.
scientific_findings.synthesis: O’Donnell supplies the neuromodulatory attention and arousal account. MacDonald shows that ADHD-related catecholamine findings vary by process and method and cannot be restated as a single deficit. Fernstrom describes meal-level precursor transport upstream of signalling. Together they support a biology-to-attention mapping while blocking a food-as-noradrenaline-treatment reading.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: No attached study measures attention after a dietary change aimed at noradrenaline. Plasma amino-acid ratios and dopamine-process reviews are not noradrenaline signalling.

title: Serotonergic Signalling Regulation
mission: Support serotonergic signalling so mood stability, inhibition, and behavioural regulation remain well grounded.
summary: Serotonin is made in neurons when tryptophan is converted through two enzyme steps, then shaped by release, receptors, reuptake and breakdown. Across brain regions, the same transmitter can support different responses. That system supports mood stability, inhibition and behavioural regulation. Tryptophan, iron and vitamin B6 are part of the chemistry.
dose_sensitivity: No intake-response range established; serotonin effects are receptor-, region- and task-dependent

phenome_relationships.rationale: Serotonin signalling is a core biological substrate for emotional regulation, impulse control and affective stability {{cite:shaw_emotion_2014}}. ADHD-focused serotonin reviews do not establish a uniform serotonin deficit that diet can correct {{cite:faraone_serotonin_2025}} {{cite:banerjee_does_2015}}.

Serotonin signalling participates in emotional processing and stress-related control {{cite:shaw_emotion_2014}}. The attached sources do not measure stress resilience after a dietary change aimed at serotonin {{cite:tang_nutritional_2025}}.
Serotonin participates in sleep–wake and calming neurochemistry {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. Meal-level precursor transport is not a sleep outcome {{cite:fernstrom_lnna_2013}}.

Serotonin can interact with dopaminergic reward circuits and behavioural inhibition {{cite:faraone_serotonin_2025}}. That interaction is not a measured reward outcome after diet {{cite:tang_nutritional_2025}}.

Serotonin signalling intersects negative-valence and control circuits discussed in mood and anxiety contexts {{cite:briguglio_dietary_2018}}. Systemic-inflammation connectivity is not a serotonin measurement {{cite:marsland_systemic_2017}}.

Serotonin pathways sit near positive-valence mood biology {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. Saffron supplementation trials are not serotonin-process measurements and are not a Dietary Requirement of this mechanism {{cite:jackson_effects_2021}}.

Serotonin can modulate affiliative and social-affective behaviour in translational accounts {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. A saffron social-relationship outcome is not a serotonin signalling measurement {{cite:jackson_effects_2021}}.

scientific_findings_intro: Enzyme studies and biochemical reviews establish the neuronal tryptophan-to-serotonin synthesis sequence and its cofactor dependence. [[13]](#pm-ref-13) [[14]](#pm-ref-14) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) Broader reviews support receptor diversity and transporter-mediated handling as additional determinants of serotonergic function. [[15]](#pm-ref-15) Together, the evidence supports synthesis and signalling as related but distinct capacities; it does not directly establish that ordinary dietary changes regulate human brain serotonin or produce uniform functional benefits.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Serotonin supports mood stability, inhibition and behavioural regulation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine) is a neuromodulator that helps set emotional tone, behavioural inhibition and related control. That is a signalling role, not a dietary dosing rule.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports the mechanism’s mood-stability and inhibition mission. It does not show that changing food intake raises brain serotonin or treats mood, sleep or ADHD.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Serotonin modulates emotional processing, impulse control and behavioural regulation rather than acting as a single directional mood chemical.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Human emotion-dysregulation and ADHD-related serotonin reviews treat serotonergic signalling as relevant to affective stability and inhibition. A broader serotonin-biology review places the same transmitter across receptor families that shape mood- and behaviour-related circuits. Together they support the signalling mission. They do not measure dietary intake, brain serotonin after meals, or a uniform clinical lesion that food can correct.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The sources are reviews, not dietary trials. They do not isolate everyday serotonin tone, quantify receptor-specific effects after meals, or show that precursor or cofactor intake changes signalling.

evidence_considered.label: Shaw et al. (2014)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Emotion dysregulation in ADHD is discussed as a clinically important phenotype with serotonergic and broader monoamine context, without testing diet.

assessment.study: Narrative review of emotion dysregulation in ADHD.
assessment.population: Children and adults with ADHD and comparison groups described in the reviewed literature.
assessment.result: Identified emotion dysregulation as a core associated feature rather than a single-chemical deficit.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled dietary or serotonin-process effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Anchors the mood-stability and inhibition mission in human clinical-mechanistic literature.
assessment.limitations: ADHD-focused review; not a serotonin dietary trial.

evidence_considered.label: Berger, Gray and Roth (2009)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Serotonin acts through multiple receptor families and central circuits that include mood, sleep–wake and behavioural-control functions.

assessment.study: Narrative review of expanded serotonin biology.
assessment.population: Mixed experimental and human mechanistic literature; not a dietary sample.
assessment.result: Described receptor diversity and non-dietary physiological roles of serotonin.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary or clinical effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes serotonin as a multi-receptor neuromodulator rather than a single mood chemical.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; does not demonstrate dietary modification.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Serotonin formation depends on tryptophan hydroxylation and PLP-dependent decarboxylation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Brain serotonin is formed from tryptophan. Tryptophan hydroxylase (the first and rate-limiting enzyme) needs iron and tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). Pyridoxal-5′-phosphate (PLP; the active form of vitamin B6) then supports decarboxylation of 5-hydroxytryptophan to serotonin. These are biological requirements, not proof that extra tryptophan, iron or B6 raises brain serotonin.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Tryptophan remains the pathway starting material. Circulating amino-acid supply and competitive brain entry are earlier steps. Iron, BH4 and PLP are candidates for dietary assessment. This finding does not admit an intake-responsive serotonin lever.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Serotonin formation depends on tryptophan-hydroxylase conversion of tryptophan to 5-hydroxytryptophan, requiring iron and BH4, followed by PLP-dependent decarboxylation; cofactor or substrate necessity is not evidence of intake-responsive human brain serotonin.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Aromatic-amino-acid hydroxylase biochemistry identifies tryptophan hydroxylase as an iron- and tetrahydrobiopterin-dependent monooxygenase that forms 5-hydroxytryptophan. A second tryptophan hydroxylase isoform (TPH2) accounts for neuronal serotonin synthesis. BH4-pathway review evidence places the same cofactor on serotonin as well as dopamine synthesis. B-vitamin review evidence places PLP in neurochemical decarboxylation, and a transport study shows that B6 vitamers can enter the central nervous system. Together they establish the defining synthesis sequence and its participants. They do not show ordinary-diet control of human brain serotonin.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The synthesis is mechanistic and review-level. It does not show that ordinary dietary tryptophan, iron or vitamin B6 changes human brain serotonin, mood, sleep or ADHD when status is already adequate.

evidence_considered.directional_finding: Tryptophan hydroxylase is a tetrahydropterin-dependent aromatic amino-acid hydroxylase that uses non-haem iron and molecular oxygen to form 5-hydroxytryptophan.

assessment.study: Biochemical review of tetrahydropterin-dependent amino-acid hydroxylases.
assessment.population: Enzyme and experimental literature; not a human dietary sample.
assessment.result: Identified iron, tetrahydrobiopterin and oxygen as required participants in tryptophan hydroxylation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary or functional effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the rate-limiting hydroxylation chemistry.
assessment.limitations: Enzyme-mechanism review; not an intake-to-serotonin trial.

evidence_considered.directional_finding: A second tryptophan hydroxylase isoform (TPH2) synthesises serotonin in the brain, distinct from the peripheral TPH1 enzyme.

assessment.study: Identification of neuronal tryptophan hydroxylase 2.
assessment.population: Experimental biochemistry and mouse genetics; not a dietary trial.
assessment.result: Showed that brain serotonin synthesis uses TPH2 rather than treating TPH as a single peripheral enzyme.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Not a dose-response estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Places the hydroxylase step in neuronal serotonin formation.

connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Nutrition review; it does not establish intake-responsive human brain serotonin on this mechanism.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Serotonin signalling uses receptor families, reuptake and enzymatic metabolism
scientific_findings.finding_summary: After synthesis, serotonin is released, acts on several receptor families, is taken back up by the serotonin transporter (SERT) and can be metabolised enzymatically. That sequence is signalling biology, not a dietary rule.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This finding covers the release-and-receptor part of the Overview. It identifies later-stage dietary candidates as still unassessed. It does not admit a SERT or MAO dietary lever.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Serotonergic signalling includes vesicular handling, receptor-mediated actions, transporter-mediated reuptake and enzymatic metabolism; those stages are not interchangeable with precursor supply and are not evidence of dietary control.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The expanded-biology review describes serotonin’s receptor diversity, transporter-mediated clearance and metabolic handling as the operational signalling sequence. ADHD-focused serotonin reviews use receptor and transporter language as pharmacological and neurobiological context, not as food targets. Together they establish that signalling is more than synthesis. They do not measure diet-responsive receptor or transporter change.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Review-level coverage. Specific dietary dependencies of monoamine oxidase or of SERT function remain unassessed.

evidence_considered.label: Berger, Gray and Roth (2009)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Serotonin signalling involves multiple receptor families, transporter-mediated reuptake and further metabolic fates, including a pineal route toward melatonin.

assessment.study: Same serotonin-biology review used for PM5-F1, reused here for the signalling-sequence proposition.
assessment.population: Mixed mechanistic literature; not a dietary sample.
assessment.result: Described post-synthesis signalling stages without testing food intake.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes release, receptor, reuptake and metabolism as part of the mechanism.
assessment.limitations: Review; no dietary or ADHD endpoint.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Faraone et al. (2025)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Systematic review of serotonin in ADHD neurobiology, including receptor and transporter context.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: ADHD literature review; not a dietary signalling measurement.

evidence_dependency: Berger, Gray and Roth (2009) is also primary evidence in PM5-F1. Reuse here answers the signalling-sequence proposition, not an independent replication of the mood-role review.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Emotional-regulation relevance is not a dietary or ADHD-treatment finding
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The attached sources support serotonin as emotion-regulation-relevant biology. They do not show that meals, tryptophan, iron or B6 change human serotonin signalling, and they do not show a uniform ADHD lesion that diet can correct.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Keep biological relevance separate from dietary modulation and from inflammation or saffron findings that are not serotonin-process measurements.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Repository and bounded-review evidence supports a translational relationship from serotonergic signalling to Emotional Regulation without establishing dietary modification of serotonin or an ADHD treatment effect.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Shaw supplies the emotion-regulation account. Faraone and Banerjee show that ADHD-related serotonin discussion is heterogeneous and cannot be restated as a single deficit. Fernstrom describes meal-level precursor transport upstream of signalling. Together they support a biology-to-emotion mapping while blocking a food-as-serotonin-treatment reading.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: No attached study measures emotional regulation after a dietary change aimed at serotonin. Plasma amino-acid ratios, inflammation connectivity and saffron trials are not serotonin signalling.

evidence_considered.label: Shaw et al. (2014)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Emotion dysregulation is a clinically important ADHD-related phenotype discussed with monoamine context, without testing diet.

assessment.study: Same emotion-dysregulation review used for PM5-F1, reused here for the Phenome-relationship proposition.
assessment.population: ADHD and comparison literature; not a dietary sample.

assessment.evidence_summary: Anchors the Phenome mapping in signalling biology.
assessment.limitations: Review; no dietary endpoint.

evidence_considered.label: Faraone et al. (2025)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: ADHD-related serotonin findings are mixed across methods and constructs and do not support a uniform global deficit that can be treated as a serotonin-diet claim.

assessment.study: Systematic literature review of serotonin in ADHD neurobiology.
assessment.population: ADHD clinical and mechanistic literature.
assessment.result: Reported heterogeneous serotonin-related findings rather than one directional lesion.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled dietary serotonin effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Constrains ADHD wording attached to this Phenome relationship.
assessment.limitations: ADHD-focused; not a serotonin dietary trial.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Fernstrom (2013)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Describes meal-level large-neutral-amino-acid transport that can change tryptophan presentation before serotonin synthesis.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Transport and plasma-ratio biology; it does not measure serotonin signalling or emotion regulation.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Jackson et al. (2021)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Saffron supplementation trial in low mood; sometimes attached to mood phenomes.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Wrong construct for this mechanism: not a serotonin-process measurement and not a Dietary Requirement.

connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Links systemic inflammation to default-mode connectivity discussed near perseverative thought.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Inflammation and connectivity; it does not measure serotonin signalling.

evidence_dependency: Shaw et al. (2014) is also primary evidence in PM5-F1. Reuse here answers the Phenome-relationship proposition, not an independent replication of the signalling review.
Fernstrom (2013) is connected evidence here and primary evidence in PM5-IC1. That is one transport review used for two propositions, not two independent studies.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Precursor transport is not serotonergic signalling
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Plasma amino-acid ratios and meal-level LAT1 competition can sit next to this mechanism. They do not measure serotonin release, receptor signalling or a mood outcome of changing diet.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Use these sources to keep measurements distinct. Do not promote them as headline serotonin Findings.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: LAT1-related precursor presentation is not interchangeable with serotonergic signalling.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Fernstrom addresses competitive precursor transport, including tryptophan. That is useful as a boundary on how other evidence is read. It does not establish serotonin signalling change or a dietary mood effect.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Interpretive only. This source does not fill the missing human dietary-to-serotonin measurement.
evidence_dependency: Fernstrom (2013) is also connected evidence in PM5-F3. Reuse here constrains measurement identity, not a second transport experiment.

evidence_considered.label: Fernstrom (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Meal composition can change plasma tryptophan-to-LNAA ratios and therefore competitive presentation of tryptophan at LAT1.

assessment.study: Review of large-neutral-amino-acid transport and brain neurochemistry.
assessment.population: Human meal-study and mechanistic literature.
assessment.result: Showed transport-level precursor presentation, not serotonin signalling.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Plasma-ratio changes; not a serotonin-release estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Constrains transport evidence as upstream presentation.
assessment.limitations: Does not measure serotonin receptors, mood or ADHD.

scientific_findings.finding_summary: Riboflavin-deficient rats had lower brain mitochondrial MAO activity measured with tyramine.

decision.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared indispensable-amino-acid quality pool can constrain this mechanism’s governed serotonergic capacity.
established_links: Tryptophan is indispensable and is the serotonin starting material (PM5-F2).
DIAAS and related scores measure digestible IAA adequacy for protein quality (FAO 2013; Mariotti 2019).
inferred_links: Incomplete meal protein quality would therefore lower tryptophan supply and constrain serotonin signalling.
decision.rationale: Assessment was completed. Quality-scoring evidence does not connect IAA-quality inadequacy to serotonergic capacity. Fernstrom’s protein effects operate through the plasma tryptophan-to-LNAA ratio, which is the competitive arm. Extreme tryptophan-poor diets are a different construct. The capacity-constraint link remains a material gap, not a negative finding.

kc_adjudication_history.rationale: Superseded scope: this proposition concerns the former broad indispensable-amino-acid quality arm. Current BRS1 KC1 is the monoamine-precursor LNAA competitive pool. Archiving does not reject general protein-quality biology or alter the separately assessed competitive/supply decisions.

kc_adjudication_history.rationale: Metadata migration only: preserve the established governs/constrained-by interpretation as a typed Conditional constraint for FM summary derivation. No stronger scientific admission.

dietary_supply.statement: Food riboflavin supplies the precursor activated by human RFK and FLAD1 to FMN/FAD. Cofactor loading is not increased neurotransmitter output.

conversion_pathway.process: Riboflavin kinase (RFK) phosphorylates riboflavin to FMN using ATP.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Enzyme identity does not quantify tissue cofactor supply or flux after a meal.
