conversion_pathway.limitations: FAD production and enzyme loading depend on cellular context; no fixed food-to-FAD yield is inferred.

evidence.statement: Human FLAD1 catalyses FMN adenylation; UniProt Q8NFF5 entry 182 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 17237.

title: Acetylcholine Synthesis Support
mission: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.
summary: Acetylcholine is made in nerve endings when choline is joined to acetyl-CoA, a cell-made acetate carrier. Diet can provide choline itself or choline from phosphatidylcholine, and vitamin B5 supports the acetyl-CoA side. Entry into the nerve ending still controls access to the reaction. The reaction supplies acetylcholine for later cholinergic signalling.
dose_sensitivity: No intake-response range established for human brain acetylcholine

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Direct substrate combined with acetyl-CoA by choline acetyltransferase to form acetylcholine
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Choline is required and diet supplies it, but additional intake has not been shown here to raise acetylcholine synthesis in the human brain or improve attention.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Dietary choline-containing phospholipid that is digested and remodelled, producing circulating choline as one route to the direct choline substrate
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Human tracer evidence establishes phosphatidylcholine as a choline-provision route; it does not show delivery to cholinergic terminals or increased brain acetylcholine synthesis.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted intracellular/endogenous participant; no dietary supply relationship is admitted for this entry in this PM.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Acetyl-group donor combined with choline by choline acetyltransferase to form acetylcholine
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Acetyl-CoA is a cellular reaction substrate, not a dietary acetyl-CoA recommendation; ordinary dietary control of its availability in human cholinergic neurons is not established.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Existing biological role explicitly admits the nutritional precursor route to coenzyme A; intracellular reaction participation does not negate that dietary route.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Nutritional precursor of coenzyme A, from which cells form the acetyl-CoA required for acetylcholine synthesis
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Chronic ethanol-associated pantothenate depletion and rescue affected acetylcholine synthesis in rats; this does not establish that extra B5 raises brain acetylcholine in adequately nourished humans.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Folate-dependent methyl metabolism helps maintain the brain choline resource available for acetylcholine formation; folate deprivation lowered choline and acetylcholine in studied mouse models, with SAM rescue supporting this upstream resource relationship.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Animal evidence is conditional on age, brain region and experimental context. Choline and acetylcholine concentrations were measured; methyl-dependent choline retention and the consequence for synthesis capacity are mechanistic inferences, not measured human synthesis flux. Folate is not a ChAT cofactor; extra folate above adequacy and cognitive benefit are not established.

dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Sodium supports the electrochemical coupling required for high-affinity CHT1 choline uptake, sustaining substrate-entry capacity for acetylcholine synthesis.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Transport-ion capacity does not establish that added dietary salt increases brain choline uptake or acetylcholine output. CNS homeostasis and membrane gradients intervene. Chloride is not assumed to have identical transport stoichiometry and is not independently admitted here.

dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Choline is the starting material transported into cholinergic nerve endings and joined to acetyl-CoA to make acetylcholine.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Phosphatidylcholine
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Phosphatidylcholine is digested and remodelled as a choline-containing food form. It provides choline rather than acting as a second substrate in the synthesis reaction.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Vitamin B5 (pantothenate)
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Pantothenate is used to make coenzyme A, which cells use to form acetyl-CoA—the second substrate in acetylcholine synthesis.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Acetyl-CoA
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Acetyl-CoA is generated through compartmented neuronal metabolism and donates the acetyl group used by choline acetyltransferase.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Acetylcholine is the cholinergic transmitter used in attention and learning circuits {{cite:johansson_decreased_2013}} {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. Receptor-binding differences in boys with ADHD and choline/neurodevelopment reviews supply translational context. They do not show that changing choline intake treats ADHD or raises brain acetylcholine.

Cholinergic signalling is a biological context for working-memory and cognitive precision {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}} {{cite:briguglio_dietary_2018}}. The attached sources do not measure cognitive-clarity scores after a choline change aimed at acetylcholine synthesis.

pm_kc_relationships.dietary_input_note: Pool/constraint reference; constituent dietary supply is recorded separately.
pm_kc_relationships.pm_biological_role: Inadequate one-carbon donor availability can increase pressure on choline-dependent methyl donation and disturb brain choline and acetylcholine availability, thereby constraining the substrate capacity used for acetylcholine synthesis.
pm_kc_relationships.evidence_limitation: The mapping is supported by dietary and genetic animal models plus the established choline substrate reaction. It does not show that folate, B12, or betaine supplementation increases acetylcholine synthesis in nutrient-replete humans, and it does not inherit the KC food list.

constituent_relationships.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
constituent_relationships.reader_description: Folate-dependent methyl metabolism helps maintain the choline available for acetylcholine formation in the studied deficiency models.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methyl-donor pool can constrain this mechanism’s governed acetylcholine-synthesis capacity.
established_links: Choline plus acetyl-CoA forms acetylcholine via choline acetyltransferase (PM6-F2).
Dietary folate deficiency reduced brain choline and acetylcholine in mouse models, and SAM restored both under folate compromise (PM6-F6).
Methionine-synthase-reductase deficiency lowered hippocampal choline, betaine, and acetylcholine (PM6-F6).
A separate folate-deficiency experiment found region- and age-dependent acetylcholine changes rather than a uniform whole-brain response (PM6-F6).
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: Type D is met through a supported mechanistic chain rather than a single end-to-end human capacity assay: one-carbon compromise changes the choline resource state, animal models show lower choline and acetylcholine under folate or methionine-cycle impairment, and choline is the required synthesis substrate. BRS1(KC1) was screened out because choline is not a LAT1 large-neutral-amino-acid cargo.

scientific_findings_intro: Transporter evidence identifies terminal choline uptake as a control step for acetylcholine synthesis, while human tracing demonstrates systemic assimilation of choline from dietary phosphatidylcholine. [[6]](#pm-ref-6) [[7]](#pm-ref-7) Animal depletion and rescue studies support bounded pantothenate and one-carbon dependencies, with acetylcholine responses varying by experimental condition, region and age. [[8]](#pm-ref-8) [[9]](#pm-ref-9) [[10]](#pm-ref-10) The evidence therefore supports provision and local synthesis capacity without equating plasma choline delivery with neuronal release, attention benefit or a human dose response.

scientific_findings.finding_label: High-affinity choline uptake controls substrate entry into cholinergic terminals
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The high-affinity choline transporter recovers choline into cholinergic nerve endings and is a major control point for acetylcholine production.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Substrate supply is not only a food-intake question: choline must reach the nerve terminal through a regulated transporter before choline acetyltransferase can use it.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Sodium-coupled high-affinity choline uptake through CHT/SLC5A7 is required to recover choline into cholinergic nerve terminals and commonly limits acetylcholine production under physiological demand.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A focused transporter review shows that CHT recovers synaptic choline into cholinergic terminals, that inhibiting or genetically impairing this transport reduces cholinergic capacity, and that activity-dependent trafficking changes uptake capacity. This establishes terminal uptake as a control step upstream of the ChAT reaction.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Transporter biology is largely mechanistic and preclinical. It does not show that ordinary choline intake changes CHT capacity in humans or that more dietary choline overcomes a transporter defect.

evidence_considered.label: Ojiakor and Rylett (2020)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: CHT-mediated high-affinity choline uptake recovers choline into cholinergic terminals and is the principal regulated supply step for sustaining acetylcholine production.

assessment.study: Review of CHT function, trafficking, genetic disruption, and pharmacological manipulation.
assessment.population: Cellular, animal, human genetic, and neuropathology evidence; not a dietary trial.
assessment.result: Reduced CHT function or availability limits choline uptake and cholinergic transmission, while neuronal activity recruits transport capacity.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the regulated choline-entry step required before acetylcholine synthesis.
assessment.limitations: Does not test ordinary food intake or human brain synthesis after a meal.

evidence_considered.label: Xue et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: Controlled transport substrates and ions; not a dietary salt experiment.
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human CHT1 structures and transport-site mutations identify sodium-dependent choline uptake; chloride binding has a distinct functional role.

assessment.study: Human CHT1 cryo-EM structures and uptake/site-mutant experiments.
assessment.population: Human transporter expressed in experimental systems.
assessment.result: Human CHT1 structures and transport-site mutations identify sodium-dependent choline uptake; chloride binding has a distinct functional role.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No additional magnitude inferred.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human CHT1 structures and transport-site mutations identify sodium-dependent choline uptake; chloride binding has a distinct functional role.
assessment.limitations: Transport-ion capacity does not establish that added dietary salt increases brain choline uptake or acetylcholine output. CNS homeostasis and membrane gradients intervene. Chloride is not assumed to have identical transport stoichiometry and is not independently admitted here.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary structural and transport results retrieved 26 October 2026.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Inazu (2019)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Separates CTL1/CTL2-mediated choline handling at brain microvascular endothelium from CHT/SLC5A7 uptake at cholinergic terminals.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Does not test whether an oral choline exposure increases delivery to terminals or acetylcholine synthesis in humans.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Choline and acetyl-CoA form acetylcholine via choline acetyltransferase
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Choline combines with acetyl-CoA through choline acetyltransferase to form acetylcholine. Necessity of those reactants is not proof that extra choline raises human brain acetylcholine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Choline and acetyl-CoA are the two substrates. Phosphatidylcholine and pantothenate matter through provision routes assessed separately; vitamin B12 and folate do not act as ChAT cofactors.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Acetylcholine is formed from choline and acetyl-CoA by choline acetyltransferase; biochemical necessity is not intake-responsive human brain acetylcholine.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A choline-acetyltransferase review and a modern choline-transporter review agree that ChAT transfers the acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to choline in cholinergic neurons. Together they establish the defining reaction and both substrates.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Reaction and review evidence does not establish which substrate limits synthesis in every physiological state, an ordinary dietary dose response, or a human functional benefit.

evidence_considered.label: Oda (1999)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Choline acetyltransferase condenses choline and acetyl-CoA to form acetylcholine and is the defining synthetic enzyme in cholinergic neurons.

assessment.study: Review of choline-acetyltransferase structure, distribution and pathology.
assessment.population: Experimental and neuropathology literature; not a dietary sample.
assessment.result: Identified choline and acetyl-CoA as the enzyme’s substrates.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary or clinical effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the acetylcholine-forming reaction.
assessment.limitations: Enzyme and pathology review; not an intake-to-acetylcholine trial.

evidence_considered.label: Ojiakor and Rylett (2020)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: ChAT transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to choline in the neuronal cytoplasm after CHT-mediated choline entry.

assessment.study: Review of CHT function and cholinergic terminal biology.
assessment.population: Mechanistic, animal, and human genetic literature.
assessment.result: Describes substrate entry followed by ChAT-dependent synthesis from choline and acetyl-CoA.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Independently confirms the reaction participants within the presynaptic synthesis pathway.
assessment.limitations: Does not measure human synthesis after dietary exposure.

evidence_dependency: Ojiakor and Rylett (2020) is also primary evidence in PM6-F1; reuse here establishes reaction placement after choline transport, not independent replication.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Kennedy (2016)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews B-vitamin roles in brain energy and one-carbon chemistry.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Does not establish vitamin B12 or folate as acetylcholine-synthesis cofactors.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Dietary phosphatidylcholine is a choline-provision route
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Phosphatidylcholine is a choline-containing dietary form that is digested, absorbed, and remodelled. It provides choline but is not a second substrate in the ChAT reaction.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Represent phosphatidylcholine as Derived provision to choline, not as an independent acetylcholine-synthesis requirement.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Dietary phosphatidylcholine is digested and remodelled into circulating phosphatidylcholine and free choline, establishing a dietary provision route to the direct choline substrate.
scientific_findings.synthesis: In a randomized crossover tracer study in six healthy men, labelled phosphatidylcholine produced a delayed rise in labelled plasma choline and a larger phosphatidylcholine exposure than water-soluble choline forms. The tracer results directly establish digestion and systemic assimilation as a choline-containing dietary route.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Small single-dose study in healthy men. Plasma appearance does not measure delivery to cholinergic terminals, acetylcholine synthesis, neurotransmitter release, attention, or clinical benefit.

evidence_considered.label: Böckmann et al. (2023)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: isolated-substance
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Oral labelled phosphatidylcholine produced delayed circulating labelled choline and the highest labelled phosphatidylcholine exposure among four tested choline forms.

assessment.study: Randomized crossover stable-isotope comparison of four oral choline forms.
assessment.population: Six healthy adult men.
assessment.result: Phosphatidylcholine was digested and remodelled, with delayed plasma choline appearance and higher plasma phosphatidylcholine exposure.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Delayed choline peak and approximately 2.3-fold higher peak labelled phosphatidylcholine than water-soluble forms.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes phosphatidylcholine as an assimilated choline-provision route.
assessment.limitations: Small sample; supplement bolus rather than whole food; no brain or acetylcholine measurement.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Pantothenate supports the acetyl-CoA side of acetylcholine synthesis
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Pantothenate (vitamin B5) is needed to make coenzyme A, which cells use to form acetyl-CoA. Acetyl-CoA supplies the acetyl group in acetylcholine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Vitamin B5 is a biochemical precursor route to acetyl-CoA, not a ChAT cofactor or a second Direct Dietary Requirement. The evidence supports dependency and an animal depletion effect, not routine high-dose supplementation.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Pantothenate supports acetylcholine-synthesis capacity through coenzyme A and acetyl-CoA formation, and severe chronic pantothenate depletion can reduce brain acetylcholine synthesis in rats.
scientific_findings.synthesis: In rats exposed chronically to ethanol, brain pantothenate fell to 7% of control and labelled acetylcholine synthesis from pyruvate was inhibited; pantothenate co-administration raised brain pantothenate and acetylcholine synthesis. Together with the established acetyl-CoA reaction requirement, this closes the pantothenate → coenzyme A/acetyl-CoA → synthesis chain.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The intervention used chronic high-dose ethanol and pharmacological pantothenate doses in rats. It does not establish that ordinary B5 intake limits acetylcholine synthesis or that supplementation benefits adequately nourished humans.

evidence_considered.label: Rivera-Calimlim et al. (1988)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: isolated-substance
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Chronic ethanol depleted rat-brain pantothenate and inhibited acetylcholine synthesis, while pantothenate co-administration increased both brain pantothenate and synthesis.

assessment.study: Chronic and acute ethanol exposure with or without oral pantothenate in rats, measuring labelled acetylcholine synthesis.
assessment.population: Rats; no human participants.
assessment.result: The chronic four-month condition reduced brain pantothenate and acetylcholine synthesis; pantothenate co-treatment partly restored both.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Brain pantothenate fell to 7% of control with chronic ethanol; synthesis differences were statistically significant but no transferable human effect size is available.
assessment.evidence_summary: Directly links severe pantothenate depletion to reduced acetylcholine synthesis through acetyl-CoA provision.
assessment.limitations: Ethanol-specific animal model, very high pantothenate doses, and no ordinary-diet or human outcome.

scientific_findings.finding_label: One-carbon insufficiency can constrain the choline resource used for acetylcholine
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Folate- and B12-dependent one-carbon metabolism shares choline-related methyl resources. Dietary or genetic impairment can lower brain choline and acetylcholine in animal models.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports a constrained-by mapping to the Methyl Donor Pool. It does not make folate, B12, or betaine ChAT cofactors or separate Direct Dietary Requirements.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Inadequate folate-dependent or B12-dependent methionine-cycle capacity can disturb brain choline metabolism and lower acetylcholine availability, creating a supported shared-resource constraint on acetylcholine-synthesis capacity.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Dietary folate compromise lowered brain choline and acetylcholine in mice, with SAM restoring both under the deficient condition. Genetic methionine-synthase-reductase impairment likewise lowered hippocampal choline, betaine, and acetylcholine. A separate rat study found mixed, region- and age-dependent acetylcholine changes, showing that the effect is not uniform. Together these sources establish a shared-resource constraint while preserving biological variability.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Animal dietary and genetic models measure metabolite pools more often than synthesis flux. They do not show that folate, B12, betaine, or SAM supplementation raises acetylcholine synthesis in nutrient-replete humans.

evidence_considered.label: Chan et al. (2008)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Dietary folate compromise lowered mouse-brain choline and acetylcholine, while SAM supplementation under folate deficiency restored both pools.

assessment.study: Dietary folate deficiency across adult, aged, and genetically susceptible mouse models with SAM rescue.
assessment.population: Mice of several genotypes and ages.
assessment.result: Folate compromise reduced choline and acetylcholine; SAM restored these measures and cognitive performance in the deficient condition.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Directionally consistent rescue across several mouse contexts; no human effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports the link from one-carbon donor insufficiency to loss of the choline resource used for acetylcholine.
assessment.limitations: Mixed dietary, oxidative, age, and genotype contexts; pool concentrations rather than direct synthesis flux.

evidence_considered.label: Jadavji et al. (2014)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Methionine-synthase-reductase-deficient mice had lower hippocampal choline, betaine, and acetylcholine with compensatory ChAT and AChE expression changes.

assessment.study: Genetic mouse model of impaired methionine synthase reductase.
assessment.population: Three-month-old wild-type and Mtrr-deficient mice.
assessment.result: Deficiency reduced hippocampal choline, betaine, and acetylcholine and impaired short-term memory.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Significant group differences reported; no dietary or human effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Adds B12-dependent methionine-cycle evidence to the shared-resource constraint.
assessment.limitations: Genetic mouse model; altered concentration and enzyme expression do not quantify synthesis flux.

evidence_considered.label: Crivello et al. (2010)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Ten weeks of folate deficiency changed brain acetylcholine in adult rats by region—lower in hippocampus but higher in cortex and striatum—with little brain effect in young rats.

assessment.study: Controlled folate-deficient versus control diets in young and adult male rats.
assessment.population: Male Sprague Dawley rats starting at four weeks or nine months.
assessment.result: Brain choline and acetylcholine responses depended on age and region rather than moving uniformly.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Significant regional differences; no whole-brain or human synthesis estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Qualifies the constraint as context-dependent and prevents a universal lower-acetylcholine claim.
assessment.limitations: Concentrations rather than synthesis flux; animal model; mixed regional direction.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Acetyl-CoA supply is metabolically generated and compartmented
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Choline acetyltransferase works in the neuronal cytosol, while much acetyl-CoA is generated in mitochondria. Acetyl-unit transfer and local regeneration therefore form a separate substrate-supply control.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Acetyl-CoA availability can constrain synthesis, but this does not make glucose, pyruvate, citrate, or dietary acetyl-CoA separate Dietary Requirements for this PM.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Cytosolic acetyl-CoA for acetylcholine synthesis is supplied through compartmented neuronal metabolism, and its availability can regulate synthesis independently of choline transport.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A focused review of brain acetylcholine synthesis distinguishes mitochondrial acetyl-CoA production from the cytosolic ChAT reaction and reviews citrate cleavage, pyruvate-dependent production, and possible direct mitochondrial export routes. The evidence supports acetyl-CoA availability as a control point while leaving the proportional contribution of each route context-dependent.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The source literature is mechanistic and largely preclinical, and competing acetyl-unit transfer routes were not fully resolved. It does not establish glucose, pyruvate, citrate, or acetyl-CoA as useful dietary targets for this PM.

evidence_considered.label: Jope (1979)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Acetyl-CoA availability may limit acetylcholine synthesis, with evidence for citrate-lyase, pyruvate-dehydrogenase, and mitochondrial export routes supplying the cytosolic reaction.

assessment.study: Review of high-affinity choline transport, acetyl-CoA production, compartmentation, and regulation of brain acetylcholine synthesis.
assessment.population: Biochemical, synaptosomal, and animal literature; no dietary human trial.
assessment.result: Distinguished mitochondrial acetyl-CoA generation from cytosolic use by ChAT and identified several supported supply routes.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled dietary or clinical effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes compartmented acetyl-CoA provision as a second upstream substrate-control problem.
assessment.limitations: Older mechanistic literature; the relative contribution of proposed routes remains context-dependent.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Szutowicz et al. (2010)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Pyrithiamine-induced thiamine deficiency reduced pyruvate-dehydrogenase flux and mitochondrial and cytosolic acetyl-CoA in rat nerve terminals, supporting the compartmented acetyl-unit supply model.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: The reported cholinergic endpoint was altered quantal acetylcholine release, while ChAT activity was unchanged; it does not establish vitamin B1 as a PM6 synthesis requirement or intake-responsive lever.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Cholinergic biology is translationally relevant to attention
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Acetylcholine-receptor and choline-status findings sit near attention biology in ADHD-related samples. That is translational context, not an ADHD treatment rule.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Use these studies as attention-relevant cholinergic context. They do not show that choline supplementation treats ADHD.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human ADHD-related muscarinic-binding and choline-status evidence is translationally relevant to attention; it is not a demonstration that changing choline intake treats ADHD.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Lower muscarinic binding in boys with ADHD and choline-status discussion in a neurodevelopmental review together support a cholinergic context for attention. They do not isolate acetylcholine synthesis as a treatment target and they do not measure attention after a choline intervention designed to change synthesis.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Cross-sectional receptor binding and a narrative review. No choline intervention arm for ADHD or attention scores is attached.

evidence_considered.label: Johansson et al. (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Decreased muscarinic binding in boys with ADHD supplies attention-relevant cholinergic context, not a treatment effect.

assessment.study: Same fibroblast binding comparison used in PM6-F1, reused here for the attention relationship.
assessment.population: Boys with ADHD and comparison boys.
assessment.result: Lower muscarinic binding in the ADHD group.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Binding contrast only; no attention-score change after diet.
assessment.evidence_summary: Anchors the attention relationship in human cholinergic biology.
assessment.limitations: Not brain imaging of acetylcholine and not a dietary trial.

evidence_considered.label: Derbyshire and Maes (2023)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Altered choline status is discussed in ADHD-related literature without proving choline treatment of ADHD.

assessment.study: Same narrative review used in PM6-F1 and PM6-F2, reused here for phenome context.
assessment.population: ADHD and other neurodevelopmental subgroups summarised in the review.
assessment.result: Discussed choline as a possible modifiable neurodevelopmental factor.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No ADHD treatment-effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supplies choline-status context for attention, not a dosing rule.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; not a choline-for-ADHD trial.

dietary_input_assessments.operation: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.
dietary_input_assessments.assessment_limitations: Transport-ion capacity does not establish that added dietary salt increases brain choline uptake or acetylcholine output. CNS homeostasis and membrane gradients intervene. Chloride is not assumed to have identical transport stoichiometry and is not independently admitted here.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Existing structured composition and provisional food research for this exact canonical input were inspected. Reuse these source/form-qualified foods; do not infer an effective food dose or invent additional relationships.

functional_dependency.statement: Sodium supports the electrochemical coupling required for high-affinity CHT1 choline uptake, sustaining substrate-entry capacity for acetylcholine synthesis.

dietary_supply.statement: The same canonical nutrient is supplied by the inspected food records. Tissue uptake and homeostasis remain distinct from an effect of extra intake.

title: Neuronal Membrane DHA Incorporation
mission: Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.
summary: DHA, a long-chain omega-3 fat, is built into the phospholipids of neuronal membranes. Membranes that contain it support the structure neurons use to signal. The carrier matters: DHA bound as lysophosphatidylcholine can cross into the brain, and in animals phospholipid DHA accumulated in the brain more than triglyceride DHA. That is structural delivery, not a general omega-3 effect.
dose_sensitivity: No intake-response range established for human neuronal-membrane DHA

dietary_lever_presentations.label: DHA
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: DHA is the omega-3 fat built into neuronal membranes. Phospholipid-bound DHA changes how the fat is carried for barrier transport; it is not a second independent treatment lever.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Membrane DHA is a structural context for synaptic signalling {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}}. An observational multi-nutrient study in children seeking help for ADHD-related symptoms cannot isolate membrane DHA from co-supplemented minerals {{cite:huss_supplementation_2010}}. Omega-3 ADHD reviews remain contextual {{cite:pei-chen_chang_personalised_2021}}.

DHA in neuronal phospholipids supports membrane architecture used in synaptic signalling {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}} {{cite:patrick_role_2019}}. Delivery form can change accretion in an animal model {{cite:liu_higher_2014}}. Those are structural and transport findings, not cognitive-clarity scores after a human DHA change.

Combined omega-3/6 with magnesium and zinc was followed by fewer emotional-problem scores in an observational ADHD-seeking cohort {{cite:huss_supplementation_2010}}. Membrane DHA remains the mechanism boundary; the multi-nutrient design cannot isolate incorporation {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}}.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methyl-donor pool can constrain this mechanism’s governed neuronal-membrane DHA-incorporation capacity.
established_links: Phospholipid-DHA carrier biology is supported by PM7-F2 and PM7-F3.
Upstream BRS2-FM3-PM7 conditionally admits KC1 for hepatic PEMT formation using donor-restriction evidence (PM7-F5; chew_folate_choline_2011). This upstream admission is not automatically inherited.
Human feeding evidence supports methyl-derived LPC-DHA enrichment, not absolute carrier supply or brain uptake: Klatt et al., https://doi.org/10.1017/S0007114519002009 (Figures 5–7).
MFSD2A loss reduces labelled LPC-DHA brain uptake in mice: Nguyen et al. (2014), https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24828044/.

PEMT knockout and dietary DHA rescue connect PEMT biology to fetal brain phospholipid DHA: da Costa et al. (2010), https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19889625/. Genetic enzyme loss is not donor inadequacy, and fetal accretion is not adult maintenance.
inferred_links: Named methyl-donor inadequacy reduces net brain-available DHA-carrier supply sufficiently to constrain the DHA incorporation capacity governed here; compensation and clearance are not resolved.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: Retain unresolved, not rejected. A supported upstream chain is permissible; no end-to-end human trial or absolute-flux assay is universally required. The prior carrier-only assessment did not review the relevant upstream chain. Supplementary primary sources are identified in established_links and appraised in the Stage 2B report. They support carrier production, transport and a developmental PEMT dependency, but do not yet establish that named-donor inadequacy constrains this PM's capacity in an applicable context. Resolve the effect of donor inadequacy on net carrier availability and brain incorporation, including compensatory routes; an explicitly evidenced mechanistic chain may suffice. No admitted mapping follows from relevance alone, and no biological absence follows from non-admission.

scientific_findings_intro: Human PET and plasma measurements estimated whole-brain DHA incorporation at 3.8 ± 1.7 mg/day; turnover and half-life estimates additionally used a previously reported brain DHA pool and steady-state assumptions. [[8]](#pm-ref-8) A porcine study found greater gray-matter DHA accretion from phospholipid-bound than triglyceride-bound DHA, consistent with reviewed carrier-dependent delivery biology. [[5]](#pm-ref-5) [[1]](#pm-ref-1) These findings establish measured incorporation and delivery-form relevance, without defining an optimal oral dose, capsule-to-brain transfer fraction or cognitive benefit.

scientific_findings.finding_label: DHA is a structural neuronal-membrane polyunsaturated fat
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) is a long-chain omega-3 fat built into neuronal-membrane phospholipids. That is a structural role, not a dosing rule.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports the mission of a signal-ready lipid foundation. It does not show that a single meal resets membranes or that DHA treats ADHD.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: DHA is a structural polyunsaturated fatty acid of neuronal membranes; that structural role is not a human dosing or ADHD-treatment rule.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A review of omega-3 fats in brain development and function treats DHA as a major structural component of neuronal membranes with implications for signalling architecture. That supports reading this mechanism as membrane composition. It does not measure everyday dietary control of human membrane DHA or isolate ADHD treatment.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Narrative review spanning development and psychopathology hypotheses. It is not a human membrane-accretion trial after a defined DHA food form.

evidence_considered.label: McNamara and Carlson (2006)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Long-chain omega-3 fats, especially DHA, are structural components of neuronal membranes relevant to brain development and function.

assessment.study: Narrative review of omega-3 roles in brain development, function and psychopathology risk.
assessment.population: Mixed developmental, animal and human literature summarised in the review.
assessment.result: Identified DHA as a principal membrane PUFA with signalling-architecture implications.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary dose-response or ADHD treatment estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the structural membrane role of DHA.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; not a human incorporation trial.

scientific_findings.finding_label: LPC-DHA uses MFSD2A for barrier transport
scientific_findings.finding_summary: DHA carried as lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC-DHA) is a preferred substrate for MFSD2A transport at the blood–brain barrier. The phospholipid carrier form matters for presentation.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Phospholipid-bound DHA is delivery context for this mechanism. It is not a second independent clinical lever and does not by itself prove that choline intake constrains incorporation.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: LPC-DHA is transported by MFSD2A more efficiently than free or triglyceride-bound DHA; carrier form is a transport property, not a choline-intake or ADHD-dosing rule.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A phosphatidylcholine-DHA review describes conversion toward LPC-DHA and MFSD2A-mediated barrier transport as the efficient route relative to free or triglyceride-bound DHA. That establishes why phospholipid carriage is mechanistically distinct. It does not measure human membrane DHA after ordinary choline intake.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Mechanistic and disease-context review, including APOE4 discussion. It is not a human dietary-choline or ADHD trial.

evidence_considered.label: Patrick (2019)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Phosphatidylcholine-DHA can generate LPC-DHA, which crosses the blood–brain barrier via MFSD2A more efficiently than non-phospholipid forms.

assessment.study: Review of phosphatidylcholine-DHA transport and APOE4-associated Alzheimer context.
assessment.population: Mixed human genetic and mechanistic literature; not a dietary ADHD sample.
assessment.result: Identified LPC-DHA / MFSD2A as the efficient barrier-transport route.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No ordinary-diet incorporation estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes carrier-form transport chemistry.
assessment.limitations: Review; does not show choline intake constrains DHA incorporation.

evidence_considered.label: Quek et al. (2016)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: Radiolabelled LPC and controlled transport-site/ion conditions.
evidence_considered.directional_finding: MFSD2A transport is sodium-dependent; human transporter binding-site mutations and lipid-uptake assays support the coupling mechanism.

assessment.study: Human MFSD2A modelling with biochemical site-mutant lipid transport assays.
assessment.population: Experimental cells expressing human transporter.
assessment.result: MFSD2A transport is sodium-dependent; human transporter binding-site mutations and lipid-uptake assays support the coupling mechanism.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No additional magnitude inferred.
assessment.evidence_summary: MFSD2A transport is sodium-dependent; human transporter binding-site mutations and lipid-uptake assays support the coupling mechanism.
assessment.limitations: This supports the specific LPC-DHA carrier route, not all DHA delivery or direct neural incorporation from a meal. Sodium homeostasis, carrier formation and membrane gradients intervene; no added-salt recommendation, food-effective dose or clinical benefit.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary transport/mutant experiments and model limitations retrieved 26 October 2026.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Phospholipid DHA accretes more than triglyceride DHA in a porcine model
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Dietary DHA provided as phospholipid produced higher gray-matter DHA accretion than the same fatty acid as triglyceride in neonatal piglets. That is an animal delivery-form finding, not a human dosing rule.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Use this as evidence that phospholipid versus triglyceride form can change accretion in that model. Do not read it as a human capsule dose or an ADHD protocol.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Phospholipid-bound dietary DHA produced greater gray-matter DHA accretion than triglyceride-bound DHA in neonatal piglets; that animal contrast is not a human dosing or ADHD-treatment rule.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A controlled porcine comparison found about 1.9-fold greater gray-matter DHA accretion from phospholipid DHA than from triglyceride DHA. That supports a delivery-form difference for accretion. It does not establish human membrane dosing or that choline intake, rather than the DHA phospholipid itself, was the limiting input.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Neonatal piglets, not children or adults. The contrast is lipid class of DHA, not a choline-supplement arm.

evidence_considered.label: Liu et al. (2014)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Phospholipid-bound dietary DHA produced higher brain gray-matter DHA accretion than triglyceride-bound DHA in neonatal piglets.

assessment.study: Controlled comparison of matched DHA intake as phospholipid versus triglyceride.
assessment.population: Neonatal piglets.
assessment.result: Approximately 1.9-fold greater gray-matter DHA accretion from the phospholipid form.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About 1.9-fold accretion contrast in that animal model.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows delivery form can change brain DHA accretion in piglets.
assessment.limitations: Animal model; not a human dose and not a choline-intake test.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Colletti et al. (2021)

connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Sourcing and clinical-application review; not a neuronal-membrane incorporation measurement.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Patted et al. (2024)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Broader omega-3 source and function review, including contaminant-context discussion.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: General source review; not a finding on MFSD2A transport or membrane accretion.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Multi-nutrient ADHD-seeking observations cannot isolate membrane DHA
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Children seeking help for ADHD-related symptoms showed attention and emotional-score changes after combined omega-3/6, magnesium and zinc. That observational mix cannot isolate neuronal-membrane DHA.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Treat Huss as supportive phenome context with hard limits. It is not evidence that membrane DHA incorporation treats ADHD.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Observational multi-nutrient supplementation in ADHD-seeking children is translationally adjacent to attention and emotion scores; it cannot isolate membrane DHA incorporation as the cause.
scientific_findings.synthesis: An observational cohort taking omega-3/6 with magnesium and zinc reported SNAP-IV and SDQ changes from baseline. An omega-3 ADHD review supplies personalised-medicine context. Together they keep attention and emotion mappings in view. They do not isolate phospholipid-DHA transport or membrane accretion.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Uncontrolled observational design and co-supplemented minerals. Chang is a review, not a membrane-DHA trial.

evidence_considered.label: Huss et al. (2010)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Combined PUFA, magnesium and zinc was followed by attention and emotional-problem score changes; membrane DHA cannot be isolated.

assessment.study: Observational cohort of multi-nutrient supplementation.
assessment.population: Children seeking medical advice for ADHD-related symptoms.
assessment.result: SNAP-IV attention/hyperactivity and SDQ emotional-problem scores improved versus baseline.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Within-cohort score changes; no DHA-only contrast.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supplies ADHD-adjacent outcome context with hard attribution limits.
assessment.limitations: Observational; omega-3/6 plus magnesium and zinc; not membrane DHA.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Pei-Chen Chang (2021)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews omega-3 fatty acids in ADHD as personalised-medicine context.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Narrative review; does not measure neuronal-membrane DHA incorporation.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Human brain DHA incorporation is not an oral dose requirement
scientific_findings.finding_summary: A PET study in 14 healthy adults estimated whole-brain DHA incorporation at 3.8 ± 1.7 mg/day. This is brain uptake from circulating unesterified DHA, not a dietary or supplement dose.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Distinguish measured tracer uptake and plasma DHA from model-derived net incorporation and turnover. These figures do not establish supplement efficacy or an optimal intake.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human PET estimates of circulating DHA incorporation quantify brain replacement under studied conditions; they do not directly measure oral dose requirements.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Umhau et al. combined intravenous [1-11C]DHA PET incorporation coefficients with plasma unesterified DHA concentrations to estimate 3.8 ± 1.7 mg/day (mean ± SD) for the whole brain. Using a previously reported 5 g brain DHA pool, the authors estimated approximately 0.076% daily turnover and a 911-day (about 2.5-year) half-life under a steady-state replacement model.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The 5 g pool was an external estimate, not measured brain DHA in these participants. Net consumption and half-life are model-derived. The study did not test oral dosing, distinguish all delivery routes, measure supplement benefit, or establish needs during development, deficiency or disease.

evidence_considered.label: Umhau et al. (2009)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: PET and plasma measurements supported an estimated adult whole-brain DHA incorporation rate of 3.8 ± 1.7 mg/day.

assessment.study: Intravenous [1-11C]DHA PET kinetic study.
assessment.population: 14 healthy adult humans.
assessment.result: Measured tracer uptake and plasma DHA were used to calculate whole-brain net incorporation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 3.8 ± 1.7 mg/day; estimated 911-day half-life using a reported 5 g pool.
assessment.evidence_summary: Quantifies adult brain incorporation rather than oral intake.
assessment.limitations: Steady-state kinetic model; pool size assumed from prior literature; no oral supplementation comparison.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Choline contributes to methyl-derived LPC-DHA carrier supply
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Choline tracing supports contribution to the PEMT-derived LPC-DHA route; separate transport experiments establish LPC-DHA as a brain-delivery substrate.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Choline tracing supports contribution to the PEMT-derived LPC-DHA route; separate transport experiments establish LPC-DHA as a brain-delivery substrate.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Human plasma isotopic enrichment is not absolute hepatic flux, net carrier supply or adult neuronal DHA incorporation. Higher choline intake did not increase total plasma LPC-DHA in the feeding study. The carrier-to-brain connection uses separate cell/mouse transport evidence. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint, compensation and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The human controlled-feeding study distinguished methyl-derived d3-LPC-DHA from intact-choline-route d9-LPC-DHA. Higher choline intake increased d3 enrichment without increasing total plasma LPC-DHA. Separate MFSD2A cell assays and labelled uptake in mice establish the transport route. Connecting these studies supports bounded upstream carrier provision, not measured additional adult neuronal incorporation.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Human plasma isotopic enrichment is not absolute hepatic flux, net carrier supply or adult neuronal DHA incorporation. Higher choline intake did not increase total plasma LPC-DHA in the feeding study. The carrier-to-brain connection uses separate cell/mouse transport evidence. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint, compensation and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.

evidence_considered.label: Klatt et al. (2019)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Higher choline intake increased methyl-derived d3-LPC-DHA enrichment but not total plasma LPC-DHA.

assessment.study: Post hoc isotope analysis of a controlled 10-week choline feeding trial with supplemental DHA.
assessment.population: Non-pregnant, pregnant and lactating women; not an adult brain-incorporation experiment.
assessment.result: Figures 5–7 distinguish total LPC-DHA from d3 and d9 enrichment; d3 identifies the methyl-derived route.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No main choline effect on total plasma LPC-DHA; increased d3 enrichment. No brain uptake effect estimated.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports choline contribution to the methyl-derived carrier route.
assessment.limitations: Full Results and figure captions inspected. Plasma enrichment does not isolate net carrier production or brain delivery; reproductive context affects interpretation.

evidence_considered.label: Nguyen et al. (2014)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: MFSD2A transported LPC-DHA in cell assays; knockout mice had reduced labelled plasma-to-brain LPC uptake.

assessment.study: Cell transport experiments and Mfsd2a knockout mouse uptake studies.
assessment.population: Cells and mice; not choline-fed adult humans.
assessment.result: Cell and brain uptake experiments establish the LPC-DHA transport substrate.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reduced labelled uptake after transporter loss; no dietary methyl-donor effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports the carrier-to-brain transport link independently of dietary choline responsiveness.
assessment.limitations: Abstract and figure descriptions inspected; full subscription methods/results not obtained. Transporter loss is not donor inadequacy.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Folate and betaine replenish the methyl resource upstream of DHA-carrier formation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Folate-dependent remethylation and hepatic betaine/BHMT remethylation replenish methionine for SAM-dependent PEMT chemistry, which connects to the independently established methyl-derived LPC-DHA carrier route.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Folate-dependent remethylation and hepatic betaine/BHMT remethylation replenish methionine for SAM-dependent PEMT chemistry, which connects to the independently established methyl-derived LPC-DHA carrier route.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Supported biochemical supply chain, not a demonstrated increase in net adult brain DHA incorporation. Folate/choline compensation, hepatic BHMT, SAM turnover and carrier remodelling vary by context. Mouse folate effects were sex/tissue dependent; betaine rescue used ethanol-exposed rats. The downstream human tracer study administered choline, not folate or betaine. A donor-specific limiting effect and extra-intake benefit remain unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Folate-dependent remethylation and hepatic betaine/BHMT remethylation replenish methionine for SAM-dependent PEMT chemistry, which connects to the independently established methyl-derived LPC-DHA carrier route.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Supported biochemical supply chain, not a demonstrated increase in net adult brain DHA incorporation. Folate/choline compensation, hepatic BHMT, SAM turnover and carrier remodelling vary by context. Mouse folate effects were sex/tissue dependent; betaine rescue used ethanol-exposed rats. The downstream human tracer study administered choline, not folate or betaine. A donor-specific limiting effect and extra-intake benefit remain unresolved.

evidence_considered.label: Chew et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Donor restriction reduced pathway-specific methyl incorporation in female liver.

assessment.study: Eight-week folate restriction versus otherwise matched control diets with labelled choline. Indexed primary methods, results and discussion assessed.
assessment.population: Male and female Mthfr wild-type and heterozygous mice.
assessment.result: Females had lower hepatic d3-PC enrichment and product/precursor enrichment ratio; males lacked that hepatic response.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Hepatic d3-PC enrichment 30% lower (P=0.017); d3-PC:d9-choline ratio P=0.049.
assessment.evidence_summary: Donor restriction reduced pathway-specific methyl incorporation in female liver.
assessment.limitations: Precursor enrichment, turnover and methyl competition affect this measurement; total PEMT flux was not measured.

evidence_considered.label: Kharbanda et al. (2007)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Betaine corrected production under an imposed methylation imbalance.

assessment.study: Control/ethanol liquid diets with or without 1% betaine for four weeks. Primary abstract assessed; full assay methods unavailable.
assessment.population: Male Wistar rats.
assessment.result: Betaine restored SAM:SAH balance and reported PEMT-mediated PC production under ethanol exposure.

assessment.evidence_summary: Betaine corrected production under an imposed methylation imbalance.
assessment.limitations: Supplement rescue does not establish ordinary betaine deficiency; assay details and ethanol context limit attribution.

title: GABA Synthesis Capacity
mission: Maintain sufficient glutamate decarboxylase capacity, and sufficient PLP cofactor to support it, so GABA can be synthesised from glutamate.
summary: The brain makes GABA, its main calming transmitter, by converting glutamate with an enzyme that needs the active form of vitamin B6. That reaction supplies GABA for later inhibitory signalling. Vitamin B6 in food is the dietary route to the cofactor, and it mainly affects reserve capacity rather than everyday output.

dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: The evidence establishes glutamate as the GAD substrate, not that dietary glutamate or protein controls neuronal glutamate availability or human brain GABA synthesis.
