scientific_findings_intro: Human MAT structural and kinetic studies identify reaction participants, while kinetic models disagree about substrate-binding order. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) These studies directly establish enzyme mechanism and biochemical requirements. They do not test ordinary dietary modulation, human in-vivo synthesis flux or downstream methylation outcomes, so those effects remain beyond the evidence summarised here.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Biochemical provenance: MAT reaction
scientific_findings.finding_summary: MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis directly requires methionine and ATP and uses active-site magnesium and potassium ions to support ATP-dependent catalysis.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This establishes the biochemical reaction and its direct requirements. It does not establish that increasing dietary methionine, magnesium or potassium increases SAMe synthesis in adequately nourished humans; ATP is an intracellular biochemical substrate, not a dietary lever.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis directly requires methionine and ATP and uses active-site magnesium and potassium ions to support ATP-dependent catalysis.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The MAT reaction and catalytic participants have curated provenance. Human MAT2A studies support conflicting ATP-first and rapid-equilibrium random substrate-binding models; no settled universal order is asserted. MAT2B stability is assessed separately in proposed F5.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The primary evidence uses purified recombinant protein and crystallised human enzyme rather than intact human physiology. Active-site ion requirements do not show that physiological magnesium or potassium availability ordinarily limits MAT activity. The studies do not establish a methionine intake-response relationship, a clinically meaningful reserve-capacity threshold, or a phenome outcome.

evidence_considered.label: Bailey et al. (2021)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Purified human MAT2A followed an ordered ATP-first, methionine-second kinetic mechanism; MAT2B stabilised the enzyme without materially changing the tested catalytic parameters.

assessment.study: Purified recombinant human MAT2A steady-state kinetics, product/dead-end inhibition and isothermal titration calorimetry, with and without MAT2B.
assessment.population: Purified human MAT2A/MAT2B proteins; no cells, animals or human participants.
assessment.result: ATP bound before methionine; SAM was released before phosphate and pyrophosphate. MAT2B bound tightly and stabilised low-concentration MAT2A but did not significantly change the tested kinetic parameters.
assessment.effect_magnitude: ATP Kd 80 ± 30 μM and Km 50 ± 10 μM; MAT2B Kd 6 ± 1 nM. No significant catalytic-parameter change under saturating MAT2B conditions.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human-enzyme evidence for the ordered MAT2A reaction and distinction between catalytic activity and MAT2B-mediated stability.
assessment.limitations: In-vitro purified-enzyme conditions do not establish in-vivo flux limitation, dietary responsiveness, tissue-specific regulation or phenome effects.

evidence_considered.label: Murray et al. (2016)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: High-resolution human MATα2 structures captured substrates/products and active-site ion coordination across ATP-driven SAMe formation.

assessment.study: X-ray crystallography of human MATα2 with methionine, ATP analogues, SAMe, adenosine and phosphate-state ligands.
assessment.population: Purified crystallised human MATα2 protein; no cells, animals or human participants.
assessment.result: Structures captured methionine repositioning toward ATP C5′, SAMe/product states and phosphate-group coordination by magnesium and potassium ions.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Structures ranged from 1.1 Å to 2.34 Å resolution; no physiological effect size applies.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct structural support for the reaction chemistry and catalytic-ion requirement of human MAT.
assessment.limitations: Static ligand-bound structures establish catalytic geometry, not physiological nutrient limitation, in-vivo reaction rate, dietary dose response or clinical outcome.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Chiang et al. (1996)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Foundational review establishes SAMe as a major methyl donor and places MAT synthesis upstream of transmethylation.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: It is a broad methylation review and does not independently quantify human MAT kinetics, active-site ion requirements or dietary control of synthesis flux.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Corrillero Bravo et al. (2022)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Measured circulating SAM, SAH and SAM:SAH after contrasting four-week dietary patterns in healthy adults.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: The biomarkers do not isolate MAT synthesis flux; group trajectories were similar, so the study does not establish a dietary lever for PM3.

scientific_findings.finding_label: SAM and SAM:SAH are pool-state markers, not synthesis-flux measures
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Measured SAM concentration and the SAM:SAH ratio reflect the balance of synthesis, methyl-group utilisation, SAH formation and clearance and therefore cannot by themselves identify MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity.
scientific_findings.synthesis: SAM concentration is a metabolite-pool measurement. The SAM:SAH ratio is commonly interpreted as a methylation index because SAM supplies methyl groups while SAH inhibits methyltransferases. Both values integrate production and consumption processes; neither is a direct MAT flux assay. Careful sample handling is also material because SAM is unstable under neutral and alkaline conditions.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The principal source is a methods and profiling study, not a formal validation against isotope-traced MAT flux. The ratio may be useful for methyl-group homeostasis and inherited-metabolism assessment, but its exact meaning varies by biological matrix, compartment and pre-analytical handling.

evidence_considered.label: Corrillero Bravo et al. (2022)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Validated SAM/SAH measurement as a pool/homeostasis readout and found no differential change after four-week vegan versus meat-rich dietary assignment in healthy adults.

assessment.study: LC-MS/MS method optimisation plus a randomised four-week vegan-versus-meat-rich dietary intervention.
assessment.population: Method reference cohort of 33 healthy adults and dietary intervention cohort of 53 healthy adult omnivores aged 18–60 years.
assessment.result: The method quantified low-nanomolar SAM and SAH across matrices; plasma and urinary SAM, SAH and SAM:SAH showed similar baseline-to-end changes in both diet groups.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Healthy plasma reference ranges were SAM 120 ± 36 nM and SAH 21.5 ± 6.5 nM (mean ± 2 SD); no between-diet synthesis-flux effect was measured.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct evidence that SAM/SAH are measurable pool-state biomarkers and that short-term dietary pattern contrast did not establish PM3 modulation.
assessment.limitations: Small healthy-adult cohorts, four-week duration, circulating/urinary pools rather than tissue-specific MAT flux, and no cognitive or emotional outcome measurement.

scientific_findings.finding_summary: Measured SAM concentration and the SAM:SAH ratio reflect the balance of synthesis, methyl-group utilisation, SAH formation and clearance and therefore cannot by themselves identify MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Mood-treatment evidence does not test endogenous SAMe synthesis
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The repository-attached mood-disorder evidence does not directly demonstrate an effect of endogenous MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity on Emotional Regulation.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The Emotional Regulation relationship is biologically plausible downstream of methyl-donor chemistry but remains indirect for this PM.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The repository-attached mood-disorder evidence does not directly demonstrate an effect of endogenous MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity on Emotional Regulation.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The attached review supports clinical interest in administered SAMe and combined one-carbon nutrients for mood disorders, but its intervention construct is exogenous treatment and its outcomes are mood symptoms. It does not manipulate MAT, quantify endogenous SAMe synthesis flux, or isolate PM3 from upstream folate/B12 remethylation and downstream methyltransferase biology. The PM3-to-Emotional Regulation proposition is therefore an inferred downstream bridge rather than a directly demonstrated relationship.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is an adjudicated gap within the bounded attached corpus, not proof that no relationship exists. The source is a narrative clinical review, mixes interventions and pathway levels, and does not provide a PM3-specific causal test.

evidence_considered.label: Cicero and Minervino (2022)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Reviews exogenous SAMe with folate/B12 in mood-disorder treatment but does not measure MAT activity or endogenous SAMe synthesis flux.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Cognitive relevance is downstream, not a direct MAT-synthesis result
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The repository-attached methylation evidence establishes SAMe's donor role but does not directly demonstrate that endogenous MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity modulates Cognitive Clarity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: General dependence of cognition-relevant pathways on methyl donors must not be presented as direct phenome evidence for PM3.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The repository-attached methylation evidence establishes SAMe's donor role but does not directly demonstrate that endogenous MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis capacity modulates Cognitive Clarity.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The foundational review establishes SAMe as a central methyl donor used in numerous downstream reactions. That broad biochemical role supports plausibility but does not isolate MAT synthesis capacity, measure cognitive clarity, or show that changing synthesis flux changes a cognitive outcome. The PM3-to-Cognitive Clarity relationship therefore remains a mechanistic inference with a direct-evidence gap.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This conclusion is bounded to the attached corpus plus targeted construct clarification. It does not exclude cognitive consequences in severe inherited disorders or downstream methylation studies; those contexts would not by themselves establish ordinary PM3 modulation.

evidence_considered.label: Chiang et al. (1996)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Establishes SAMe as a principal methyl donor across downstream chemistry but does not measure Cognitive Clarity or endogenous MAT synthesis flux.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Biochemical provenance: methionine regeneration
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Folate and betaine remethylation regenerate methionine upstream of MAT-dependent SAMe formation; choline can contribute through betaine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This establishes connected precursor provision. It does not make folate, betaine or choline MAT reactants, demonstrate that more intake raises synthesis, or resolve a donor-inadequacy constraint on MAT capacity.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Folate and betaine remethylation regenerate methionine upstream of MAT-dependent SAMe formation; choline can contribute through betaine.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Existing reviewed PM1-F1, PM2-F1/PM2-F2 and PM3-F1 establish the successive reaction identities. Folate provides 5-methyltetrahydrofolate for B12-dependent methionine synthase, while betaine supplies the alternative BHMT reaction, predominantly in liver and kidney. Choline oxidation can supply betaine. The regenerated methionine is available to the MAT reaction. Evidence supports the route, without requiring each donor to act directly on MAT.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Tissue expression, alternative methionine supply and pathway compensation limit generalisation. SAMe and SAM:SAH are pool-state measurements rather than isolated synthesis rates. No established limiting effect on MAT capacity or nutrient-replete intake benefit is claimed.

evidence_considered.label: Obeid (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Establishes betaine donation and choline provision in connected remethylation; reviewed on PM2-F1/F2.

evidence_considered.directional_finding: Establishes methionine and ATP use in human MAT2A; reviewed on PM3-F1.

evidence_considered.label: Evans et al. (2002)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human BHMT reaction identity; supports betaine-to-methionine provision, not dietary MAT responsiveness.

evidence_considered.label: Salvi and Gadda (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Choline oxidation through betaine aldehyde to betaine; supports route identity, not MAT flux.

evidence_dependency: Bailey et al. (2021) is reused from PM3-F1 to identify MAT substrate use; it is not independent supply-chain or dietary-response evidence.

scientific_findings.finding_label: MAT2B and MAT2A stability
evidence_dependency: Bailey et al. (2021) is also used by PM3-F1 and PM3-F4. Reuse for the stability proposition is not independent replication.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: MAT2B association can preserve MAT2A protein or catalytic stability in purified-human-enzyme and mammalian-cell experiments. This supports a stability contribution to enzyme regulation, not an exclusive explanation of MAT2B action or a demonstrated increase in human SAMe synthesis flux.
scientific_findings.finding_summary: MAT2B association can preserve MAT2A protein or catalytic stability in purified-human-enzyme and mammalian-cell experiments. This supports a stability contribution to enzyme regulation, not an exclusive explanation of MAT2B action or a demonstrated increase in human SAMe synthesis flux.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Purified-enzyme activity decay and mammalian-cell perturbation/rescue support a stability contribution, with non-identical endpoints. Additional allosteric/catalytic regulation remains possible.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Partial cross-model corroboration does not quantify MAT2B-dependent stability or SAMe flux in the human brain. Does not establish that stability is the only MAT2B mechanism: allosteric/catalytic interpretations remain relevant. No dietary methionine, folate, betaine, choline or ADHD intervention effect was assessed.

evidence_considered.label: 10.1021/acs.biochem.1c00672
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Purified human MAT2A lost activity during substrate-free incubation at 37 C; MAT2B preserved activity. Coupled phosphate and direct LC-MS assays distinguish stability from steady-state kinetic effects. Activity half-life about 2.3 minutes without MAT2B; activity retained over the 120-minute experiment with MAT2B. Technical repeats do not constitute independent replication.

title: Methionine Cycle Flux
mission: Maintain balanced methionine-cycle flux so methionine availability, SAM-dependent methylation, homocysteine recycling and transsulfuration remain coordinated across changing physiological demand.
summary: The methionine cycle forms S-adenosylmethionine from methionine, transfers its methyl group, and hydrolyses S-adenosylhomocysteine to adenosine and homocysteine. Homocysteine is then remethylated to methionine or sent into transsulfuration toward cysteine. SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate influence that split. Every tissue can remethylate homocysteine, while transsulfuration is limited to liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas. Metabolite concentrations describe pool state, not the branch rates.
dose_sensitivity: Methionine, folate, vitamin B12, vitamin B6 and riboflavin participate in the cycle. No ordinary-diet dose-response for human remethylation or transsulfuration rates is established.

phenome_relationships.rationale: SAM donates methyl groups, and homocysteine is then split between remethylation and transsulfuration {{cite:chiang_s-adenosylmethionine_1996,finkelstein_homocysteine_1998}}. Homocysteine concentration is discussed as a risk marker for cognitive decline and Alzheimer disease {{cite:luzzi_homocysteine_2022,yu_evidence-based_2020}}. Those studies measure a metabolite level. They do not measure branch rates, and they do not show that changing cycle throughput improves Cognitive Clarity.

Boys with ADHD had higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 than controls, and a separate case-control study linked less healthy diets with lower folate, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12 and with ADHD {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024,wang_dietary_2019}}. Those are concentration and dietary-pattern associations. They do not measure remethylation or transsulfuration rates {{cite:finkelstein_homocysteine_1998,lamers_vitamin_b6_methionine_cycle_2011}}.

kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: The newly retrieved kinetic study supports context-specific intervention responsiveness, not inadequacy of every KC1 constituent or a uniform branch-allocation constraint.
kc_applicability_adjudications.evidence_gap: Evidence for inadequacy of the named shared pool constraining integrated branch allocation, separated from a pharmacological folic-acid response.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methionine–cysteine pool constrains integrated methionine-cycle throughput or the remethylation–transsulfuration split.
established_links: Methionine is the amino acid from which SAM and then homocysteine are formed (PM4-F1).
A liver MAT isoenzyme allows excess methionine to continue SAM synthesis (PM4-F1).
In aged mice, too little or too much methionine removed benefits of a low-amino-acid longevity diet on frailty and metabolic signalling (connected evidence on PM4-F1).
Lamers 2011 measured human methionine-cycle rates and shows context-dependent preservation under moderate B6 restriction; it did not manipulate the sulfur pool.
inferred_links: A defined nutritional/impairment context connecting the named sulfur pool to altered remethylation–transsulfuration allocation beyond substrate provision.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: Whole-body flux can be measured, but no universal human-flux requirement is imposed. Mechanistic entry and mouse frailty outcomes do not establish the additional shared-pool rate limitation.
kc_applicability_adjudications.evidence_gap: A defined nutritional/impairment context connecting the named sulfur pool to altered remethylation–transsulfuration allocation beyond substrate provision.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: KC1’s folate and betaine routes replenish methionine within the integrated cycle; choline supplies the betaine route.
established_links: KC1’s folate and betaine routes replenish methionine within the integrated cycle; choline supplies the betaine route.
inferred_links: BHMT is mainly hepatic/renal and alternative methionine supply can compensate. The supported routes do not show that donor availability limits net cycle rates or the remethylation–transsulfuration split. Homocysteine concentration is not branch flux.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: Each route is reviewed against PM4’s integrated remethylation scope. Folate’s existing atom is retained; betaine/choline are separately supported KC inputs, not inherited Direct/Derived requirements. The stronger limitation on integrated rates remains unresolved.

dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Betaine donates a methyl group through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) to regenerate methionine returned to the integrated methionine cycle.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: BHMT activity is concentrated mainly in liver and kidney; this is not local BHMT activity in every tissue. Folate-dependent remethylation and dietary methionine provide alternative supply. Homocysteine lowering does not establish increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from extra intake in replete individuals.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted upstream dietary constituent provision is distinct from the pool/constraint reference. Existing role, conditional scope and limitations remain unchanged.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Choline can be oxidised to betaine, supplying methyl groups through [PM2 — Betaine/BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation) for methionine regeneration within the integrated methionine cycle.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Only the choline-to-betaine methyl-supply route is admitted here, not choline membrane or neurotransmitter roles. Oxidation, predominantly hepatic/renal BHMT activity and alternative supply constrain interpretation. Increased integrated cycle flux or improved branch balance or benefit from additional choline in replete individuals is not established.

dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Glycine is the acceptor substrate of glycine N-methyltransferase, which consumes SAM and forms SAH and sarcosine during methyl-group handling.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Endogenous glycine synthesis and other methyltransferases also contribute. Enzyme loss is not glycine deficiency; extra dietary glycine has not been established to normalise whole-cycle or brain methylation.
dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Admitted provision/exposure is distinct from a food-specific intervention effect.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Glycine
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Glycine is the acceptor substrate of glycine N-methyltransferase, which consumes SAM and forms SAH and sarcosine during methyl-group handling.

scientific_findings_intro: A controlled human tracer study found unchanged mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation and transsulfuration rates during moderate vitamin B6 restriction, despite sharply reduced plasma PLP and increased cystathionine concentration. [[13]](#pm-ref-13) Pathway reviews provide the regulatory context for these measured branch rates. [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) The combined evidence shows why an altered intermediate concentration cannot be treated as an equivalent change in overall cycle flux; individual responses and the restriction conditions limit generalisation.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Homocysteine is split between remethylation and transsulfuration
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Methionine becomes SAM, SAM donates a methyl group, and SAH is hydrolysed to homocysteine. Homocysteine is then either remethylated to methionine or sent into transsulfuration toward cysteine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This is the integrated route and the branch. It does not assign the MAT, remethylation or transsulfuration reactions to this mechanism, and it does not show that ordinary diet changes the rates.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Methionine-cycle throughput runs from methionine to SAM, methyl transfer and SAH hydrolysis to homocysteine, after which homocysteine is distributed between remethylation and transsulfuration under the influence of SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A methylation review establishes SAM as the methyl donor and SAH hydrolysis to adenosine and homocysteine, and it shows that blocking that hydrolysis can affect methylation of phospholipids, proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules together. A pathway review then places regulation at the distribution of homocysteine between remethylation, which every tissue can perform, and transsulfuration to cystathionine, which is limited to liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas, with SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate as effectors. A human tracer study uses that same partition, measuring postprandial remethylation, transmethylation and total transsulfuration as rates.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The pathway accounts are reviews. Transsulfuration is not present in every tissue. The human rate study was a 28-day vitamin B6 restriction in nine healthy young adults. It does not show that ordinary changes in methionine, folate, or B-vitamin intake change those rates. Individual enzyme reactions remain neighbouring mechanisms.

evidence_considered.label: Chiang et al. (1996)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: SAM donates methyl groups; SAH formed by that transfer is hydrolysed to adenosine and homocysteine; blocking SAH hydrolysis can affect methylation across phospholipids, proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules.

assessment.study: Narrative review of SAM-dependent methylation, SAH hydrolysis and downstream methyl acceptors.
assessment.population: Review of biochemical and cellular literature; no new human cohort.
assessment.result: SAM is the methyl donor. SAH is hydrolysed by SAH hydrolase to adenosine and homocysteine. Blocking that hydrolase can affect methylation of several classes of acceptor at once.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No quantitative flux or concentration effect size.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes methyl transfer and the SAH-to-homocysteine step as a shared route into many methylation reactions.
assessment.limitations: Does not describe remethylation, transsulfuration or a measured SAM:SAH ratio, and does not test diet or cognition.

evidence_considered.label: Finkelstein (1998)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Homocysteine is distributed between tissue-wide remethylation and transsulfuration to cystathionine in liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas; SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate are effectors of that distribution.

assessment.study: Review of mammalian methionine-cycle and transsulfuration pathways and their regulation.
assessment.population: Mammalian pathway review; no new human experiment.
assessment.result: Every tissue can synthesise SAM, use it for transmethylation, hydrolyse SAH and remethylate homocysteine. Transsulfuration catabolises homocysteine in liver, kidney, small intestine and pancreas. Regulation is the distribution of homocysteine between remethylation and conversion to cystathionine.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No numeric rate or intake-response estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the regulated branch between recycling and transsulfuration and names SAM, SAH and methyl-tetrahydrofolate as effectors.
assessment.limitations: Review-level pathway evidence. It does not measure human rates, test ordinary diets, or show a cognitive or attention outcome.

evidence_considered.label: Lamers et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human postprandial kinetics were quantified as remethylation, transmethylation and total transsulfuration rates, confirming that the branch is measurable as rates rather than as a single metabolite level.

assessment.study: Primed constant infusion of labelled methionine and leucine in the postprandial state, repeated after 28 days of dietary vitamin B6 restriction.
assessment.population: Nine healthy adults (4 men, 5 women), aged 20–35 years.
assessment.result: The protocol quantified remethylation, transmethylation and total transsulfuration. Mean rates were unchanged by the restriction.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Plasma PLP fell from 49 ± 4 nmol/L to 19 ± 2 nmol/L. Mean cycle rates did not change. No rate delta is reported because the mean change was null.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows that human cycle throughput can be partitioned into measured rates.
assessment.limitations: Small healthy-adult sample, 28-day restriction, postprandial state only, and large individual variation. Not a test of cognitive or attention outcomes.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Kumar et al. (2017)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: The repository record describes a review of transsulfuration from homocysteine toward cysteine and glutathione.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: That record does not establish remethylation or the regulated split between the two exits.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Aragão et al. (2024)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Riboflavin was listed beside this mechanism because vitamin B2 is a cofactor of a folate-cycle enzyme.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: The paper is a general riboflavin physiology review and does not test methionine-cycle throughput or the homocysteine split.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Fanti et al. (2026)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Tests how little or how much methionine sits inside a low-amino-acid longevity diet.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: The mouse endpoints are frailty and metabolic signalling, and the human component is epidemiology rather than a methionine trial. Neither measures cycle branch rates or an attention or cognitive treatment effect.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Parkhitko et al. (2026)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews methionine restriction as an ageing intervention.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: It is an ageing and disease review, not a measurement of human cycle rates and not an ADHD treatment study.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Moderate vitamin B6 restriction left mean cycle rates unchanged
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In healthy young adults, 28 days of dietary vitamin B6 restriction lowered the active B6 coenzyme in blood but did not change mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation or total transsulfuration rates.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: A lower vitamin B6 supply in this range did not limit the integrated rates. The rise in cystathionine is a separate intermediate signal.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Moderate dietary vitamin B6 restriction that lowered plasma pyridoxal 5'-phosphate did not change mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation or total transsulfuration rates in healthy young adults.
scientific_findings.synthesis: One controlled feeding study measured the three cycle rates with methionine tracers before and after restriction. Plasma pyridoxal 5'-phosphate fell sharply. The mean rates did not change, although individuals differed. Cystathionine concentration rose, and its fractional synthesis rate rose in most participants. The integrated rates and that intermediate marker moved differently.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Nine healthy young adults, 28 days, and the postprandial state only. The authors report large individual variation, so a mean null result does not describe every person. The study does not test severe deficiency, folate or vitamin B12 restriction, ordinary mixed diets, or any cognitive or attention outcome.

evidence_considered.label: Lamers et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation and total transsulfuration rates did not change after vitamin B6 restriction, while cystathionine concentration and its fractional synthesis rate rose.

assessment.study: Within-person tracer study of methionine-cycle kinetics at usual B6 status and after 28 days of dietary vitamin B6 restriction.
assessment.population: Nine healthy adults (4 men, 5 women), aged 20–35 years.
assessment.result: Mean remethylation, transsulfuration and transmethylation rates were unchanged. Plasma cystathionine rose, and fractional cystathionine synthesis increased in 8 of 9 participants.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Plasma PLP fell from 49 ± 4 nmol/L to 19 ± 2 nmol/L (P < 0.0001). Cystathionine rose from 142 ± 8 to 236 ± 9 nmol/L (P < 0.001). Fractional cystathionine synthesis rose by a mean of 12% in 8 of 9 participants. Mean cycle-rate changes were null.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human evidence that this degree of vitamin B6 restriction did not change the integrated postprandial rates.
assessment.limitations: Small sample, short restriction, healthy young adults, postprandial conditions, and wide individual variation. Cystathionine kinetics are not a substitute for the total transsulfuration rate.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Metabolite concentrations are not cycle branch rates
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Homocysteine, SAM, SAH and cystathionine concentrations do not measure remethylation, transmethylation or total transsulfuration rates.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The human studies attached to this mechanism report blood homocysteine, or in one tracer study cystathionine, as concentrations. Folic acid lowered blood homocysteine, with a further fall when vitamin B12 was added, and vitamin B6 added no further concentration change. A separate small trial reported lower plasma homocysteine after vitamin B12, fish oil, or both. In the tracer study, cystathionine concentration rose while mean total transsulfuration rate did not. The pathway review defines the biological quantity as the distribution of homocysteine between two routes, which these concentration changes do not report.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The concentration trials were not designed as flux studies, so their null or positive homocysteine results cannot be reread as rate results. The tracer dissociation is limited to cystathionine versus total transsulfuration in nine young adults. SAM and SAH were not the measured endpoints of the homocysteine trials.
evidence_dependency: Finkelstein (1998) is also primary Evidence Considered in PM4-F1. Lamers et al. (2011) is also primary Evidence Considered in PM4-F1 and PM4-F2.

evidence_considered.label: Collaboration (1998)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Folic acid lowered blood homocysteine concentration, vitamin B12 added a further concentration reduction, and vitamin B6 did not.

assessment.study: Individual-patient meta-analysis of 12 randomised trials of folic acid-based supplements.
assessment.population: 1114 people in the pooled trials.
assessment.result: Blood homocysteine concentration fell with folic acid. Vitamin B12 produced an additional reduction. Vitamin B6 did not add a significant further reduction.
assessment.effect_magnitude: After standardisation to pretreatment homocysteine of 12 μmol/L and folate of 12 nmol/L, folic acid reduced homocysteine by 25% (95% CI 23% to 28%). Vitamin B12 (mean 0.5 mg/day) added 7% (3% to 10%). Vitamin B6 (mean 16.5 mg/day) had no significant additional effect.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes a concentration response to folic acid and vitamin B12.
assessment.limitations: The endpoint is blood homocysteine concentration. Remethylation and transsulfuration rates were not measured.

evidence_considered.label: Huang et al. (2015)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Plasma homocysteine concentration fell during vitamin B12, fish-oil, and combined supplementation.

assessment.study: Eight-week randomised trial of vitamin B12, fish oil, or both.
assessment.population: 38 participants randomised to three groups.
assessment.result: Plasma homocysteine was lower in each group after the intervention. The recorded outcomes also included fatty acids and cardiovascular risk markers.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The report states plasma homocysteine reductions of 22%, 19% and 39% in the vitamin B12, fish-oil, and combination groups. No cycle-rate estimate is given.
assessment.evidence_summary: A small supplementation trial changed a homocysteine concentration.
assessment.limitations: Concentration and cardiovascular markers only. No remethylation or transsulfuration rate, and no cognitive or attention endpoint.

evidence_considered.label: Lamers et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Cystathionine concentration rose while mean total transsulfuration rate did not change.

assessment.study: Tracer measurement of methionine-cycle rates and cystathionine kinetics before and after vitamin B6 restriction.
assessment.population: Nine healthy adults aged 20–35 years.
assessment.result: Plasma cystathionine increased and fractional cystathionine synthesis rose in most participants, while mean total transsulfuration rate was unchanged.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Cystathionine rose from 142 ± 8 to 236 ± 9 nmol/L. Mean total transsulfuration rate change was null.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct within-study evidence that an intermediate concentration can change while the integrated transsulfuration rate does not.
assessment.limitations: One small postprandial study. The dissociation is for cystathionine versus total transsulfuration, not a general proof about every metabolite in every tissue.

evidence_considered.label: Finkelstein (1998)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: The regulated quantity is the distribution of homocysteine between remethylation and conversion to cystathionine, not a standing metabolite concentration.

assessment.study: Review of pathway regulation.
assessment.population: Mammalian pathway review; no new cohort.
assessment.result: Metabolic regulation is described as the distribution of available homocysteine between the two exits.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No numeric estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Names the biological quantity that concentration studies did not measure.
assessment.limitations: Does not itself compare a concentration with a tracer rate.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Homocysteine–cognition evidence does not measure cycle rates
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Reviews link higher homocysteine with cognitive decline and Alzheimer risk. They do not measure cycle branch rates, and they do not show that changing those rates improves Cognitive Clarity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Homocysteine can mark strain at the branch point. A dementia risk association is not evidence that this mechanism treats a cognitive disorder.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Evidence linking homocysteine concentration to cognitive decline or Alzheimer risk does not demonstrate that integrated methionine-cycle rates modulate Cognitive Clarity.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A narrative review treats homocysteine as a risk factor for cerebrovascular disease and degenerative dementias and states that effects on specific cognitive domains are poorly mapped. A large prevention review places hyperhomocysteinaemia among Class I factors for Alzheimer disease. Both concern homocysteine level or status. Neither measures remethylation or transsulfuration rates, and neither tests an intervention on integrated cycle throughput.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is a boundary on the attached cognition sources, not a claim that homocysteine is irrelevant to brain disease. Methionine-restriction experiments were assessed separately and address ageing phenotypes rather than Cognitive Clarity.

evidence_considered.label: Luzzi et al. (2022)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Higher homocysteine is reviewed as a risk factor for cognitive decline and degenerative dementias, without a cycle-rate measurement.

assessment.study: Narrative review of homocysteine, cognitive functions and degenerative dementias.
assessment.population: Published human studies of homocysteine and dementia or cognitive decline; no new cohort.
assessment.result: The review treats homocysteine as a risk factor for cerebrovascular disease and degenerative dementias, and states that domain-specific cognitive effects are poorly investigated.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No single pooled effect size is reported.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports a homocysteine-concentration association with cognitive decline contexts.
assessment.limitations: Does not measure methionine-cycle rates or test a dietary cycle intervention against Cognitive Clarity.

evidence_considered.label: Yu et al. (2020)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Hyperhomocysteinaemia is classed as a strong observational risk factor for Alzheimer disease, not as a measured cycle-flux exposure.

assessment.study: Systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective observational studies and randomised trials on Alzheimer prevention.
assessment.population: 243 observational prospective studies and 153 randomised trials across 104 factors and 11 interventions.
assessment.result: Hyperhomocysteinaemia is listed among Class I, Level A suggestions for Alzheimer prevention.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The paper assigns an evidence class. It does not report a methionine-cycle rate effect.
assessment.evidence_summary: Places homocysteine status among modifiable Alzheimer risk factors.
assessment.limitations: The factor is hyperhomocysteinaemia, not integrated cycle throughput. The review does not show that changing branch rates improves Cognitive Clarity.

scientific_findings.finding_label: ADHD nutrient associations do not measure cycle rates
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Children with ADHD have been reported to have higher homocysteine, lower B vitamins, and less favourable diets. Those associations do not measure cycle branch rates and do not show that changing the rates improves attention.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Serum homocysteine and B-vitamin differences can sit beside attention disorders. They are not evidence that this mechanism determines focus or that a diet treats ADHD.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Homocysteine and B-vitamin differences in ADHD cohorts, and dietary-pattern associations, do not demonstrate that integrated methionine-cycle rates determine Focus / Attention Stability.
scientific_findings.synthesis: One case-control study of boys found higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 in ADHD than in controls. Another case-control study found lower folate, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12, together with a less favourable dietary pattern, and modelled nutritional biochemistry as a link between diet and ADHD. Both are observational concentration or intake associations. Neither infused tracers or reported remethylation or transsulfuration rates.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The studies can still describe real group differences in homocysteine and B vitamins. They cannot isolate this mechanism from the many other nutrients that differed, and they contain no attention outcome after a cycle-rate intervention. Methionine-restriction literature was assessed separately and is not an ADHD treatment result.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Boys with ADHD had higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 than age-matched controls.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum comparison with behavioural and cognitive tests.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years (67 with ADHD, 66 controls).
assessment.result: Homocysteine was higher and vitamin B12 was lower in the ADHD group. Logistic regression treated homocysteine as a prognostic indicator.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The abstract states significant differences and does not report the mean difference or an odds ratio.
assessment.evidence_summary: A serum association between homocysteine, vitamin B12 and ADHD status in boys.
assessment.limitations: Male children only, cross-sectional, no cycle-rate measurement, and no dietary intervention.

evidence_considered.label: Wang et al. (2019)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Children with ADHD had lower folate, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12 and less favourable diets than controls; the analysis links diet to ADHD through a broad nutritional profile.

assessment.study: Case-control food-frequency and fasting biochemistry study with structural equation modelling.
assessment.population: 216 children with ADHD and 216 age-, height- and sex-matched controls from elementary schools in Taiwan.
assessment.result: The ADHD group had lower serum vitamin B12, folate, vitamin B6, ferritin and monounsaturated fatty acids, and higher saturated fatty acids, n-6/n-3 ratio and inorganic phosphorus, with higher intake of nutrient-poor foods.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Group differences are described as significant. The abstract does not report mean concentrations or a single nutrient effect size.
assessment.evidence_summary: Dietary pattern and several biochemical markers differ together in childhood ADHD.
assessment.limitations: Observational, multi-nutrient, and not a measurement of methionine-cycle rates. The path model does not isolate cycle throughput.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Folate and betaine routes return methionine to the integrated cycle
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Folate-dependent remethylation and the mainly hepatic/renal BHMT route return methionine to the integrated cycle; choline can supply betaine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: These are evidenced methionine-return routes within this PM’s integrated cycle. Their existence does not establish that donor availability limits integrated branch rates or that greater intake improves cycle balance.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Folate-dependent remethylation and the mainly hepatic/renal BHMT route return methionine to the integrated cycle; choline can supply betaine.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Froese and Obeid identify the folate/B12 and betaine routes of methionine regeneration. Human BHMT biochemistry identifies betaine donation, and choline oxidation evidence identifies its precursor route. PM4-F1 independently establishes that regenerated methionine participates in the integrated methionine cycle. These links support donor-fed remethylation within that cycle, not a claim about measured net throughput or remethylation–transsulfuration balance.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Parallel-route compensation, dietary methionine and tissue-specific BHMT expression limit interpretation. Human circulating homocysteine responses are not branch-rate measurements. Donor inadequacy as a limiting determinant of integrated cycle rates remains unresolved.

title: Transsulfuration Pathway
mission: Divert homocysteine toward cysteine so methylation demand is balanced against sulfur amino-acid and redox needs.
summary: Cystathionine beta-synthase joins homocysteine and serine to form cystathionine. Cystathionine gamma-lyase then cleaves cystathionine and releases cysteine. Both enzymes require pyridoxal 5′-phosphate, the active cofactor made from vitamin B6. This irreversible branch disposes of homocysteine and produces cysteine. Studies of the purified enzymes establish these reactions and the cofactor requirement.
dose_sensitivity: Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor) is required by both enzymes. No human dose-response showing that vitamin B6 intake controls transsulfuration flux was established.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Homocysteine can be joined to serine and then cleaved to cysteine, but that chemistry is not evidence of a stress-reactivity effect. A study of boys with ADHD found higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12. It did not measure these enzymes, cysteine production, or stress outcomes, and it is not a treatment result {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.

Cysteine released by cystathionine cleavage can be used later for glutathione synthesis, which is a separate mechanism. The enzyme studies do not measure recovery capacity, and they do not show that changing this conversion treats recovery {{cite:zhu_cgl_kinetics_2008,steegborn_cgl_kinetics_1999}}.

scientific_findings_intro: Purified and recombinant human enzyme studies establish the two transsulfuration reaction boundaries and their PLP dependence: CBS forms cystathionine, and CGL uses it to release cysteine. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[4]](#pm-ref-4) [[3]](#pm-ref-3) The findings converge on biochemical pathway identity, including cysteine’s position as a product of the second step. They do not measure whole-body dietary responsiveness or glutathione synthesis, so neither increased flux from extra vitamin B6 nor downstream benefit is established by these assays. Human tracer evidence adds a physiological boundary: moderate vitamin B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling without significantly changing total transsulfuration. [[7]](#pm-ref-7)

scientific_findings.finding_label: CBS joins homocysteine and serine
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human cystathionine beta-synthase uses pyridoxal 5'-phosphate to join L-homocysteine and L-serine, forming L-cystathionine. Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is the active form of vitamin B6 recycled from food.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Homocysteine and serine are both substrates. The cofactor requirement does not show that eating more vitamin B6 increases cystathionine formation in people.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human cystathionine beta-synthase catalyses a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent condensation of L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine, and pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is the active vitamin B6 cofactor recycled from food.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Purified human enzyme kinetics and a crystal structure agree that cystathionine beta-synthase condenses L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine and that the reaction depends on pyridoxal 5'-phosphate. A cofactor review identifies that same molecule as the active form of vitamin B6, recycled from food by the salvage pathway. Together these sources define the first reaction and its cofactor. They do not measure whole-body transsulfuration flux or an intake response.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The kinetic and structural evidence uses recombinant or crystallised human enzyme, not intact human physiology. The salvage review does not assay cystathionine beta-synthase. Substrate inhibition constants and cofactor identity do not show that ordinary vitamin B6 intake sets the reaction rate.

evidence_considered.label: Belew et al. (2009)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: isolated-substance
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Purified human cystathionine beta-synthase catalysed the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent condensation of L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine, with substrate inhibition by L-homocysteine.

assessment.study: Steady-state kinetics of recombinant human cystathionine beta-synthase purified from E. coli, using a continuous coupled assay for cystathionine formation.
assessment.population: Purified recombinant human enzyme; no cells, animals, or human participants.
assessment.result: The enzyme condensed L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine. L-Homocysteine inhibited the enzyme at higher concentrations. The reverse hydrolysis of cystathionine was slower than the condensation on a specificity basis.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reported Ki for L-homocysteine was 2.1 ± 0.2 mM. The abstract states that kcat/Km for cystathionine hydrolysis was approximately 2-fold lower than kcat/Km for L-serine in the condensation.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human-enzyme evidence that both serine and homocysteine are substrates and that pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is required.
assessment.limitations: In-vitro kinetics do not establish in-vivo flux, dietary responsiveness, or a phenome outcome.

evidence_considered.label: Meier et al. (2001)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: isolated-substance
evidence_considered.directional_finding: The crystal structure of truncated human cystathionine beta-synthase describes a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent condensation of serine and homocysteine to cystathionine.

assessment.study: X-ray crystal structure of a truncated form of human cystathionine beta-synthase.
assessment.population: Crystallised human enzyme; no cells, animals, or human participants.
assessment.result: The structure shows a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent heme protein that catalyses condensation of serine and homocysteine to cystathionine.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No physiological effect size applies to this structure.
assessment.evidence_summary: Independent structural support for the same reaction and for pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence.
assessment.limitations: A static structure of a truncated enzyme does not measure flux, nutrient limitation, or dietary dose response.

evidence_considered.label: di Salvo et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: review
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is the active form of vitamin B6 and is recycled from food by the salvage pathway.

assessment.study: Narrative review of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate availability, salvage enzymes, and consequences of inadequate intracellular cofactor.
assessment.population: No new human cohort; review of human biochemistry and clinical cofactor disorders.
assessment.result: In humans, pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is recycled from food and from degraded enzymes by pyridoxal kinase, pyridoxine 5'-phosphate oxidase, and phosphatases.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No transsulfuration rate or vitamin B6 intake-response figure is reported.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports the identity of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate as the vitamin B6 cofactor supplied from food. It does not assay this pathway.
assessment.limitations: A salvage review cannot show that vitamin B6 intake changes cystathionine beta-synthase flux.

evidence_dependency: di Salvo et al. (2012) is also used in PM5-IC1 to bound intake claims. It is not a second measurement of the condensation reaction.

scientific_findings.finding_label: CGL cleaves cystathionine and releases cysteine
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human cystathionine gamma-lyase is a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent enzyme that cleaves L-cystathionine in the transsulfuration step that produces cysteine. Cysteine is the product of this step. Glutathione synthesis is a later pathway.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Cystathionine is the substrate and cysteine is the product. Cysteine is not a substrate of this conversion, and glutathione synthesis is not this reaction.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human cystathionine gamma-lyase requires pyridoxal 5'-phosphate and cleaves L-cystathionine in the transsulfuration step that produces cysteine.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Kinetic work on recombinant human cystathionine gamma-lyase shows gamma-lyase activity toward L-cystathionine and only marginal reactivity toward L-cysteine. A separate human-enzyme study identifies the enzyme as pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent and places it in the transsulfuration route that converts homocysteine to cysteine, with cystathionine as the assayed substrate. Cysteine is therefore the pathway product of this step, not its substrate. Neither study measures glutathione synthesis.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Both studies use recombinant human enzyme. The 2008 paper's numeric comparisons concern disease-associated mutants and a common polymorphism, not dietary intake. The abstracts establish cystathionine cleavage and the homocysteine-to-cysteine role; they were not used as a product-table for every coproduct. Glutathione synthesis remains outside this finding.

evidence_considered.label: Steegborn et al. (1999)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: isolated-substance
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Recombinant human cystathionine gamma-lyase showed high gamma-lyase activity toward L-cystathionine and only marginal reactivity toward L-cysteine.

assessment.study: Cloning of human cystathionine gamma-lyase from Hep G2 RNA, bacterial expression, and steady-state kinetics with L-cystathionine.
assessment.population: Purified recombinant human enzyme; no human participants.
assessment.result: The enzyme preferred L-cystathionine as a gamma-lyase substrate. Reactivity toward L-cysteine and L-cystine was marginal, and cystathionine beta-lyase activity was not detected.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reported Km for L-cystathionine was 0.5 mM and Vmax was 2.5 units/mg, with an optimum pH of 8.2.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct kinetic evidence that L-cystathionine is the substrate and that L-cysteine is a poor substrate of this enzyme.
assessment.limitations: In-vitro kinetics do not establish in-vivo flux or a dietary response. The abstract does not tabulate every coproduct.

evidence_considered.label: Zhu et al. (2008)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: isolated-substance
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human cystathionine gamma-lyase is pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent, functions in the transsulfuration pathway that converts homocysteine to cysteine, and was assayed with cystathionine.

assessment.study: Kinetic and spectrophotometric comparison of wild-type human cystathionine gamma-lyase with pathogenic mutants and a common polymorphism.
assessment.population: Recombinant human enzyme variants; no human participants in the kinetic assays.
assessment.result: The polymorphism did not change cofactor content or the tested steady-state parameters. Pathogenic mutants had lower Vmax, lower pyridoxal 5'-phosphate content, and cystathionine Km values comparable to wild type.
assessment.effect_magnitude: T67I Vmax was about 3.5-fold lower and Q240E Vmax about 70-fold lower than wild type. Mutant pyridoxal 5'-phosphate content was about 4-fold and 80-fold lower. Wild-type Km was not stated in the abstract.
assessment.evidence_summary: Confirms pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence and cystathionine as the substrate in the homocysteine-to-cysteine pathway.
assessment.limitations: Mutant fold-changes describe rare enzyme defects, not ordinary diet. The study does not measure glutathione synthesis or recovery.

evidence_dependency: Zhu et al. (2008) and Steegborn et al. (1999) are also cited by PM5-F4. That reuse is the same reaction evidence, not a recovery measurement.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Cofactor dependence is not an intake or flux result
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Showing that the enzymes need pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, or that food vitamin B6 can be salvaged to that cofactor, does not measure pathway flux and does not show that vitamin B6 intake controls cysteine formation.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Circulating markers and cofactor biochemistry answer different questions. Neither is a licence to treat vitamin B6 intake as a proven controller of this conversion.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence and vitamin B6 salvage do not measure cystathionine beta-synthase or cystathionine gamma-lyase flux and do not prove that vitamin B6 intake controls transsulfuration.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The enzyme studies establish a cofactor requirement under biochemical conditions. The salvage review establishes that food vitamin B6 is recycled to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate. None of these sources reports a human tracer measurement of transsulfuration flux before and after a change in vitamin B6 intake. A cofactor requirement and a salvage route therefore cannot be read as proof that intake controls flux.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is a boundary on the evidence in hand. It does not claim that a future intake study would be negative. The repository record previously used for a population association does not resolve to that study and is not part of this synthesis.

evidence_considered.label: di Salvo et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: review
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Food vitamin B6 is salvaged to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate; the review does not measure transsulfuration flux.

evidence_considered.label: Belew et al. (2009)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: isolated-substance
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human cystathionine beta-synthase kinetics show pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence in purified enzyme, not a vitamin B6 intake effect.

evidence_dependency: Belew et al. (2009) and di Salvo et al. (2012) are also primary evidence in PM5-F1. Here they constrain interpretation; they are not independent replications of an intake trial.

scientific_findings.finding_label: ADHD homocysteine markers do not test this pathway or stress treatment
scientific_findings.finding_summary: A paediatric study found higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 in boys with ADHD than in controls. It did not measure transsulfuration enzymes, cysteine production, stress reactivity, or a treatment effect.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Homocysteine concentration in that cohort must not be read as evidence that this conversion modulates stress reactivity or treats ADHD or stress.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The assessed paediatric ADHD biomarker study does not show that transsulfuration modulates stress reactivity or that it treats stress or ADHD.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The study compared serum homocysteine, vitamin B12, vitamin D, ferritin, and iron in boys with ADHD and age-matched controls. Homocysteine was higher and vitamin B12 was lower in the ADHD group, and the authors treated homocysteine as a possible prognostic marker. The measurements are circulating biomarkers. They do not include cystathionine beta-synthase, cystathionine gamma-lyase, cystathionine, cysteine, pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, stress-reactivity scores, or an intervention.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is a gap for the phenome relationship, not proof that no relationship exists. The cohort is boys only, the design is cross-sectional, and diagnosis-marker associations are not pathway flux.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: observational-biomarker
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Boys with ADHD had higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 than controls. Transsulfuration enzymes, cysteine production, and stress outcomes were not measured.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum biomarker comparison using spectrophotometry and immunoassays, with behavioural and cognitive assessments.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years; 67 with DSM-V ADHD and 66 age-matched controls.
assessment.result: Homocysteine was higher and vitamin B12 was lower in the ADHD group. Logistic regression treated homocysteine as a potential prognostic indicator. Vitamin D, ferritin, and iron were also measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The abstract reports significant group differences and does not provide the mean concentrations used here.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human observational evidence about serum homocysteine and vitamin B12 in paediatric ADHD, not about this enzyme pathway.
assessment.limitations: Boys only; no enzyme activity, flux, cysteine, stress-reactivity, or treatment endpoint.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Cysteine release is not a recovery measurement
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The pathway releases cysteine. Later glutathione synthesis can use that cysteine, but the assessed enzyme evidence does not measure recovery capacity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: An indirect biological bridge to recovery is not a recovery outcome and is not a treatment claim.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Cysteine produced by cystathionine cleavage can supply later glutathione synthesis, but the assessed evidence does not measure recovery capacity.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Human cystathionine gamma-lyase studies establish cleavage of cystathionine in the step that produces cysteine. Glutathione synthesis is a downstream use of cysteine and is outside this mechanism. Neither enzyme paper measures recovery, stress, or a clinical outcome. The recovery relationship therefore stays an indirect framework bridge.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The finding bounds the enzyme corpus. It does not review glutathione trials, and those trials would belong to glutathione synthesis rather than to this conversion.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Moderate B6 restriction changes cystathionine handling without lowering total transsulfuration
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human methionine tracers measured the methionine-cycle contribution to transsulfuration; moderate vitamin B6 restriction altered cystathionine handling while total transsulfuration was maintained.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Nine healthy young adults after 28 days of moderate vitamin B6 restriction; whole-body postprandial tracer kinetics, not tissue-specific flux or clinical outcomes. Total transsulfuration was maintained despite altered cystathionine handling. This does not establish increased flux or benefit from additional intake.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Moderate vitamin B6 restriction changed cystathionine kinetics without a significant change in total transsulfuration in this small controlled human study.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Lamers and colleagues used labelled methionine to assess whole-body pathway kinetics before and after controlled vitamin B6 restriction. The study supports methionine-cycle supply into the transsulfuration branch and a context-specific B6 response; it does not establish that moderate deficiency lowers net pathway flux.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Nine healthy young adults after 28 days of moderate vitamin B6 restriction; whole-body postprandial tracer kinetics, not tissue-specific flux or clinical outcomes. evidence_considered.directional_finding: Cystathionine concentration and fractional synthesis increased; total transsulfuration did not significantly change.

assessment.study: Within-person controlled vitamin B6 restriction with stable-isotope methionine and leucine infusions.
assessment.population: Nine healthy young adults (four men, five women), 20–35 years.
assessment.result: After 28 days of restriction, cystathionine handling changed while total postprandial transsulfuration, remethylation and transmethylation were maintained.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No significant group change in total transsulfuration; small study does not establish equivalence.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human kinetic evidence for a bounded response and for methionine-cycle sulfur supply into transsulfuration.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Combined donor deprivation reduces measured hepatic CBS capacity
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Combined folate/choline deprivation reduced measured hepatic CBS catalytic activity in rats; donor-resource context can therefore constrain this step under that defined deprivation condition. SAM-responsive CBS regulation is a supported connection, not a measured mediator of the dietary effect.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Combined folate/choline deprivation reduced measured hepatic CBS catalytic activity in rats; donor-resource context can therefore constrain this step under that defined deprivation condition. SAM-responsive CBS regulation is a supported connection, not a measured mediator of the dietary effect.

title: Glutathione Synthesis
mission: Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.
summary: Cells assemble glutathione, the main intracellular thiol, in two ATP-dependent steps. Glutamate–cysteine ligase joins glutamate and cysteine, then glutathione synthetase adds glycine. A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet slowed whole-blood synthesis in healthy young men. Combined precursor supplements raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults. These tracer studies measured synthesis in blood cells, not in the brain.
key_constraints: BRS2(KC2) - Methionine–Cysteine Sulfur Amino Acid Pool

pm_kc_relationships.dietary_input_note: Pool/constraint dependency, not another dietary constituent. Dietary supply decisions belong to its separately admitted PM input atoms.
pm_kc_relationships.pm_biological_role: Removing methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis, and removing cysteine alone did not when methionine stayed adequate. That is the sulfur-amino-acid provision relationship already recorded for cysteine and methionine.
pm_kc_relationships.evidence_limitation: Lyons used a 10-day amino-acid formula that removed both methionine and cysteine in healthy young men, and whole-blood glutathione concentration was maintained. Courtney-Martin kept methionine adequate and found that removing cysteine did not lower erythrocyte synthesis in young men. Neither study identifies a bottleneck beyond those provision relationships. This is not neuronal synthesis, ordinary mixed-diet advice, or a benefit from increasing an adequate intake.

presentation_review.rationale: Sulfur-amino-acid provision sustaining glutathione synthesis is cysteine as the direct assembly substrate and methionine as its precursor. A resource-dependency label and a KC2 origin tag do not create a further biological job. Lyons supplies the combined-depletion bound and Courtney-Martin the adequate-methionine bound. No additional competition, allocation, or other bottleneck was measured.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methionine and cysteine pool constrains glutathione synthesis capacity.
established_links: Glutamate-cysteine ligase uses cysteine and ATP to form γ-glutamylcysteine (PM6-F1).
A diet containing neither methionine nor cysteine slowed whole-blood glutathione fractional and absolute synthesis in healthy young men, while glycine intake was not reduced (PM6-F2).
With methionine held at an adequate intake, cysteine intakes from zero upward did not change erythrocyte glutathione synthesis in young men (PM6-F2).
inferred_links: Ordinary mixed diets are commonly short of this pool.
The same synthesis-rate change occurs in neurons or in clinical populations.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: KC2 applicability stays established because these sulfur-amino-acid studies bear on glutathione synthesis. The public disclosure is consolidated as a duplicate of PM6-DIT-1 and PM6-DIT-9. Lyons is combined depletion. Courtney-Martin is the adequate-methionine boundary. Neither study measures a competition, allocation, or other bottleneck beyond that provision.

dose_sensitivity: Cysteine, glutamate and glycine are assembly substrates. Combined precursor supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults only; that is not general dietary advice. Selenium and riboflavin are not synthesis requirements.

dietary_input_assessments.operation: Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.

functional_dependency.statement: Magnesium supplies the catalytic metal used in ATP-dependent human glutathione-synthetase capacity.

dietary_supply.statement: The same mineral has established dietary supply through the canonical composition records. Cellular uptake and homeostasis mediate enzyme loading; this is maintenance of capacity, not a claim that extra intake accelerates the reaction.

dietary_input_assessments.assessment_limitations: Human GSS crystallography and cofactor annotation support capacity. The structure contains two magnesium ions; this does not establish a dietary dose, increased blood or neuronal glutathione synthesis, or benefit above adequacy. Original one-per-subunit wording is retained in history rather than used as dietary stoichiometry.

Verified plant/animal sources are reused with preparation qualifiers; no new food edge, effective food dose or enzyme-response inference is created.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Glutathione assembly supplies a thiol used in cellular redox buffering, which is relevant to recovery only as downstream biology. The human synthesis measurements are erythrocyte kinetics after combined precursor supplementation in older adults, not a recovery-outcome trial {{cite:sekhar_glutathione_2011}}. A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet slowed whole-blood synthesis while concentration was maintained {{cite:lyons_glutathione_2000}}. Higher homocysteine in boys with ADHD does not measure glutathione synthesis or recovery {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.

The same thiol pool is a plausible contributor to stress buffering, but no assessed study tested a stress-resilience outcome {{cite:sekhar_glutathione_2011,lyons_glutathione_2000}}. The paediatric ADHD biomarker study measured homocysteine and vitamin B12, not glutathione synthesis or stress resilience {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.
