scientific_findings_intro: Human tracer studies show context-dependent substrate responsiveness. Removing methionine and cysteine together reduced whole-blood glutathione synthesis, whereas removing cysteine with methionine kept adequate did not reduce erythrocyte synthesis in young men. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[5]](#pm-ref-5) In older adults with lower baseline synthesis, combined N-acetylcysteine and glycine supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) These contrasts support provision under defined conditions, not universal dietary cysteine limitation; blood-cell measurements do not establish neuronal synthesis or clinical benefit.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Two ATP-dependent enzymes assemble glutathione
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Glutamate-cysteine ligase joins glutamate and cysteine using ATP. Glutathione synthetase then adds glycine, again using ATP, and binds magnesium. Selenium-dependent peroxidase activity and riboflavin-derived FAD in glutathione reductase are not part of these assembly reactions.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Glutamate, cysteine, glycine and ATP are the assembly substrates. Magnesium participates in the second enzyme. ATP and magnesium are intracellular biochemical requirements, not dietary levers. Selenium and riboflavin support later use and recycling of glutathione.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Glutathione synthesis requires ATP-dependent formation of γ-glutamylcysteine from glutamate and cysteine, followed by ATP-dependent addition of glycine, and does not use selenium or riboflavin as synthesis substrates.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Reviewed catalytic annotation of purified human glutamate-cysteine ligase records ATP-dependent ligation of L-glutamate and L-cysteine as the first step. Human glutathione synthetase structural work records ATP-dependent addition of glycine and one bound magnesium ion per subunit as the second step. Together they define the assembly boundary. Human glutathione peroxidase uses an active-site selenocysteine to reduce peroxides with glutathione already formed, and glutathione reductase binds FAD while reducing glutathione disulfide. Those enzymes consume or restore glutathione; they do not assemble it.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The enzyme evidence is purified protein and structure, not intact human flux. A lower cysteine Km on the first enzyme does not prove that ordinary diets are cysteine-limited. Magnesium binding does not show that magnesium intake changes synthesis. The dietary review that groups selenium and riboflavin with glutathione support does not move those cofactors into the assembly reactions.

evidence_considered.label: Misra and Griffith (1998)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Purified human glutamate-cysteine ligase catalyses ATP-dependent ligation of L-glutamate and L-cysteine, the first step of glutathione biosynthesis.

assessment.study: Expression and purification of human gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase, with catalytic constants recorded in the reviewed human GCLC entry that cites this paper.
assessment.population: Purified human enzyme; no human participants.
assessment.result: The reaction consumes L-glutamate, L-cysteine and ATP to form γ-glutamylcysteine, ADP and phosphate. The cited annotation reports Km values of 0.1 mM for L-cysteine, 1.8 mM for L-glutamate and 0.4 mM for ATP.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Purified-enzyme Km values only; no human synthesis-rate effect.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human-enzyme evidence for the first ATP-dependent assembly step and its amino-acid and ATP substrates.
assessment.limitations: In-vitro constants do not establish in-vivo limitation, dietary responsiveness, tissue differences or clinical effects.

evidence_considered.label: Polekhina et al. (1999)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human glutathione synthetase produces glutathione from γ-glutamylcysteine and glycine in an ATP-dependent reaction and binds one magnesium ion per subunit.

assessment.study: Crystal structure of human glutathione synthetase at 2.10 Å in complex with ADP and glutathione, with catalytic and cofactor annotation.
assessment.population: Crystallised human glutathione synthetase; no human participants.
assessment.result: The structure and catalytic annotation place glycine and ATP in the second assembly step and record one Mg2+ ion bound per subunit.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 2.10 Å structure; no physiological effect size.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct structural evidence for the second ATP-dependent step and its magnesium ion.
assessment.limitations: A product-bound structure establishes catalytic participants, not dietary dose response or in-vivo flux.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Minich et al. (2019)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews dietary nutrients discussed for glutathione support, including sulfur amino acids, selenium and riboflavin.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: It is a narrative review and does not itself measure the ligase reactions, ATP use, or separation of assembly from peroxidase and reductase cofactors.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Mullenbach et al. (1987)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Shows that human glutathione peroxidase encodes an active-site selenocysteine, so selenium belongs to peroxide removal that uses glutathione.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Peroxidase activity consumes glutathione. It is not a substrate or cofactor of either assembly enzyme.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Karplus and Schulz (1989)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Glutathione reductase structures show bound FAD, the riboflavin-derived cofactor, at the enzyme that reduces glutathione disulfide.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Disulfide reduction is recycling of glutathione already made. FAD is not a substrate of glutamate-cysteine ligase or glutathione synthetase.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Blood-cell synthesis responds only under defined substrate conditions
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Removing both methionine and cysteine slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis in healthy young men. Combined cysteine-precursor and glycine supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults. A methionine-adequate diet without cysteine did not lower erythrocyte synthesis in young men.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Substrate supply can change blood-cell synthesis in these specific conditions. That does not mean every ordinary diet is cysteine-limited, and the older-adult result is a supplemental precursor plus glycine, not a food prescription.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human blood-cell glutathione synthesis can slow when dietary methionine and cysteine are both removed and can rise in older adults after combined cysteine and glycine precursor supplementation, whereas a methionine-adequate cysteine-free diet did not limit erythrocyte synthesis in young men.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Three human tracer studies set the ceiling. In seven healthy young men, a 10-day amino-acid diet with methionine and cysteine removed lowered whole-blood fractional synthesis from 0.65 ± 0.13 to 0.49 ± 0.13 per day and lowered absolute synthesis by about 23%, while concentration stayed near 1.2 mM and glycine intake was not reduced. In eight older adults compared with eight younger adults, erythrocyte glutathione synthesis and concentration were lower, and two weeks of cysteine plus glycine precursor supplementation raised fractional synthesis by 78.8% and absolute synthesis by 230.9%. The cysteine source in that protocol is N-acetylcysteine, given with glycine. In four young men, cysteine intakes from zero to 40 mg/kg/day did not change erythrocyte synthesis when methionine was held at 14 mg/kg/day. Synthesis is therefore substrate-responsive under defined restrictions, not universally limited by dietary cysteine.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: All three studies measured blood-cell, not neuronal, synthesis. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial, and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

evidence_considered.label: Lyons et al. (2000)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: A sulfur-amino-acid-free amino-acid diet slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis in healthy young men without lowering glutathione concentration.

assessment.study: Randomised crossover of two 10-day L-amino-acid diets, adequate versus methionine and cysteine both set to zero, with a primed intravenous L-[1-13C]cysteine infusion on day 10.
assessment.population: Seven healthy men, age 24 ± 6 years.
assessment.result: Fractional synthesis fell from 0.65 ± 0.13 to 0.49 ± 0.13 per day (P < 0.01). Absolute synthesis fell from 747 ± 216 to 578.6 ± 135 µmol/L/day (P < 0.05), about 23%. Whole-blood glutathione stayed about 1.2 mM (1,142 ± 243 versus 1,216 ± 162 µM). Glycine in the formula rose from 39.6 to 75.1 mg/kg/day so nitrogen stayed constant; glutamic acid was unchanged.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About a 23% lower absolute synthesis rate after 10 days without methionine and cysteine; concentration unchanged.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human evidence that removing the shared sulfur-amino-acid supply slows whole-blood glutathione synthesis.
assessment.limitations: Experimental formula, young men, short duration, whole blood rather than brain, and no clinical outcome. Glycine was increased, so the slowdown is not a glycine deficit.

evidence_considered.label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Older adults had lower erythrocyte glutathione synthesis than younger adults, and two weeks of cysteine plus glycine precursor supplementation restored synthesis and concentration.

assessment.study: Stable-isotope erythrocyte glutathione kinetics before and after precursor supplementation. Cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine.
assessment.population: Eight older adults restudied after supplementation, compared with eight younger adults.
assessment.result: Before supplementation, older adults had lower erythrocyte glycine, cysteine, glutathione concentration, fractional synthesis (45.80 ± 5.69 versus 83.14 ± 6.43 %/day) and absolute synthesis (0.55 ± 0.12 versus 1.73 ± 0.16 mmol/L red cells per day). After two weeks, glutathione concentration was 94.6% higher, fractional synthesis 78.8% higher and absolute synthesis 230.9% higher, and plasma oxidative-stress markers were lower.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Combined precursor supplementation in older adults: fractional synthesis +78.8% and absolute synthesis +230.9% from the deficient baseline.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human evidence that combined supplemental cysteine precursor and glycine can raise erythrocyte glutathione synthesis when it is low in older adults.
assessment.limitations: Small older-adult sample, erythrocyte pool, combined supplements, not ordinary food, not neuronal synthesis, and not an ADHD or recovery trial.

evidence_considered.label: Courtney-Martin et al. (2008)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Erythrocyte glutathione synthesis did not change across cysteine intakes, including zero, when methionine intake was adequate.

assessment.study: Five graded cysteine intakes (0, 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg/kg/day) in random order with methionine fixed at 14 mg/kg/day and protein at 1 g/kg/day. Erythrocyte glutathione synthesis was measured after two days at each intake.
assessment.population: Four healthy young adult men.
assessment.result: Fractional and absolute erythrocyte glutathione synthesis and glutathione concentration did not change as cysteine intake increased. Urinary sulfate excretion rose with cysteine intake (r = 0.92).
assessment.effect_magnitude: No change in erythrocyte glutathione synthesis across the cysteine range tested.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human evidence that dietary cysteine is not independently limiting for erythrocyte glutathione synthesis when methionine intake meets the protein requirement.
assessment.limitations: Preliminary sample of four men, two-day adaptation, erythrocyte endpoint, and no neuronal or clinical outcome.

evidence_dependency: Sekhar et al. (2011) is also used in PM6-F3 and PM6-F4 for the phenome boundary, and in PM6-IC1 for the measurement boundary. Those uses are not independent replications of the synthesis-rate result.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Blood-cell glutathione kinetics are not neuronal synthesis or clinical outcome
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Erythrocyte and whole-blood glutathione synthesis rates and concentrations do not measure neuronal glutathione synthesis, do not establish that every person is substrate-limited, and are not ADHD, recovery or stress-resilience outcomes.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The human tracer studies measure incorporation of labelled cysteine or glycine into glutathione in whole blood or red cells. In the sulfur-amino-acid-free diet, synthesis slowed while concentration was maintained, so concentration is not a substitute for synthesis rate. None of the studies sampled brain glutathione synthesis or tested a recovery, stress or ADHD outcome. A paediatric ADHD study that found higher homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 did not measure glutathione.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This constraint limits interpretation. It does not prove that neuronal synthesis is unrelated to substrate supply, and it does not reclassify the blood-cell synthesis results themselves.

evidence_considered.label: Lyons et al. (2000)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Whole-blood synthesis rate changed while glutathione concentration did not, and the measurement was not a brain or clinical endpoint.

assessment.study: Sulfur-amino-acid-free versus adequate amino-acid diets with whole-blood glutathione kinetics.
assessment.population: Seven healthy young men.
assessment.result: Synthesis slowed and concentration was maintained. No neuronal or symptom endpoint was measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Concentration unchanged despite about a 23% lower absolute synthesis rate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows that blood glutathione concentration and blood synthesis rate are different measurements.
assessment.limitations: Does not describe neuronal glutathione.

evidence_considered.label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Erythrocyte synthesis and oxidative-stress markers changed in older adults; the study did not measure brain synthesis or an ADHD outcome.

assessment.study: Erythrocyte glutathione kinetics and plasma oxidative-stress markers before and after precursor supplementation.
assessment.population: Eight older adults and eight younger adults.
assessment.result: Erythrocyte synthesis and concentration rose in the older group after supplementation. No ADHD, recovery or stress-resilience outcome was tested.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Erythrocyte fractional synthesis +78.8% in the supplemented older group.
assessment.evidence_summary: The supported endpoint is older-adult erythrocyte synthesis, not a universal or clinical claim.
assessment.limitations: Blood-cell kinetics in a small older-adult sample.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Boys with ADHD had higher homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 than controls; glutathione was not measured.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum biomarkers and behavioural scores in boys with and without ADHD.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years, 67 with ADHD and 66 controls.
assessment.result: Homocysteine was higher and vitamin B12 lower in the ADHD group. Glutathione synthesis was not an endpoint.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No glutathione concentration or synthesis rate was reported.
assessment.evidence_summary: An ADHD biomarker association that does not measure this synthesis reaction.
assessment.limitations: Cross-sectional, boys only, no glutathione assay, and no dietary intervention.

evidence_dependency: Lyons et al. (2000) and Sekhar et al. (2011) are primary synthesis evidence in PM6-F2. PM6-IC1 uses them only to bound what those measurements can mean.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Recovery-capacity benefit is not established
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Glutathione assembly is biologically relevant to redox buffering, but the assessed studies do not show that changing synthesis improves Recovery Capacity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Older-adult erythrocyte synthesis and a paediatric homocysteine difference must not be read as recovery treatment evidence.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The assessed human evidence does not demonstrate that glutathione synthesis capacity changes Recovery Capacity as a functional or clinical outcome.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The older-adult trial changed erythrocyte glutathione synthesis and plasma oxidative-stress markers after combined precursor supplementation. It did not measure recovery capacity. The paediatric ADHD study measured homocysteine and vitamin B12, not glutathione synthesis and not recovery. The relationship remains a mechanistic possibility with a direct-evidence gap.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is a gap in the assessed evidence, not proof that no relationship exists. Oxidative-stress markers are not a recovery phenome.

evidence_considered.label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Precursor supplementation raised erythrocyte glutathione synthesis in older adults and lowered oxidative-stress markers, without a recovery outcome.

assessment.study: Erythrocyte glutathione kinetics and plasma oxidative-stress markers.
assessment.population: Eight older adults and eight younger adults.
assessment.result: Synthesis and glutathione concentration rose in the older group. Recovery capacity was not measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No recovery-outcome effect size exists in the study.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports a synthesis change, not a recovery-capacity benefit.
assessment.limitations: Wrong endpoint for this phenome relationship.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: ADHD was associated with higher homocysteine and lower vitamin B12, not with a glutathione or recovery measurement.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum biomarker comparison in boys with and without ADHD.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years.
assessment.result: Homocysteine and vitamin B12 differed by ADHD status. Glutathione and recovery were not measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No glutathione or recovery effect.
assessment.evidence_summary: Does not test this phenome relationship.
assessment.limitations: Cross-sectional biomarker study in boys.

evidence_dependency: Sekhar et al. (2011) is primary synthesis evidence in PM6-F2. Its use here is only to show that the trial did not measure Recovery Capacity.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Stress-resilience benefit is not established
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Substrate-responsive glutathione synthesis is relevant to redox buffering, but none of the assessed studies tested Stress Resilience.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Do not convert blood-cell synthesis changes or an ADHD homocysteine difference into a stress-resilience treatment claim.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The assessed human evidence does not demonstrate that glutathione synthesis capacity changes Stress Resilience.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Sulfur-amino-acid removal and older-adult precursor supplementation changed blood-cell glutathione synthesis. Neither study measured stress resilience. The paediatric ADHD biomarker study did not measure glutathione or stress resilience. The phenome link stays mechanistic and untested.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Absence of a direct test is not evidence against a biological contribution. It does block treatment and dietary-advice claims.

evidence_considered.label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Older-adult erythrocyte glutathione synthesis rose after precursor supplementation, with no stress-resilience endpoint.

assessment.study: Erythrocyte glutathione kinetics and plasma oxidative-stress markers.
assessment.population: Eight older adults and eight younger adults.
assessment.result: Erythrocyte synthesis changed. Stress resilience was not measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No stress-resilience effect size.
assessment.evidence_summary: Synthesis evidence without a stress-resilience outcome.
assessment.limitations: Endpoint mismatch for this phenome.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: The ADHD cohort difference was in homocysteine and vitamin B12, not glutathione synthesis or stress resilience.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum biomarkers in boys with and without ADHD.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years.
assessment.result: Homocysteine and vitamin B12 differed. Stress resilience and glutathione were not endpoints.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No stress-resilience or glutathione effect.
assessment.evidence_summary: Does not test the phenome relationship.
assessment.limitations: Cross-sectional paediatric biomarker study.

evidence_dependency: Sekhar et al. (2011) is primary synthesis evidence in PM6-F2 and is reused here only for the missing stress-resilience endpoint. Lukovac et al. (2024) is also primary evidence in PM6-F3 and PM6-IC1.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Plasma glutamine/glutamate increases do not establish glutathione synthesis
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Oral glutamine raised plasma glutamine/glutamate but did not raise whole-blood glutathione.
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Oral glutamine raised plasma glutamine/glutamate but did not raise whole-blood glutathione.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Whole-blood glutathione fell; concentrations are not synthesis rates. This does not erase glutamine metabolism, but does not support a universal glutamine-to-GSH enhancement claim.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Oral glutamine raised plasma glutamine/glutamate but did not raise whole-blood glutathione.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Whole-blood glutathione fell; concentrations are not synthesis rates. This does not erase glutamine metabolism, but does not support a universal glutamine-to-GSH enhancement claim.

evidence_considered.label: Valencia et al. (2002)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: 0.3 g/kg/day oral glutamine for ten days.
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Oral glutamine raised plasma glutamine/glutamate but did not raise whole-blood glutathione.

assessment.study: 0.3 g/kg/day oral glutamine for ten days.
assessment.population: Healthy volunteers studied before/after supplementation under a standardised diet.
assessment.result: Oral glutamine raised plasma glutamine/glutamate but did not raise whole-blood glutathione.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Only the specified source-level endpoint is assessed; no pooled effect or food-dose estimate is inferred.
assessment.evidence_summary: Plasma amino-acid and whole-blood glutathione concentrations.
assessment.limitations: Whole-blood glutathione fell; concentrations are not synthesis rates. This does not erase glutamine metabolism, but does not support a universal glutamine-to-GSH enhancement claim.
assessment.retrieval_scope: Primary abstract retrieved via Europe PMC/PubMed; no unextracted full-method claims.

evidence_dependency: The source-specific observations support different links; food composition, biochemical identity, intervention exposure and clinical outcomes are not interchangeable. Reuse across PMs is not independent replication.

decision.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methionine and cysteine pool constrains glutathione synthesis capacity.
established_links: Glutamate-cysteine ligase uses cysteine and ATP to form γ-glutamylcysteine (PM6-F1).
A diet containing neither methionine nor cysteine slowed whole-blood glutathione fractional and absolute synthesis in healthy young men, while glycine intake was not reduced (PM6-F2).
With methionine held at an adequate intake, cysteine intakes from zero upward did not change erythrocyte glutathione synthesis in young men (PM6-F2).
inferred_links: Ordinary mixed diets are commonly short of this pool.
The same synthesis-rate change occurs in neurons or in clinical populations.
decision.rationale: KC2 applicability stays established because these sulfur-amino-acid studies bear on glutathione synthesis. The public disclosure is consolidated as a duplicate of PM6-DIT-1 and PM6-DIT-9. Lyons is combined depletion. Courtney-Martin is the adequate-methionine boundary. Neither study measures a competition, allocation, or other bottleneck beyond that provision.

kc_adjudication_history.rationale: Metadata migration only: preserve the established governs/constrained-by interpretation as a typed Conditional constraint for FM summary derivation. No stronger scientific admission.

title: Phosphatidylcholine Formation
mission: Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.
summary: Cells form phosphatidylcholine through distinct routes: hepatic PEMT methylates phosphatidylethanolamine using SAMe, while the Kennedy pathway combines choline-derived phosphocholine with CTP and then diacylglycerol. Uridine can contribute upstream to nucleotide supply. These routes support membrane phospholipid provision; precursor availability does not establish that extra intake increases human membrane synthesis or improves cognition.

evidence_qualification.label: Diet-Supported
evidence_qualification.rationale: The retained Diet-Supported qualification is supported by conditional PM-specific dietary influence; it does not establish comparative intervention dominance.
evidence_qualification.scope_note: Conditional animal evidence concerns folate restriction and methyl-derived PC enrichment; it does not establish absolute PEMT flux, benefit above adequacy or cognitive benefit.

routes.intervention_effect: Eight-week folate restriction with labelled choline maintained reduced hepatic d3-PC enrichment and the product/precursor enrichment ratio in female mice.
routes.context: Female wild-type and Mthfr-heterozygous mice; the hepatic response was not demonstrated in males.
routes.limitations: Enrichment is not absolute PEMT flux. The restriction experiment does not establish supplementation benefit above adequacy, a human intake target or cognitive benefit.

principal_route_selection.rationale: Dietary Requirements is the principal displayed route because the assessed folate-restriction intervention changed pathway-specific hepatic PC methyl enrichment, a mission-relevant endpoint. The measured conditional effect, rather than nutrient necessity or absence of competing levers, supports prominence. Precursor provision records explain the route but do not independently establish intervention responsiveness.
principal_route_selection.comparative_limitations: Dietary prominence is supported within the studied animal context; it is not a head-to-head ranking against lifestyle or optimisation, a human intake target, or evidence of benefit from extra intake.

assessments.relevance: PM7-F5 measures dietary methyl contribution to hepatic PC formation, directly relevant to the PEMT branch of this PM's mission.
assessments.directness: Chew 2011 experimentally restricted folate for eight weeks with choline maintained; female mice had reduced labelled PC enrichment and a lower product/precursor enrichment ratio. This is dietary manipulation, not an inference from nutrient presence.
assessments.extent: Hepatic d3-PC enrichment was 30% lower (P=0.017), with a lower d3-PC:d9-choline ratio (P=0.049). This supports substantial conditional dietary influence on the measured PEMT-related endpoint, not absolute flux or all PC synthesis. The hepatic response was not demonstrated in males, and no human or cognitive benefit is inferred.

dose_sensitivity: Dietary methyl-donor provision is supported; increasing intake is not established to increase absolute PEMT activity or improve cognition.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methyl-donor pool constrains hepatic PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation.
established_links: KC1 defines folate, choline and betaine as a coherent remethylation donor pool; B12 remains an excluded cofactor.
Folate restriction with choline maintained reduced hepatic methyl-derived PC enrichment in female mice (PM7-F5).
Betaine restored reported PEMT-mediated production under ethanol-induced methylation imbalance (PM7-F5; abstract-level complementary evidence).
inferred_links: Absolute formation rate, universal donor limitation and human or cognitive benefit are not established.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: Type D is met conditionally: named-donor restriction and complementary imbalance rescue connect this pool to pathway-specific formation. Enrichment is not absolute flux; a human or one end-to-end flux assay is not mandatory.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methionine and cysteine pool constrains hepatic PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation.
established_links: Dietary methionine supplies the upstream MAT/SAM route used by PEMT (PM7-F1/F6). This supported chain is not rejected for being upstream.
Shimada 2003 Table 4 separates methionine-associated phospholipid changes from cystine-associated growth rescue with choline held constant; PC:PE and SAM concentrations are not PEMT flux.

Asiriwardhana 2025 Figure 4C measures dietary methionine-dependent methyl incorporation into hepatic PC in neonatal piglets; cysteine was held constant. This closes the concentration-only endpoint gap.

Robinson 2016 primary abstract reports higher hepatic PC synthesis and lower creatine synthesis after donor removal with methionine restricted in both groups. Allocation is context-dependent, not uniform suppression.
Sugiyama 1995 primary abstract reports that eritadenine did not directly inhibit PEMT in the assay; the 1998 inhibitor comparison is not a selective PEMT blockade.
Cano 2011 indexed primary results and prior appraisal support altered PEMT activity after MAT1A deletion. Genetic SAM-production impairment is not dietary sulfur-pool inadequacy.
inferred_links: Whether methionine–cysteine pool availability creates a separately supported allocation, competition or other constraint on PEMT beyond the documented methionine-to-SAM provision job. Cysteine compensation and the relevant context remain unestablished for this proposition.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: Retain the specified conditional-constraint proposition unresolved, while recognising supported upstream methionine provision and measured nutritional effects on methyl incorporation into PC. No human, universal deficiency or absolute-flux gate is imposed. Provision evidence does not by itself establish a distinct shared sulfur-pool bottleneck; donor restriction can redistribute synthesis rather than lower PC synthesis.
kc_applicability_adjudications.evidence_gap: Evidence linking the named methionine–cysteine pool, including cysteine compensation where relevant, to a constraint beyond methionine/SAM provision in a specified context. Sugiyama 1998 full methods and Cano 2011 full assay methods remain inaccessible in this pass; neither access gap is treated as proof of non-applicability.

phenome_relationships.rationale: SAMe-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation couples one-carbon methylation to membrane phospholipid chemistry — the methylation-dependent bridge between B-vitamin status and omega-3-enriched PC delivery toward the brain. VITACOG reanalysis, PEMT pathway biology, and phospholipid-bound DHA accretion evidence support cognitive-clarity framework translation. The findings support an association with cognitive outcomes, while the proposed causal role of methylation–membrane coupling remains unproven. Applicability to ADHD has not yet been established.

Diet and choline reviews discuss attention and neurodevelopment {{cite:millichap_diet_2012}} {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. They do not measure PEMT activity. Piglet brain DHA accretion and human cerebrospinal-fluid DHA likewise do not record this methylation {{cite:liu_higher_2014}} {{cite:arellanes_brain_2020}}. Any attention relationship is a downstream inference.

scientific_findings_intro: Enzyme localisation, mutagenesis and kinetic evidence establishes PEMT-mediated phosphatidylcholine formation and regulation by its substrates and methyl-transfer product. [[7]](#pm-ref-7) [[8]](#pm-ref-8) [[9]](#pm-ref-9) Donor restriction/rescue and upstream perturbation studies support bounded dependence, with experimental contexts limiting extrapolation. [[11]](#pm-ref-11) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) [[15]](#pm-ref-15) Human tracing identifies methyl-derived phosphatidylcholine separately from intact-headgroup incorporation, supporting provision without establishing indispensable dependence, increased absolute hepatic flux or brain benefit. [[10]](#pm-ref-10) Kennedy-pathway studies add a separate nucleotide-provision chain: uridine increased CDP-choline formation in rat slices, and oral UMP increased brain precursor pools in gerbils. [[19]](#pm-ref-19) [[20]](#pm-ref-20) Human MRS provides connected precursor-pool evidence rather than proof of PC synthesis or benefit. [[21]](#pm-ref-21) A longer gerbil study measured PC abundance after dietary UMP, a stronger lipid endpoint than precursor pools, but not a human flux or benefit result. [[22]](#pm-ref-22)

scientific_findings.finding_label: PEMT methylates phosphatidylethanolamine to phosphatidylcholine
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In the liver, phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT) adds three methyl groups from S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe) to phosphatidylethanolamine and releases phosphatidylcholine. Magnesium is not a cofactor of this reaction. The CDP-choline route is a separate way to make phosphatidylcholine.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Phosphatidylethanolamine and SAMe are the substrates of the methylation. Choline feeds the parallel route, and animals that lack PEMT need dietary choline. That does not make choline a substrate of this methylation, and it does not make supplemental SAMe or magnesium a requirement of it.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Hepatic PEMT converts phosphatidylethanolamine to phosphatidylcholine by three sequential SAMe-dependent methyl transfers. The reaction substrates are phosphatidylethanolamine and SAMe. Magnesium is not an established cofactor of this reaction, and the CDP-choline pathway is a parallel route outside it.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Human liver enzyme localisation, SAMe-binding mutagenesis and a physiological review agree on the reaction boundary. PEMT in the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria-associated membranes of liver uses SAMe to methylate phosphatidylethanolamine in three steps, through phosphatidylmonomethylethanolamine and phosphatidyldimethylethanolamine, to phosphatidylcholine. Conserved residues are required for SAMe binding and activity. Mice that lack PEMT tolerate a normal diet, but a choline-deficient diet causes liver failure within days because the CDP-choline route is then unavailable as well. None of these sources names magnesium as a PEMT cofactor.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The enzyme evidence is recombinant protein and a review of knockout mice, not a human dietary flux study. Absence of magnesium from the reaction description rejects the claim that magnesium is a PEMT cofactor; it does not test every buffer condition in the older assay literature. The choline-deficient knockout result shows that choline supports a parallel route. It does not show that choline is a PEMT substrate or that choline intake increases this methylation.

evidence_considered.label: Shields et al. (2003) — topography
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human liver PEMT activity localises to the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria-associated membranes and catalyses three SAMe-dependent methylations of phosphatidylethanolamine.

assessment.study: Endoproteinase-protection mapping of epitope-tagged human PEMT and biochemical localisation in human liver.
assessment.population: Human liver fractions and recombinant protein. No dietary intervention and no human participants in a feeding study.
assessment.result: Methyltransferase activity localised primarily to the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria-associated membranes. The enzyme spans the membrane four times. S-adenosylmethionine is the methyl donor for three sequential methylations.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary dose or in-vivo flux estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct description of the human hepatic reaction, its localisation and its methyl donor.
assessment.limitations: Topography and localisation do not show that ordinary diet changes PEMT rate.

evidence_considered.label: Shields et al. (2003) — SAMe binding
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Conserved residues in human PEMT are required for S-adenosylmethionine binding and for enzyme activity.

assessment.study: Site-directed mutagenesis of predicted S-adenosylmethionine-binding motifs in recombinant human PEMT, with binding measurements.
assessment.population: Recombinant human PEMT. No animals or human participants.
assessment.result: Gly100 and Glu180 were essential for S-adenosylmethionine binding. Conservative changes at Gly98 and Glu181 raised the reported binding parameter relative to unmodified enzyme. The abstract describes three sequential methylations of phosphatidylethanolamine and names S-adenosylhomocysteine as a product.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The paper reports the binding comparison as 303.1 pmol for unmodified enzyme, 400 pmol after the Gly98 change and 666.7 pmol after the Glu181 change. These are not dietary doses.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct evidence that SAMe binding is required for human PEMT activity.
assessment.limitations: A recombinant binding study does not show that supplemental SAMe increases hepatic phosphatidylcholine formation in people.

evidence_considered.label: Vance (2014)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: PEMT methylates phosphatidylethanolamine using AdoMet. Supply of AdoMet, phosphatidylethanolamine and the product AdoHcy can regulate activity. Loss of PEMT plus a choline-deficient diet causes rapid liver failure in mice.

assessment.study: Narrative review of PEMT localisation, regulation and knockout-mouse physiology.
assessment.population: Review, including Pemt knockout mice fed chow or a choline-deficient diet. Not a human enzyme-rate trial.
assessment.result: PEMT is a liver endoplasmic-reticulum and mitochondria-associated-membrane enzyme. Substrate supply and product AdoHcy can regulate it. Knockout mice have a mild phenotype on chow. On a choline-deficient diet they develop steatohepatitis and liver failure after 3 days, with a lower phosphatidylcholine to phosphatidylethanolamine ratio and leakage from hepatocyte membranes.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Liver failure by 3 days in Pemt knockout mice fed a choline-deficient diet. No human PEMT flux.
assessment.evidence_summary: Physiological boundary for the substrates, product regulation and the parallel choline-dependent route.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis. The knockout diet result removes PEMT and dietary choline together. It does not show that choline is methylated by PEMT.

evidence_dependency: Vance (2014) is also primary evidence in PM7-F2 for the separate claim that S-adenosylhomocysteine can regulate activity. It is not a second independent demonstration of the methyl-transfer chemistry.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Ridgway and Vance (1988)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Purified rat-liver kinetics place phosphatidylethanolamine and SAMe in an ordered mechanism and release S-adenosylhomocysteine after methyl transfer.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: The primary use of this paper is the product-regulation proposition in PM7-F2. It is cited here only to confirm the same substrates.

scientific_findings.finding_label: S-adenosylhomocysteine can regulate PEMT
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Each methyl transfer releases S-adenosylhomocysteine. The supply of that product can regulate PEMT activity. These sources do not show that a high homocysteine concentration itself was measured as a PEMT inhibitor.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Product regulation is part of the reaction. It is not evidence that lowering homocysteine with B vitamins changes the rate of this methylation in people.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: S-adenosylhomocysteine, the product released after each PEMT methyl transfer, can regulate PEMT activity. The attached and retrieved sources do not demonstrate that elevated homocysteine itself inhibits human PEMT.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The physiological review states that the product AdoHcy, together with the substrates AdoMet and phosphatidylethanolamine, can regulate PEMT. Purified rat-liver kinetics fit an ordered mechanism in which the phospholipid binds first, S-adenosylmethionine then binds, the methyl group is transferred and S-adenosylhomocysteine is released. Product-inhibition patterns were part of that kinetic analysis. Neither source reports a human experiment in which homocysteine concentration was the inhibitor tested against PEMT.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Regulation is stated in a review and inferred from product release and product-inhibition patterns in purified enzyme. The kinetic abstract does not give an S-adenosylhomocysteine inhibition constant. Homocysteine and S-adenosylhomocysteine are not interchangeable measurements. No human PEMT rate under raised homocysteine was assessed.

evidence_considered.label: Vance (2014)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: The supply of product AdoHcy can regulate PEMT activity, along with the supply of AdoMet and phosphatidylethanolamine.

assessment.study: Narrative review of PEMT regulation and physiology.
assessment.population: Review of biochemical and mouse evidence. Not a human inhibition trial.
assessment.result: Names AdoMet and phosphatidylethanolamine as substrates and AdoHcy as a product that can regulate activity. Does not report a homocysteine dose that inhibits PEMT.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No inhibition constant or human rate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Review-level statement that product AdoHcy can regulate PEMT.
assessment.limitations: Does not itself present the inhibition curves. Does not show that homocysteine concentration is the measured inhibitor.

evidence_considered.label: Ridgway and Vance (1988)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Purified rat-liver PEMT releases S-adenosylhomocysteine after methyl transfer, and product-inhibition patterns fit an ordered Bi Bi mechanism.

assessment.study: Steady-state kinetics and product-inhibition analysis of PEMT purified from rat liver, using phosphatidylethanolamine and its mono- and dimethyl intermediates.
assessment.population: Purified rat-liver enzyme in detergent-phospholipid micelles. No human participants.
assessment.result: Phospholipid substrates bind first and phospholipid products leave last. S-adenosylmethionine binds, the methyl group is transferred and S-adenosylhomocysteine is released. The three phospholipid substrates compete for one active site. Added egg phosphatidylcholine converted sigmoidal phospholipid curves toward hyperbolic kinetics.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The abstract does not report an S-adenosylhomocysteine inhibition constant. Hill coefficients for the phospholipid substrates were 3.6, 2.5 and 4.7 without added egg phosphatidylcholine and about 0.9 to 1.2 with 30 or 40 mol percent egg phosphatidylcholine.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct kinetic evidence that S-adenosylhomocysteine is the released product and that product inhibition was used to assign the mechanism.
assessment.limitations: Micellar enzyme kinetics are not liver flux in an intact animal or person. The abstract does not quantify homocysteine as the inhibitor.

evidence_dependency: Vance (2014) is also primary evidence in PM7-F1 for substrates and the choline-deficient knockout boundary. Reuse here is only for product regulation.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Brain DHA measurements do not measure PEMT rate
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Neonatal piglet brain DHA accretion and human cerebrospinal-fluid DHA enrichment measure delivery of DHA. They do not measure the rate of hepatic PEMT methylation.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Piglets given the same DHA dose as phosphatidylcholine or as triglyceride deposited more labelled DHA in brain gray matter from the phospholipid form. Liver labelling was the highest, which the study reads as processing and export rather than as an assay of phosphatidylethanolamine methylation. Adults given supplemental DHA, with B vitamins in both arms, increased cerebrospinal-fluid DHA and EPA. Brain volumes and cognitive scores did not differ from placebo. Neither endpoint is PEMT activity.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Both studies are informative about DHA delivery. Using them as if they measured this methylation overstates what they observed. The piglet contrast is one developmental model. The human trial is small, lasted six months and gave B vitamins to both groups.

evidence_considered.label: Liu et al. (2014)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: dietary
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Phosphatidylcholine-bound labelled DHA produced about 1.9-fold more gray-matter DHA accretion than triglyceride-bound DHA in neonatal piglets. Liver labelling was greatest.

assessment.study: Formula-fed neonatal piglets received an oral carbon-13 DHA dose bound to triglyceride or to phosphatidylcholine.
assessment.population: Neonatal piglets.
assessment.result: The phosphatidylcholine form was about 1.9-fold more efficacious for gray-matter DHA accretion and was also more efficacious in synaptosomes, retina, liver and red blood cells. The authors infer initial hepatic processing and later export.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About 1.9-fold gray-matter accretion contrast in that piglet comparison.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows a delivery-form difference for DHA accretion, with the liver as an early processing organ.
assessment.limitations: Not a PEMT activity or phosphatidylethanolamine-methylation assay. Not a human brain measurement.

evidence_considered.label: Arellanes et al. (2020)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Six months of supplemental DHA raised cerebrospinal-fluid DHA by about 28 percent versus placebo. Cognitive scores did not differ. PEMT was not measured.

assessment.study: Randomised placebo-controlled trial. Everyone received a B-vitamin complex. The randomised contrast was DHA versus placebo.
assessment.population: 33 adults, of whom 26 completed both lumbar punctures. Dose was 2,152 mg DHA per day for 6 months.
assessment.result: Cerebrospinal-fluid DHA rose 28 percent and EPA 43 percent in the DHA arm versus placebo. The cerebrospinal-fluid EPA rise in non-APOE4 carriers was about three times that in APOE4 carriers. Hippocampal volume, entorhinal thickness and cognitive scores did not differ between groups.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Mean cerebrospinal-fluid DHA difference 0.08 µg/mL (95 percent confidence interval 0.05 to 0.10). No PEMT or phosphatidylcholine methylation measurement.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human evidence of supplemental DHA reaching cerebrospinal fluid, not of hepatic PEMT rate.
assessment.limitations: Both arms received folic acid, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12, so the trial cannot isolate methylation from DHA delivery. Cognition was unchanged.

scientific_findings.finding_label: B-vitamin cognitive interaction does not measure PEMT
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In mild cognitive impairment, B vitamins were associated with slower cognitive decline when omega-3 status was higher. The study did not measure PEMT or phosphatidylcholine formation.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The result is a clinical interaction. The suggestion that B vitamins build omega-3-rich phosphatidylcholine is an interpretation, not a measurement of this reaction.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The VITACOG reanalysis shows a B-vitamin by omega-3 interaction on cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment. It does not measure PEMT activity or phosphatidylcholine formation, so a Cognitive Clarity link is a downstream inference.
scientific_findings.synthesis: People with mild cognitive impairment who received folic acid, vitamin B6 and vitamin B12 had better final memory, global cognition and clinical dementia ratings as baseline omega-3 status rose. Placebo scores did not. Docosahexaenoic acid tracked that interaction more than eicosapentaenoic acid. When omega-3 status was low, B vitamins had no cognitive effect. The paper does not report PEMT activity, phosphatidylethanolamine methylation or phosphatidylcholine composition.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: One reanalysis of one trial in older adults with mild cognitive impairment. It cannot separate homocysteine lowering, other B-vitamin actions and omega-3 status. It does not prove that no cognitive connection exists. It does prove that this dataset is not a PEMT assay.

evidence_considered.label: Oulhaj et al. (2016)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: supplemental-formulation
evidence_considered.directional_finding: B-vitamin treatment slowed cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment only when baseline omega-3 status was higher. PEMT was not measured.

assessment.study: Reanalysis of the VITACOG randomised trial, testing whether baseline plasma omega-3 status modified the cognitive effect of B vitamins.
assessment.population: 266 participants with mild cognitive impairment, aged 70 years or older, assigned to B vitamins or placebo for 2 years.
assessment.result: Verbal delayed recall, global cognition and clinical dementia rating sum-of-boxes were better on B vitamins as baseline omega-3 concentrations increased. Among those with good omega-3 status, 33 percent of the B-vitamin group had a global clinical dementia rating above zero, compared with 59 percent on placebo. Docosahexaenoic acid enhanced the B-vitamin effect more than eicosapentaenoic acid. Low omega-3 status removed the B-vitamin cognitive effect.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 33 percent versus 59 percent with a global clinical dementia rating above zero in the higher omega-3 stratum. No PEMT or phospholipid methylation estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Clinical interaction between B-vitamin treatment and omega-3 status.
assessment.limitations: Cognitive endpoints only. The phosphatidylcholine mechanism is proposed, not measured.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Vance (2014)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Establishes hepatic PEMT as a real route from phosphatidylethanolamine to phosphatidylcholine, which is the biology the cognitive paper invokes.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: It is a PEMT review, not a cognitive trial, and it does not test the B-vitamin by omega-3 interaction.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Attention reviews do not measure PEMT
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Reviews of diet in ADHD and of choline in neurodevelopment discuss attention-related nutrition. They do not measure PEMT or phosphatidylcholine formation.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Folate, omega-3 fats and choline can be relevant to other mechanisms. They are not evidence that this methylation changes attention.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Attached diet and choline reviews do not measure PEMT activity or phosphatidylcholine formation. A relationship to Focus / Attention Stability is a downstream inference.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A pediatrics review of dietary approaches to ADHD discusses additive-free diets, iron, zinc, omega-3 supplements and a pattern containing fibre, folate and omega-3 fats. A narrative review of choline in autism, ADHD and dyslexia discusses low choline intake and neurodevelopment. Neither review reports PEMT activity, phosphatidylethanolamine methylation or a phosphatidylcholine formation rate.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Narrative reviews mix many dietary exposures and outcomes. Absence of a PEMT measurement is a gap in what these papers can support. It is not proof that attention is unrelated to membrane phospholipids.

evidence_considered.label: Millichap and Yee (2012)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Reviews dietary approaches to ADHD, including omega-3 supplements and patterns containing folate and omega-3 fats, without measuring PEMT.

assessment.study: Narrative review of diet as a complementary approach when ADHD medication is unsatisfactory.
assessment.population: Children with ADHD in the reviewed literature. Not a PEMT sample.
assessment.result: Discusses sugar restriction, additive-free diets, elimination diets, iron, zinc, omega-3 supplements and a Western versus fibre, folate and omega-3 pattern. Does not report phosphatidylethanolamine methylation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No PEMT or phosphatidylcholine formation estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Dietary context for ADHD. Not an enzyme result.
assessment.limitations: Mixed interventions and opinion. Cannot attribute attention scores to this methylation.

evidence_considered.label: Derbyshire and Maes (2023)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Narrative review links lower choline intake or status with neurodevelopmental conditions and does not measure PEMT.

assessment.study: Narrative review of choline in autism spectrum conditions, ADHD and dyslexia.
assessment.population: Pregnancy, childhood and neurodevelopmental groups summarised from other studies.
assessment.result: Describes reports of low choline intake or altered choline status in those groups and treats choline as a possible modifiable factor. Calls for more mechanistic work. Does not assay PEMT.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No PEMT rate or attention effect size for this reaction.
assessment.evidence_summary: Choline and neurodevelopment context. Choline here is not shown to be the PEMT substrate.
assessment.limitations: Narrative review. Choline also feeds the CDP-choline route and acetylcholine, which are outside this methylation.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Donor insufficiency can constrain hepatic methylation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Folate restriction can reduce the contribution of dietary methyl groups to hepatic phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT in female mice.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Conditional animal evidence; tracer enrichment is not absolute flux. No universal donor limitation, human intake target or cognitive benefit is established.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Folate restriction can reduce the contribution of dietary methyl groups to hepatic phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT in female mice.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Named-donor restriction altered pathway-specific methyl incorporation with choline maintained. Betaine rescue under ethanol-induced imbalance is complementary evidence, not independent confirmation of the same exposure.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Conditional animal evidence; tracer enrichment is not absolute flux. No universal donor limitation, human intake target or cognitive benefit is established.

evidence_considered.label: Chew et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Donor restriction reduced pathway-specific methyl incorporation in female liver.

assessment.study: Eight-week folate restriction versus otherwise matched control diets with labelled choline. Indexed primary methods, results and discussion assessed.
assessment.population: Male and female Mthfr wild-type and heterozygous mice.
assessment.result: Females had lower hepatic d3-PC enrichment and product/precursor enrichment ratio; males lacked that hepatic response.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Hepatic d3-PC enrichment 30% lower (P=0.017); d3-PC:d9-choline ratio P=0.049.
assessment.evidence_summary: Donor restriction reduced pathway-specific methyl incorporation in female liver.
assessment.limitations: Precursor enrichment, turnover and methyl competition affect this measurement; total PEMT flux was not measured.

evidence_considered.label: Kharbanda et al. (2007)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Betaine corrected production under an imposed methylation imbalance.

assessment.study: Control/ethanol liquid diets with or without 1% betaine for four weeks. Primary abstract assessed; full assay methods unavailable.
assessment.population: Male Wistar rats.
assessment.result: Betaine restored SAM:SAH balance and reported PEMT-mediated PC production under ethanol exposure.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No usable numerical production estimate in the abstract.
assessment.evidence_summary: Betaine corrected production under an imposed methylation imbalance.
assessment.limitations: Supplement rescue does not establish ordinary betaine deficiency; assay details and ethanol context limit attribution.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Methionine supports PC methylation; the shared-pool constraint remains unresolved
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Dietary methionine supplies the SAM-dependent PC methylation route. Piglet tracing measures nutritional effects on methyl incorporation into PC, but does not establish a distinct methionine–cysteine pool bottleneck.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Substrate provision, synthesis allocation and a separately limiting pool are different claims. Neonatal feeding and genetic findings do not establish adult intake benefits or cysteine-specific effects.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Dietary methionine supplies the SAM-dependent PC methylation route. Piglet tracing measures nutritional effects on methyl incorporation into PC, but does not establish a distinct methionine–cysteine pool bottleneck.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Rat phospholipid measurements support the upstream supply route. New piglet tracer evidence moves beyond concentration endpoints, while donor restriction can redistribute methyl use toward PC. MAT1A impairment separately affects PEMT activity. These findings do not yet establish the proposed shared sulfur-pool constraint beyond provision.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: No universal human or absolute-flux threshold applies. Neonatal diet composition, competing methyl demands and pathway compensation bound the inference; neither shared pool limitation nor benefit from extra adult intake follows automatically.

evidence_considered.label: Sugiyama et al. (1998)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Dietary and inhibitor perturbations are consistent with altered PE methylation.

assessment.study: Fourteen-day feeding at three methionine levels with or without eritadenine. Primary abstract assessed; full text not obtained.
assessment.population: Rats.
assessment.result: Methionine increased SAM and microsomal PC:PE; eritadenine abolished lipid effects.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Methionine 2.5, 4.5 and 7.5 g/kg; eritadenine 30 mg/kg. No usable outcome magnitude in the abstract.
assessment.evidence_summary: Dietary and inhibitor perturbations are consistent with altered PE methylation.
assessment.limitations: PC:PE is not synthesis rate. Full intake-adequacy methods were not obtained. The 1995 primary abstract shows eritadenine is not a direct PEMT inhibitor, so its lipid effects are not selective enzyme-blockade evidence.

evidence_considered.label: Shimada et al. (2003)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Methionine-specific dietary effects were separable from choline removal.

assessment.study: Fourteen-day protein-level and methionine/cystine supplementation experiments; choline held constant. Primary full text assessed.
assessment.population: Male Wistar rats; six groups of eight per experiment.
assessment.result: Methionine raised SAM and PC:PE. Table 4 shows cystine rescued growth without the corresponding PC/PE change; glycine attenuated methionine-associated lipid responses.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Choline bitartrate 0.25 g/100 g diet; methionine 0.43%, cystine 0.34% supplements.
assessment.evidence_summary: Methionine-specific dietary effects were separable from choline removal.
assessment.limitations: Rat SAM concentrations, phospholipid pools and desaturase measurements do not measure PEMT flux. Growth rescue is not interchangeable with methyl provision; non-monotonic SAM responses suggest compensation.

evidence_considered.label: Cano et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Upstream enzyme impairment affected measured PEMT activity.

assessment.study: Indexed primary results and prior canonical appraisal of MAT1A knockout; full assay methods could not be retrieved in this pass.
assessment.population: Three- and eight-month-old wild-type and MAT1A-knockout mice.
assessment.result: PEMT activity decreased in young knockouts; older animals showed a different lipid/activity pattern.
assessment.effect_magnitude: PEMT activity 30% lower and transcript expression 40% lower in three-month-old knockouts; 4–8 animals per group.
assessment.evidence_summary: Upstream enzyme impairment affected measured PEMT activity.
assessment.limitations: Genetic loss changes expression and metabolism; it does not isolate dietary methionine inadequacy or cysteine sparing.

evidence_considered.label: Sugiyama et al. (1995)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Eritadenine reduced labelled methionine incorporation into PC without direct PEMT inhibition in the assay.

assessment.study: Primary publisher abstract; full methods not obtained.
assessment.population: Rats.
assessment.result: Eritadenine reduced labelled methionine incorporation into PC without direct PEMT inhibition in the assay.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 200 micromol/kg diet in the tracer comparison.
assessment.evidence_summary: Eritadenine reduced labelled methionine incorporation into PC without direct PEMT inhibition in the assay.
assessment.limitations: SAH accumulation and a lower SAM:SAH ratio accompanied the effect; not a selective PEMT probe.

evidence_considered.label: Robinson et al. (2016)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: PC synthesis rose while creatine synthesis fell under donor restriction.

assessment.study: Primary abstract; donor-deficient versus sufficient feeding, followed by methionine restriction in both groups.
assessment.population: Neonatal piglets; 8 deficient and 7 sufficient.
assessment.result: PC synthesis rose while creatine synthesis fell under donor restriction.
assessment.effect_magnitude: PC +60%; creatine -30%; methionine 80% of requirement.
assessment.evidence_summary: PC synthesis rose while creatine synthesis fell under donor restriction.
assessment.limitations: Combined donor exposure; not isolated methionine/cysteine effects, adult biology or uniform PC suppression.

evidence_considered.label: Asiriwardhana et al. (2025)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Methyl-tracer incorporation into hepatic PC increased with dietary methionine.

assessment.study: Primary full XML; Methods and Figure 4C. Each pig received one methionine dose for 48 hours.
assessment.population: 20 neonatal Yucatan piglets.
assessment.result: Methyl-tracer incorporation into hepatic PC increased with dietary methionine.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 20–220% of estimated requirement; linear r2=0.53, P<0.0003.
assessment.evidence_summary: Methyl-tracer incorporation into hepatic PC increased with dietary methionine.
assessment.limitations: Cysteine fixed; no added free choline, but lipid emulsion supplied PC. Total Kennedy/PEMT flux and cysteine sparing were not independently determined. No adult dose or benefit inference.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Dietary choline forms supply methyl groups to the PEMT route
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Choline and dietary phosphatidylcholine can provide methyl groups used in PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Plasma tracing does not measure absolute hepatic flux, intermediary SAM, ordinary-food equivalence or benefit.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Choline and dietary phosphatidylcholine can provide methyl groups used in PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Provision is supported by methyl-derived labelling, separately from intact-headgroup PC. This does not establish indispensable dependence or enhanced activity.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Plasma tracing does not measure absolute hepatic flux, intermediary SAM, ordinary-food equivalence or benefit.

evidence_considered.label: Böckmann et al. (2023)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: D3-PC supports methyl-donor provision after choline chloride and POPC.

assessment.study: Randomised crossover, labelled choline forms; full text assessed.
assessment.population: Six healthy men.
assessment.result: Results subsection D3-PC from the PEMT pathway: Figure S5B reports delayed D3-PC after all four inputs; S5A relates it to betaine labelling.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No significant D3-PC difference between formulations.
assessment.evidence_summary: D3-PC supports methyl-donor provision after choline chloride and POPC.
assessment.limitations: D3-PC (m/z 187) is distinct from D9-PC (193). Methionine/SAM intermediates and hepatic origin are mechanistically attributed, not directly measured here.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Uridine supplies nucleotide precursors for the Kennedy pathway
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Uridine can contribute to CTP and CDP-choline supply for the Kennedy route of phosphatidylcholine formation.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Uridine can contribute to CTP and CDP-choline supply for the Kennedy route of phosphatidylcholine formation.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The supported precursor chain is distinct from PEMT; dietary provision does not establish indispensability, increased human PC flux or cognitive benefit.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Rat-slice CDP-choline formation and oral-UMP gerbil precursor measurements support nucleotide provision. Human MRS is connected evidence for phospholipid precursor responses, not direct confirmation of PC synthesis. A four-week gerbil experiment also measured increased PC abundance with UMP alone on a choline-containing diet, extending support beyond precursor pools without establishing human synthesis flux.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Endogenous nucleotide production and salvage remain alternative sources. Tissue, species, exposure form and measured endpoint limit translation; no ordinary-food uridine target is established.

evidence_considered.label: Ulus et al. (2006)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Uridine increased CDP-choline formation in rat brain slices without reducing acetylcholine release.

assessment.study: Primary full text; Abstract, Introduction, Methods and Results. Rat slices exposed to uridine or cytidine with and without choline.
assessment.population: Rat striatal slices; hippocampal and cortical slices also tested for acetylcholine release.
assessment.result: At 400 micromolar, uridine increased choline utilisation to form CDP-choline by 61%; acetylcholine release and levels were not reduced.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 61% increase in CDP-choline formation at 400 micromolar uridine; tested nucleoside concentrations 25–400 micromolar.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports a nucleotide-provision route to a Kennedy-pathway intermediate, distinct from PEMT methyl transfer.
assessment.limitations: Ex-vivo concentrations; CDP-choline formation is not an absolute PC synthesis-flux assay, an ordinary-food exposure or a human cognitive outcome.

evidence_considered.label: Cansev et al. (2005)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Oral UMP increased brain uridine, UTP, CTP and CDP-choline in gerbils.

assessment.study: Primary publisher abstract and accessible Results summary; single oral UMP gavage, serial plasma and brain measurements.
assessment.population: Adult male Mongolian gerbils.
assessment.result: Oral UMP increased circulating and brain uridine and brain nucleotide/CDP-choline pools.
assessment.effect_magnitude: At 1 mmol/kg, plasma uridine rose from 6.6 to 32.7 micromolar at 30 minutes; brain uridine from 22.6 to 89.1 pmol/mg.
assessment.evidence_summary: Measured oral provision to brain precursor pools supports the UMP/uridine-to-nucleotide chain.
assessment.limitations: UMP exposure is not isolated dietary uridine or an ordinary-food dose; altered pool concentrations do not determine net PC flux, human adequacy or benefit.

evidence_considered.label: Wurtman et al. (2006)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Dietary UMP increased brain PC abundance in gerbils consuming a choline-containing diet.

assessment.study: Primary full text; Results §2.1 and Table 1A. Four-week UMP and/or DHA treatment compared with control.
assessment.population: Adult gerbils on a choline-containing diet.
assessment.result: UMP alone increased PC abundance; the UMP/DHA combination produced a larger response.
assessment.effect_magnitude: PC per mg protein: UMP alone +13%; DHA alone +22%; combination +45%.
assessment.evidence_summary: Adds a measured PC abundance endpoint beyond short-term nucleotide pools.
assessment.limitations: UMP rather than isolated uridine; animal exposure. PC abundance is not synthesis flux or a human outcome. Combination responses cannot be attributed to uridine alone; protein markers do not count synapses.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Agarwal et al. (2010)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Randomised uridine/placebo study in 17 healthy men; 1 g twice daily for seven days, with phosphorus MRS. Brain phosphomonoesters increased.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: MRS precursor pools do not identify CTP supply, PC synthesis flux or membrane accretion; no uridine-specific cognition claim follows.

pm_kc_relationships.dietary_input_note: Pool/constraint dependency, not another dietary constituent. Dietary supply decisions belong to its separately admitted PM input atoms.
pm_kc_relationships.reader_description: A limited or imbalanced methyl-donor pool can constrain hepatic PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation in demonstrated animal contexts.
pm_kc_relationships.pm_biological_role: One-carbon donor insufficiency or imbalance can constrain PEMT-dependent formation; folate restriction reduced hepatic methyl incorporation in female mice.
pm_kc_relationships.evidence_limitation: Conditional animal evidence; tracer enrichment is not absolute flux. No universal donor limitation, human intake target or cognitive benefit is established.

constituent_relationships.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
constituent_relationships.reader_description: Folate availability supports methyl-group provision for PEMT-dependent formation.

constituent_relationships.label: Betaine
constituent_relationships.reader_description: Betaine can support PEMT-dependent formation when methylation is impaired in the studied ethanol model.

title: NF-kB Signalling Regulation
mission: Regulate NF-κB transcriptional tone so pro-inflammatory gene programmes do not fire excessively.
summary: NF-κB regulates inflammatory gene programmes. IKK-dependent inhibitor phosphorylation permits its activation; glutathione-dependent redox changes also regulate kinase activity and DNA binding. These distinct cellular readouts support the mechanism, but do not establish a dietary dose that improves human inflammatory regulation.

scientific_findings_intro: IKK experiments establish an activation gate, while redox studies demonstrate glutathione-dependent regulation of kinase activity and DNA binding. Human precursor tracing supports glutathione provision, but does not measure NF-κB. Together these findings support a bounded upstream supply relationship, not a proven dietary anti-inflammatory effect.

scientific_findings.finding_label: IKK phosphorylation is required for NF-κB activation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: A purified complex from HeLa cells contains two related kinases, IKK-1 and IKK-2. They phosphorylate the inhibitor proteins that hold NF-κB. Mutant IKK-2 changes NF-κB movement into the nucleus and NF-κB-dependent reporter activity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This identifies the kinase step. It does not show that dietary magnesium, polyphenols, fibre, or omega-3 fats change how fast those genes are transcribed.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: IKK-1 and IKK-2 phosphorylate the NF-κB inhibitor proteins, and IKK-2 is required for NF-κB activation in the cell systems tested. This is an upstream activation step, rather than transcription itself.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Mercurio and colleagues purified a large IκB kinase complex from cytokine-stimulated HeLa cells. It phosphorylated IκB-alpha and IκB-beta. The two kinase components, IKK-1 and IKK-2, are related serine kinases. Mutant IKK-2 had pronounced effects on RelA nuclear translocation and on an NF-κB-dependent reporter. The paper does not test diet.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The result is a cell-biochemistry identification of the kinase. It is not a human intake trial, and it does not measure dietary magnesium.

evidence_considered.label: Mercurio et al. (1997)
evidence_considered.exposure_context: cytokine-stimulated HeLa cells
evidence_considered.directional_finding: IKK-1 and IKK-2 were identified as cytokine-activated kinases that phosphorylate IκB-alpha and IκB-beta. Mutant IKK-2 altered RelA nuclear translocation and NF-κB-dependent reporter activity.

assessment.study: Purification of the IκB kinase signalsome from HeLa cells, with identification of IKK-1 and IKK-2 and tests of IKK-2 mutants.
assessment.population: Cultured HeLa cells. No human dietary cohort.
assessment.result: The complex phosphorylates the inhibitor proteins, and IKK-2 mutants change NF-κB activation readouts.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The paper reports a pronounced effect of IKK-2 mutants on RelA translocation and reporter activity. It does not report a fold change in human transcription rate.
assessment.evidence_summary: The kinase step that releases NF-κB is IKK phosphorylation of the inhibitor proteins.
assessment.limitations: Cell biochemistry is not dietary magnesium, and it is not a measure of how fast inflammatory genes are transcribed in people.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Adams (2001)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Protein kinases transfer phosphate from ATP, and that class of reaction is the chemical setting for the IKK step.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: The review is not an IKK assay, not an NF-κB transcription measurement, and not a dietary magnesium trial. Kinase assays that include magnesium chloride do not show that ordinary magnesium intake sets this transcription rate.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Glutathione-dependent redox regulation connects precursor supply to NF-κB
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Glutathione participates in redox control of NF-κB. Human precursor supplementation supports glutathione provision; cellular studies establish a separate redox-regulation link.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The chain supports upstream resource supply, while its tissue-specific dietary limiting effect remains unresolved. Regulation is not uniformly anti-inflammatory.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Cysteine and glycine supply glutathione used in redox regulation of NF-κB; this establishes upstream supply rather than proven dietary control of transcription.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The evidence measures different links: precursor provision and red-cell glutathione synthesis in humans; glutathione-dependent kinase, nuclear-translocation and DNA-binding regulation in experimental cells. Joining these links is mechanistic triangulation, not an end-to-end human intervention result.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is supported upstream supply, not a demonstrated dietary constraint on NF-κB. Human precursor supplementation measured red-cell glutathione, not NF-κB; cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine. Cellular redox studies show context-dependent effects, including inhibition after glutathione depletion or increased extracellular cysteine. Neither individual dietary limitation, brain transfer nor benefit from additional intake is established.
