scientific_findings_intro: The expanded evidence supports several ways to change entry: cereal processing and defined fibre preparations redistribute tracer-derived appearance, while sequencing and whey preloading delay measured gastric delivery. Pasta structure and cooling add supported digestion/composition links, with systemic entry still inferred. Effects are preparation-specific: the guar blend did not change its primary half-absorption-time endpoint, and mycoprotein did not slow exogenous appearance. Slower entry is not always preferable, as the vinegar gastroparesis result illustrates. Vinoy et al. (2013) [[8]](#pm-ref-8); Nazare et al. (2009) [[11]](#pm-ref-11); Ma et al. (2009) [[13]](#pm-ref-13); Whelehan et al. (2024) [[18]](#pm-ref-18)

title: Glycaemic Variability Regulation
mission: Limit glycaemic volatility so post-prandial glucose swings do not create unnecessary metabolic and neuroendocrine stress.
summary: Blood glucose varies as meals arrive and tissues take up their fuel. Regulation concerns the size, duration and frequency of these changes, rather than keeping glucose perfectly flat. In people with type 2 diabetes, short aerobic training reduced measured excursions. The order of a meal also changed within-meal variability. These findings identify activity and meal protocols that can influence different parts of the glucose pattern.
dose_sensitivity: Effects depend on the tested exposure, preparation and study population; no universal dose is established.

title: Insulin Sensitivity & Glucose Disposal
mission: Sustain insulin-sensitive glucose disposal so post-meal glucose clears efficiently without prolonged metabolic strain.
summary: Insulin helps tissues take up and store circulating glucose after a meal. The effectiveness of that response depends on cellular signalling and the condition of muscle, liver and fat tissue. Exercise training can improve measured insulin action even without weight loss. Magnesium also participates in insulin-receptor function, with deficiency experiments showing impaired action. These routes concern the capacity to handle glucose already available in the circulation.
dose_sensitivity: Effects depend on the tested exposure, preparation and study population; no universal dose is established.

title: Cortisol Rhythm Regulation
mission: Maintain diurnal cortisol amplitude and phase so morning activation and evening downshift stay well timed.
summary: Cortisol helps coordinate daily activation, fuel handling and responses to demand. Its timing matters: the body normally produces a pattern across the day, rather than one ideal concentration. A laboratory shift of sleep and meals reversed that pattern relative to the waking schedule. This makes the alignment of daily routines a relevant route. A prebiotic trial measured a narrower waking response, which is useful evidence but a different endpoint.
dose_sensitivity: Effects depend on the tested exposure, preparation and study population; no universal dose is established.

title: Sympathetic Activation & Parasympathetic Recovery
mission: Maintain autonomic flexibility by shifting cleanly from sympathetic activation back into parasympathetic recovery.
summary: Autonomic responses prepare the body for demand and then support recovery. Sympathetic and parasympathetic activity are not a simple on/off pair: their responses can differ across organs and over time. Useful regulation means measuring both activation and the return towards baseline. A brief meditation experiment tracked cardiac variability and skin conductance after stress, providing a specific recovery route rather than assuming that every calming exposure has the same physiological effect.
dose_sensitivity: Effects depend on the tested exposure, preparation and study population; no universal dose is established.

title: Vagal Tone / HRV Regulation
mission: Sustain vagal tone so heart-rate-variability-linked recovery signalling remains robust under repeated stress exposure.
summary: The vagus nerve helps regulate the heart’s response to demand. Heart-rate variability, the changing interval between beats, provides one window onto cardiac regulation when breathing and measurement conditions are considered. Paced breathing can change this signal during a session. An omega-3 trial also found changes in adults with elevated triglycerides. These findings make cardiac regulation addressable, while requiring a clear distinction between measured HRV and the wider functions of the vagus.
dose_sensitivity: Effects depend on the tested exposure, preparation and study population; no universal dose is established.

title: Adipose Endocrine Regulation

evidence_gaps.title: Dietary systemic cortisol changes do not establish local adipose target engagement
evidence_gaps.establishes: Human tracer studies distinguish local adipose cortisol regeneration from whole-body metabolism. The dietary crossover changed whole-body cortisol metabolism without a corresponding change in measured subcutaneous adipose 11β-HSD1. Separate long-term dietary evidence measured decreased adipose 11β-HSD1 mRNA, not direct enzyme activity; this qualifies a blanket claim of no local dietary response.
evidence_gaps.cannot_establish: That the tested diet changes the local adipose glucocorticoid operation defined by PM8.
evidence_gaps.missing_link: Systemic cortisol metabolism is not a measurement of local adipose enzyme activity. Depot and measurement context remain material.
evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Dietary studies measuring relevant local adipose glucocorticoid target engagement alongside systemic endpoints.
evidence_gaps.affected_relationship: Activity/flux and tissue specificity of dietary glucocorticoid regulation; local transcript responses retained without inferring enzyme activity.

evidence_gaps.title: Mouse adipocyte-receptor effects do not establish a human dietary stress-feedback route
evidence_gaps.establishes: Adipocyte glucocorticoid-receptor reduction altered stress-feedback responses in a genetic mouse experiment.
evidence_gaps.cannot_establish: An identified adipokine mediator, an equivalent human pathway or a human dietary intervention acting through that pathway.
evidence_gaps.missing_link: The signalling mediator remains unresolved; genetic perturbation in mice is not human dietary target engagement.
evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Identification of the mediator and appropriate human pathway and intervention measurements before a dietary claim is supported.
evidence_gaps.affected_relationship: Adipocyte glucocorticoid-to-brain stress feedback.

evidence_gaps.title: DHA food composition does not establish supplement-equivalent local secretion
evidence_gaps.establishes: Defined oral DHA can modulate circulating adiponectin; mixed fish oil can be incorporated into adipose tissue. Human cell experiments separately measured secretion.
evidence_gaps.cannot_establish: That ordinary DHA-containing foods reproduce trial formulations, or that the circulating response proves local secretion or receptor sensitivity.
evidence_gaps.missing_link: Food-to-formulation equivalence and the local secretory mediator remain unestablished; this is not a general failure of oral delivery.
evidence_gaps.required_evidence: A defined dietary exposure with relevant adipose exposure and endocrine engagement measurements, retaining formulation and population boundaries.
evidence_gaps.affected_relationship: The bounded DHA Type B circulating-signal admission is retained; stronger food-efficacy or local-secretory claims remain unsupported.

evidence_gaps.title: Local exercise responses do not establish a universal secretion or benefit claim
evidence_gaps.establishes: Some aerobic protocols altered local interstitial hormone concentration or adipose transcripts; another training context was null.
evidence_gaps.cannot_establish: A universal secretion-rate response, optimal training dose or improved receptor sensitivity.
evidence_gaps.missing_link: Local concentration, transcript, release flux and clinical outcomes are separate endpoints.
evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Comparable protocols with prespecified secretion/flux or responsiveness endpoints and energy-balance control.
evidence_gaps.affected_relationship: The admitted aerobic practice is limited to context-specific local endocrine engagement.

evidence_gaps.title: Flaxseed trial effects do not identify an active constituent or universal response
evidence_gaps.establishes: A defined milled-food trial reported a circulating adiponectin difference; pooled evidence was heterogeneous and not significant overall.
evidence_gaps.cannot_establish: An isolated ALA, lignan or fibre effect, a weight-independent secretory mechanism or a universal recommendation.
evidence_gaps.missing_link: Component attribution and reproducibility across populations/forms remain unresolved.
evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Comparable food protocols with appropriate weight mediation and endocrine mechanism measurements.
evidence_gaps.affected_relationship: Bounded PM8-SOP-2; no isolated-substance admission.

evidence_gaps.title: Soluble-fibre endocrine claim lacks coherent overall trial support
evidence_gaps.establishes: Pooled circulating results include no-effect values and substantial heterogeneity.
evidence_gaps.cannot_establish: A generic soluble-fibre intervention for PM8 endocrine regulation.
evidence_gaps.missing_link: Specific preparation/exposure and coherent endocrine engagement remain unestablished.
evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Subtype- and population-specific trials with prespecified relevant endpoints and reproducible effects.
evidence_gaps.affected_relationship: No general fibre Type A/B admission.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Adipokine responses depend on hormone, depot and exposure
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Insulin and glucocorticoid exposures regulate leptin synthesis or release and adiponectin expression or release in human adipose preparations, with context-dependent responses.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Insulin and glucocorticoid exposures regulate leptin synthesis or release and adiponectin expression or release in human adipose preparations, with context-dependent responses.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Human adipose pulse-labelling separates leptin biosynthesis from release of stored protein. Dexamethasone can increase leptin synthesis while suppressing adiponectin release in other preparations; these are distinct hormone-specific responses. Circulating adiponectin responses to systemic glucocorticoids are not uniformly reproduced.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Human adipose pulse-labelling separates leptin biosynthesis from release of stored protein. Dexamethasone can increase leptin synthesis while suppressing adiponectin release in other preparations; these are distinct hormone-specific responses. Circulating adiponectin responses to systemic glucocorticoids are not uniformly reproduced.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Ex vivo hormone exposures and pharmacological glucocorticoids do not establish ordinary dietary effects. Donor adiposity, depot, exposure duration and concentration matter; circulating concentrations do not measure secretion rates or receptor sensitivity.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Local adipose cortisol regeneration differs from systemic metabolism
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human adipose cortisol regeneration is tissue- and metabolic-context dependent; whole-body dietary changes in cortisol metabolism do not necessarily alter subcutaneous adipose 11β-HSD1.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human adipose cortisol regeneration is tissue- and metabolic-context dependent; whole-body dietary changes in cortisol metabolism do not necessarily alter subcutaneous adipose 11β-HSD1.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Microdialysis and tracer measurements distinguish local cortisone-to-cortisol conversion from systemic turnover. Insulin effects differed by adiposity. A low-carbohydrate crossover altered systemic cortisol metabolism without a measured adipose 11β-HSD1 response; weight loss in another small study increased adipocyte transcript expression rather than demonstrating universal suppression.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Microdialysis and tracer measurements distinguish local cortisone-to-cortisol conversion from systemic turnover. Insulin effects differed by adiposity. A low-carbohydrate crossover altered systemic cortisol metabolism without a measured adipose 11β-HSD1 response; weight loss in another small study increased adipocyte transcript expression rather than demonstrating universal suppression.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Small selected samples and differing assays; transcript abundance is not in vivo regeneration flux. Systemic or hepatic effects cannot be assigned to adipose, and less local cortisol activity is not assumed universally beneficial.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Adipocyte glucocorticoid-receptor reduction changes mouse stress feedback
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Reducing glucocorticoid-receptor expression in adiponectin-Cre mice increased restraint-related corticosterone responses and impaired dexamethasone feedback, without a detected baseline leptin or adiponectin difference.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Reducing glucocorticoid-receptor expression in adiponectin-Cre mice increased restraint-related corticosterone responses and impaired dexamethasone feedback, without a detected baseline leptin or adiponectin difference.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The genetic experiment supports a qualified contribution of adipocyte-enriched GR signalling to mouse stress feedback. The communicating signal was not identified; unchanged baseline adipokines do not establish an adipokine-mediated pathway. Human stress feedback through the same route remains unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The genetic experiment supports a qualified contribution of adipocyte-enriched GR signalling to mouse stress feedback. The communicating signal was not identified; unchanged baseline adipokines do not establish an adipokine-mediated pathway. Human stress feedback through the same route remains unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Genetic mouse model, incomplete and depot-variable knockdown, possible untested off-target sites, and developmental effects. Baseline hormone concentrations do not exclude dynamic secretion changes. No human dietary, cognitive or ADHD effect is established.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Dietary weight-reduction programmes alter local adipokine release within studied contexts
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Hypocaloric weight-reduction programmes in women with obesity reduced ex vivo adipose leptin release, while adiponectin responses were depot-specific or unchanged.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Hypocaloric weight-reduction programmes in women with obesity reduced ex vivo adipose leptin release, while adiponectin responses were depot-specific or unchanged.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Independent programmes measured adipose release rather than relying on circulating concentrations alone. You measured release in 27 of 42 women and found abdominal but not gluteal adiponectin increases. Arvidsson found lower leptin secretion without an adiponectin increase. Siklova shows that active restriction and stabilisation differ. Fasting and mixed-meal arteriovenous studies provide contextual evidence of acute local regulation, not equivalent weight-loss protocols.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Independent programmes measured adipose release rather than relying on circulating concentrations alone. You measured release in 27 of 42 women and found abdominal but not gluteal adiponectin increases. Arvidsson found lower leptin secretion without an adiponectin increase. Siklova shows that active restriction and stabilisation differ. Fasting and mixed-meal arteriovenous studies provide contextual evidence of acute local regulation, not equivalent weight-loss protocols.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Energy deficit, weight loss and co-interventions are not fully separable. Ex vivo release, venous–arterial concentration difference, transcript and plasma measurements remain distinct. No universal optimal hormone direction, food attribution, brain benefit or weight-independent endocrine effect is established.

scientific_findings.finding_summary: Some catechin-enriched tea beverages reduced visceral fat, while a newer catechin-plus-inulin beverage did not.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Some catechin-enriched tea beverages reduced visceral fat, while a newer catechin-plus-inulin beverage did not.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Green tea is a reasonable component to test, with evidence tied to the actual beverage and comparator. Ordinary brewed tea, catechin-enriched products and combined formulations are not equivalent exposures.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Green tea is a reasonable component to test, with evidence tied to the actual beverage and comparator. Ordinary brewed tea, catechin-enriched products and combined formulations are not equivalent exposures.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The positive and null trials differ in formulation, population and fat assessment; neither isolates adipose inflammatory signalling or proves a general brewed-tea effect.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Marine omega-3 tissue effects vary with context
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Marine omega-3 formulations can change adipose inflammatory endpoints, but effects differ across populations and assays.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Marine omega-3 formulations can change adipose inflammatory endpoints, but effects differ across populations and assays.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Biopsy evidence is mixed: Spencer found lower macrophage/MCP-1 endpoints, Hames did not replicate a tissue inflammatory benefit despite EPA/DHA incorporation, and Fisk found limited responses in obesity. A conditional formulation-specific practice remains provisional rather than a reliable general treatment.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Biopsy evidence is mixed: Spencer found lower macrophage/MCP-1 endpoints, Hames did not replicate a tissue inflammatory benefit despite EPA/DHA incorporation, and Fisk found limited responses in obesity. A conditional formulation-specific practice remains provisional rather than a reliable general treatment.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Doses, baseline metabolic state, depot and assays differ; tissue target engagement does not establish improved insulin sensitivity or an ordinary-food equivalent.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Adipose stress includes immune and oxidative processes
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Adipose expansion is associated with macrophage inflammatory activity, while acute overnutrition can impair metabolism before measured cytokines rise.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Adipose expansion is associated with macrophage inflammatory activity, while acute overnutrition can impair metabolism before measured cytokines rise.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Macrophage recruitment and oxidative stress provide complementary biological routes; reducing fat mass or a blood cytokine cannot be treated as a complete assay of either route.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Macrophage recruitment and oxidative stress provide complementary biological routes; reducing fat mass or a blood cytokine cannot be treated as a complete assay of either route.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Human macrophage evidence includes observational associations; extreme acute overfeeding in six men is not an ordinary-diet experiment or proof of a universal sequence.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Magnesium is a research candidate with context-dependent adipose effects
scientific_findings.finding_summary: A simple claim that more magnesium reduces adipose stress is not established by the assessed evidence.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: A simple claim that more magnesium reduces adipose stress is not established by the assessed evidence.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The attached review motivates investigation; primary mouse data show that low-magnesium exposure can reduce fat accumulation while raising circulating lipids. This challenges a simple adiposity-as-benefit interpretation.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The attached review motivates investigation; primary mouse data show that low-magnesium exposure can reduce fat accumulation while raising circulating lipids. This challenges a simple adiposity-as-benefit interpretation.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Mouse deficiency is not a human dietary strategy; a PM8-specific human dependency or tissue benefit remains unresolved after targeted retrieval.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Exercise can remodel adipose tissue without weight loss
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Exercise training altered subcutaneous adipose structure without weight loss in adults with obesity.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Exercise training altered subcutaneous adipose structure without weight loss in adults with obesity.

scientific_findings.synthesis: Regular activity is relevant to adipose remodelling, but the observed signalling changes are not a blanket reduction in inflammation or proof that one training intensity is superior.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Sleep restriction can promote visceral-fat accumulation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Severe sleep restriction increased visceral fat during a controlled experiment with freely available food.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Severe sleep restriction increased visceral fat during a controlled experiment with freely available food.

scientific_findings.synthesis: Avoiding repeated severe sleep loss is relevant to adipose load. This experiment does not establish that sleep extension reverses established adipose inflammation.

dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Reduces visceral adipose volume in the tested weight-loss programme, with associated changes in circulating inflammation-related proteins.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Green Mediterranean dietary pattern
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: This tested pattern combined walnuts (28 g/day), green tea (3–4 cups/day), Mankai (100 g/day frozen plant in a shake), and reduced red/processed meat. It reduced visceral fat more than the comparison diets in adults with abdominal obesity. These foods are targets for further testing: their individual contributions remain uncertain, walnut evidence is mixed, and enriched tea beverages are not interchangeable with ordinary brewed tea.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Diet-induced weight reduction when excess adiposity is relevant

system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: Later progressive-loss comparisons involved nine participants and were not independently randomized; other depots and unmeasured inflammatory processes remain uncertain.
system_optimisation_practices.reader_description: A diet-induced weight-reduction programme changed adipose tissue biology in adults with obesity. Early insulin improvements preceded the measured inflammatory decline, and later tissue comparisons were small.
system_optimisation_practices.dietary_input_note: Dietary energy-reduction programme; not a universal weight-loss prescription.

system_optimisation_practices.input: Marine omega-3 formulations in selected metabolic contexts
system_optimisation_practices.biological_role: Tested marine omega-3 formulations altered adipose macrophage, chemokine, transcript or oxylipin endpoints in selected adults, with variable responses.
system_optimisation_practices.evidence_limitation: Doses, baseline metabolic state, depot and assays differ; tissue target engagement does not establish improved insulin sensitivity or an ordinary-food equivalent.

system_optimisation_practices.reader_description: Adipose biopsy trials have mixed results: some tissue endpoints improved, while another trial found no inflammatory benefit despite EPA/DHA incorporation. system_optimisation_practices.input: Ten-hour eating window for adults with obesity and long baseline eating windows

routes.context: Adults with abdominal obesity; combined diet and physical-activity programme.
routes.limitations: One predominantly male workplace cohort; the foods were not independently randomized, fat volume is not a biopsy of inflammation, and the protein analysis is not independent replication.

routes.intervention_effect: Defined dietary and supplemental protocols changed tissue or fat endpoints.
routes.context: Protocol-specific selected populations.
routes.limitations: Tissue responses vary; no independent component or universal protocol benefit.

routes.context: Training study and small inpatient sleep-loss crossover.
routes.limitations: Different endpoints and designs; no comparative superiority inferred.

scientific_principles.title: 11β-HSD1 cortisone–cortisol interconversion
scientific_principles.proposition: HSD11B1 catalyses NADP(H)-dependent cortisone–cortisol interconversion and predominantly acts as a reductase in vivo.
scientific_principles.mechanism: Local glucocorticoid regeneration; reaction participation of NADPH is distinct from a dietary requirement.
scientific_principles.scope_limitations: Molecular reaction identity does not establish its net rate in every tissue, dietary niacin limitation, or an optimal cortisol concentration.
scientific_principles.classification_rationale: Curated enzyme/reaction identity; context-dependent human regulation is assessed separately in SF13.

scientific_principles.title: Leptin and adiponectin are distinct endocrine molecules
scientific_principles.proposition: Leptin and adiponectin are distinct adipokines with receptor identities LEPR and ADIPOR1/ADIPOR2, respectively.
scientific_principles.mechanism: Adipose endocrine communication; production, release, circulating exposure and target responsiveness are separate relationships.
scientific_principles.scope_limitations: No claim that concentrations measure secretion or receptor sensitivity; no dietary or clinical effect follows from molecular identity.
scientific_principles.classification_rationale: Curated molecular and receptor relationships, not an intervention synthesis.

source_assessments.title: Regional adipose tissue hormone/cytokine production before and after weight loss in abdominally obese women.
source_assessments.label: You et al. (2014)
source_assessments.exposure: 42 older abdominally obese women; 20-week hypocaloric programme, with or without aerobic exercise; pooled pre/post analysis. Ex vivo release measured in 27 women.
source_assessments.endpoint: Abdominal/gluteal tissue leptin and adiponectin gene expression and ex vivo release; plasma separately.
source_assessments.result: Weight loss 10.1 ± 0.7 kg. Leptin release decreased in both depots; adiponectin release increased only abdominally. Tissue and circulating changes were not significantly correlated.
source_assessments.limitations: Release subgroup n=27, expression n=42. No untreated comparator for pooled analysis; exercise could not be isolated. Whole-tissue ex vivo release is not in vivo flux. Population, depot, weight loss and energy balance constrain interpretation.
source_assessments.decision: Supports bounded dietary-programme SOP, not universal hormone optimisation.
source_assessments.access: Full primary Methods/Results/Discussion and figures recovered through Scite; all 21,177 body characters reviewed.

source_assessments.title: Effects of different hypocaloric diets on protein secretion from adipose tissue of obese women.
source_assessments.label: Arvidsson et al. (2004)
source_assessments.exposure: 40 women with obesity randomised to 10-week hypocaloric low-fat/high-carbohydrate or moderate-fat/moderate-carbohydrate diets; deficit 600 kcal/day.
source_assessments.endpoint: Subcutaneous adipose ex vivo protein secretion and transcripts, with circulating concentrations separately.
source_assessments.result: Approximately 7.5% weight loss and 40% lower leptin secretion; adiponectin secretion unchanged. Diet arms had similar responses.
source_assessments.limitations: No weight-stable comparator; cannot separate energy deficit from weight loss. Adiponectin null qualifies You abdominal response; no macronutrient superiority. Tested deficit is a study exposure, not an effective-dose prescription.
source_assessments.decision: Independent qualified support for dietary programme; retain null adiponectin result.
source_assessments.access: Primary abstract and accessible journal/PDF excerpts; complete bias appraisal remains limited.

source_assessments.title: Effect of fish oil on circulating adiponectin: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
source_assessments.label: Wu et al. (2013)
source_assessments.exposure: Systematic review/meta-analysis: 14 fish-oil trial arms, 682 intervention/641 control; two fish-feeding arms separately.
source_assessments.endpoint: Circulating adiponectin, not adipose secretion.
source_assessments.result: Fish-oil pooled +0.37 µg/mL (95% CI 0.07–0.67), substantial heterogeneity; publication-bias adjustment +0.18 (−0.15 to 0.52). Fish-feeding estimate −0.01 (−0.65 to 0.64).
source_assessments.limitations: Secondary synthesis; do not double-count included trials. Blood concentration does not identify secretion mechanism; heterogeneous formulations and publication bias limit coherence.
source_assessments.decision: Supports physiological dietary response but does not close local secretory mediation or ordinary-fish equivalence.
source_assessments.access: Full accessible review text and abstract; synthesis not an independent primary experiment.

title: Stress-Modulated Appetite & Reward Regulation
mission: Coordinate stress-responsive hypothalamic and reward signalling to regulate appetite and food-seeking motivation as physiological demands change.
summary: Stress can change how food cues, appetite and emotional responses interact. People differ: some eat more after a stressor while others do not. The relevant process is the coupling of stress to food-seeking and reward, rather than hunger or cortisol alone. A food-related mindfulness programme reduced reported stress-eating tendencies and cravings in selected adults. Its imaging findings provide accompanying neural context, without establishing that those changes caused the behavioural response.
dose_sensitivity: Effects depend on the tested exposure, preparation and study population; no universal dose is established.

title: Light–Dark Circadian Entrainment
mission: Synchronise the central circadian clock with the external light–dark cycle through retinal light signals.
summary: Light reaching the retina provides a timing signal that helps the central circadian clock track the day–night cycle. Timed light can shift circadian phase; light before bedtime can also suppress the nightly melatonin signal. These are different effects. Practical support therefore concerns the timing and characteristics of light exposure, with the direction of a phase shift depending on internal clock timing.
dose_sensitivity: The comparison is evening room light versus dim light. It is not a lux target, a screen rule, or a daylight prescription.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Evening room light suppresses and shortens melatonin secretion
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In a retrospective analysis of 116 healthy adults aged 18–30, room light before bedtime suppressed melatonin and shortened its duration by about 90 minutes relative to dim light.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: In a retrospective analysis of 116 healthy adults aged 18–30, room light before bedtime suppressed melatonin and shortened its duration by about 90 minutes relative to dim light.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: The exposure changes a central-clock output. Acute suppression is not the same as resetting clock phase, and it is not a cortisol result.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The room-light comparison establishes acute melatonin suppression and shorter secretion. It does not by itself establish a lasting shift of the pacemaker.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Indoor laboratory illumination is not identical to every screen or to daylight. Acute suppression does not establish a durable phase correction.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Timed light changes circadian phase as well as melatonin secretion
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human light exposures can advance or delay circadian phase, depending on their timing.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human light exposures can advance or delay circadian phase, depending on their timing.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Khalsa measured pre/post melatonin phase under constant routines, providing phase-resetting evidence distinct from suppression. Chang provides a separate evening device comparison with delayed circadian timing, sleep and next-morning alertness effects. Neither specifies one best schedule for everyone.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Khalsa measured pre/post melatonin phase under constant routines, providing phase-resetting evidence distinct from suppression. Chang provides a separate evening device comparison with delayed circadian timing, sleep and next-morning alertness effects. Neither specifies one best schedule for everyone. Fargason provides a selected ADHD pilot with a measured phase advance, alongside correlated symptom change.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Timing relative to internal phase, exposure duration, intensity and prior light history matter; laboratory bright-light and eReader protocols are not interchangeable. The uncontrolled ADHD pilot combined morning light and evening restriction and cannot establish symptom mediation or a universal treatment effect.

scientific_findings_intro: The evidence separates three links: retinal photoreception, phase resetting by timed light, and acute suppression of melatonin. Human phase measurements support the entrainment scope; the suppression comparison alone does not. Evening eReader exposure also affected sleep onset and next-morning alertness. Animal photopigment evidence identifies machinery without establishing an extra-intake benefit.

evidence_gaps.title: Dietary retinoid supply to the physiological photopigment cycle
evidence_gaps.establishes: Melanopsin requires a vitamin-A-based chromophore in direct experiments. Acute SCN light-induced gene expression nevertheless persisted in a prolonged dietary-depletion mouse model.
evidence_gaps.cannot_establish: A quantitatively limiting food-to-retinal route for the full circadian entrainment operation, or improved entrainment from additional vitamin A.
evidence_gaps.missing_link: The vitamin-A class combines different precursors; retinal recycling and compensation complicate dietary limitation. No validated form-specific route is represented. A 9-cis rescue analogue is not physiological 11-cis retinal.
evidence_gaps.required_evidence: Reconcile preformed-retinol and carotenoid supply, the physiological photocycle and endpoint-specific depletion evidence. Type A capacity does not require supplementation benefit; no single class-wide conversion should be invented.

title: Feeding-Time Circadian Synchronisation
mission: Coordinate peripheral metabolic clock timing through feeding cues.
summary: Feeding time is a cue for peripheral metabolic clocks, helping organise when tissues process incoming nutrients. Changing meal timing can shift these rhythms without shifting the measured central-clock markers. Human evidence distinguishes the timing of blood glucose from the timing of a clock gene in adipose tissue. The practical route is a defined meal schedule; changing timing is not automatically evidence of better alignment or health.
dose_sensitivity: The comparison is a five-hour delay of meals in a laboratory routine. It is not an eating-window target.

scientific_findings.finding_label: A meal delay shifts peripheral timing without shifting melatonin or cortisol
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In ten healthy men, a five-hour meal delay shifted glucose rhythm timing by 5.69 ± 1.29 hours and adipose PER2 by 0.97 ± 0.29 hours, without significant changes in measured melatonin or cortisol timing.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: In ten healthy men, a five-hour meal delay shifted glucose rhythm timing by 5.69 ± 1.29 hours and adipose PER2 by 0.97 ± 0.29 hours, without significant changes in measured melatonin or cortisol timing.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Peripheral metabolic timing can move while the central melatonin and cortisol signals stay put. A metabolic benefit is not that clock result.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A 13-day ordered laboratory protocol used early meals then six days of late meals. Rhythms were assessed during 37-hour constant routines with hourly snacks. The glucose rhythm shifted much more than adipose PER2; these endpoints are not interchangeable and do not demonstrate improved whole-system alignment.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The sample is ten young men on an ordered laboratory schedule. It does not establish a universal eating window.

title: NAPE → NAE Biosynthesis Capacity
mission: Enable NAPE-to-NAE biosynthesis so endocannabinoidome signalling lipids remain available for stress and motivation regulation.
summary: N-acylethanolamines are signalling lipids made from membrane phospholipid precursors. This mechanism covers the formation step that supplies these molecules, rather than the later receptor responses or their degradation. Brain and enzyme experiments identify the precursor and catalytic machinery. That makes the synthesis pathway biologically meaningful, while leaving open whether particular foods increase neural production. A tested phosphatidylethanolamine meal did not improve satiety; that outcome does not negate its intracellular precursor role.
dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based phospholipid-rich food intake

phenome_relationships.rationale: NAPE → NAE biosynthesis may support AEA, PEA, and OEA signalling context relevant to motivation and drive through diet-actionable endocannabinoidome pathways rather than CB1 receptor pharmacology.
Dietary NAPE and NAE precursor biology may modulate endocannabinoidome context relevant to affective regulation; direct ADHD outcome claims remain cautious.
PEA and related NAEs may intersect with stress-buffering endocannabinoidome signalling; dietary phospholipid support remains the primary intervention frame.

dietary_supply.statement: The same mineral has established dietary supply through the canonical composition records. Cellular uptake and homeostasis mediate enzyme loading; this is maintenance of capacity, not a claim that extra intake accelerates the reaction.

dietary_input_assessments.assessment_limitations: Human enzyme structure and catalysis establish the metal dependency, not dietary zinc-driven brain NAE flux or benefit above adequacy. Cellular zinc homeostasis and membrane substrate access constrain loading; no extra-zinc recommendation is established.

title: Omega-3-Derived Endocannabinoidome Signalling
mission: Sustain omega-3-derived ethanolamide production so endocannabinoidome neuromodulation stays supplied from dietary fat status.
summary: EPA and DHA can supply the fatty-acid portions of omega-3-derived signalling lipids. DHA conversion into synaptamide has been traced in neuronal cells, while controlled exposures change related ethanolamides in human plasma. This gives a specific precursor-supply role to long-chain omega-3 inputs. It does not make all omega-3 molecules interchangeable: ALA conversion, delivery form, tissue metabolism and degradation affect the route. Neural production and clinical responses must be distinguished from circulating lipid measurements.
dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based omega-3 intake with membrane incorporation context

phenome_relationships.rationale: Omega-3-derived ethanolamides may support neuroprotective and neurogenesis-related signalling context relevant to cognitive clarity without CB1-centric framing.
DHEA and related omega-3 ethanolamides may intersect with anti-inflammatory and stress-buffering endocannabinoidome pathways.
Omega-3 endocannabinoidome signalling may indirectly modulate affective context through inflammatory and neuromodulatory interfaces; direct ADHD evidence remains limited.

title: FAAH-Mediated Endocannabinoid Preservation
mission: Preserve endocannabinoid signalling duration by limiting FAAH-mediated degradation of anandamide and related NAEs.
summary: FAAH is an enzyme that breaks down anandamide and related signalling lipids. Its activity helps determine how long a locally produced signal remains available. Rat pharmacology and laboratory assays establish that changing this clearance step can alter anandamide effects. They do not establish that eating soy, polyphenol-rich foods or a general phospholipid diet inhibits brain FAAH. The useful distinction is between a verified clearance mechanism and a dietary intervention that still needs exposure-specific evidence.

title: Endocannabinoid–Dopamine Neuromodulation
mission: Shape dopaminergic reward and motivation pathways through endocannabinoid neuromodulatory interaction.
summary: Endocannabinoid signalling can influence dopamine responses to reward-predicting cues. The relevant job is local circuit modulation, rather than producing lipid precursors or slowing their degradation. Rat experiments identify a VTA CB1-dependent route and distinguish 2-AG augmentation from anandamide administration. Those distinctions matter because two signalling lipids need not produce the same response. The evidence explains a mechanism contributing to cue-driven behaviour; it does not establish that a nutrient or food improves human motivation through this circuit.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Endocannabinoid signalling modulates dopaminergic reward and motivation pathways; this PM addresses neuromodulation rather than dopamine production.

title: Endocannabinoid Stress-Buffering Capacity
mission: Sustain endocannabinoid-mediated stress buffering so HPA-axis and neuroinflammatory reactivity stay proportionate.
summary: Endocannabinoid signals participate in stress regulation through region-specific brain circuits. In rats, stress-related anandamide clearance in the amygdala contributes to HPA-axis activation. Human exercise after a fear-learning protocol changes circulating anandamide and later threat responses, providing a bounded practice candidate. These are complementary findings, not a single measured gut-to-brain or diet-to-stress chain. The evidence supports investigating stress recovery while keeping peripheral lipid measurements, neural mechanisms and neuroinflammatory outcomes separate.
dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based endocannabinoidome support across stress and inflammatory context

title: Oestrogen Signalling Stability
mission: Maintain stable oestrogen-linked signalling so dopamine tone and emotional regulation remain steady across hormonal fluctuation.
summary: Oestrogen signalling interacts with neural systems involved in working memory and emotional processing. Human evidence indicates that responses vary with dopamine-related baseline context, so more hormone or less fluctuation is not automatically better. This mechanism concerns that interaction, rather than intestinal hormone recycling. Dietary exposures may change measured hormone concentrations, but those changes alone do not show steadier neural signalling. The practical boundary is to keep receptor biology separate from claims for fibre, soy or generic micronutrient supplementation.
dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based; life-stage and cycle context matter

phenome_relationships.rationale: Oestrogen influences neural signalling systems relevant to cognitive stability across menstrual and perimenopausal contexts; ADHD-specific outcome claims should remain cautious.
Oestrogen-mediated signalling may modulate affective regulation pathways that intersect with dopaminergic tone and stress sensitivity.
Oestrogen influences dopaminergic and neural signalling systems relevant to executive function; direct single-mechanism ADHD outcome claims should remain cautious.

title: Estrobolome Regulation
mission: Shape systemic oestrogen exposure through microbiome-mediated regulation of oestrogen metabolism and recycling.
summary: Some gut bacterial enzymes remove glucuronide groups from conjugated oestrogens, making the free hormones available for further handling. This is a specific recycling step, not a claim that every microbiome change improves hormone balance. Enzyme studies identify which reactions can occur, while dietary studies provide only partial evidence about systemic exposure. Supporting the gut generally therefore cannot be equated with controlling these enzymes. The key next link is whether an exposure changes this conversion and its contribution to circulating hormone availability.
dose_sensitivity: Daily fermentable substrate with plant-diversity pattern

phenome_relationships.rationale: The estrobolome can influence systemic oestrogen exposure through microbial beta-glucuronidase activity; downstream affective phenome effects are indirect and should not be presented as single-mechanism causal claims.
Altered oestrogen recycling may indirectly influence neural signalling context relevant to cognitive clarity without establishing direct single-pathway outcome certainty.
Estrobolome activity may support or disrupt oestrogen exposure depending on microbial beta-glucuronidase balance and enterohepatic recycling direction.

previous_records.summary: Supports microbiome-mediated regulation of oestrogen metabolism, deconjugation, recycling, and elimination through beta-glucuronidase activity and enterohepatic circulation (the estrobolome, the collective gut-microbial capacity to metabolise and recycle oestrogens). This pathway links gut ecology directly to systemic oestrogen exposure, meaning microbial composition can influence hormone levels independently of ovarian output itself. Fibre and plant-diversity intake that shapes microbial beta-glucuronidase activity therefore has downstream consequences for oestrogen signalling stability elsewhere in the system.

phenome_relationships.rationale: The estrobolome can influence systemic oestrogen exposure through microbial beta-glucuronidase activity; downstream affective phenome effects are indirect and should not be presented as single-mechanism causal claims.
Altered oestrogen recycling may indirectly influence neural signalling context relevant to cognitive clarity without establishing direct single-pathway outcome certainty.
Estrobolome activity may support or disrupt oestrogen exposure depending on microbial beta-glucuronidase balance and enterohepatic recycling direction.

title: Progesterone-Supportive Microbial Metabolism
mission: Sustain microbial contributions to progesterone-related hormonal stability through gut ecosystem function.
summary: Gut bacteria can convert a host-derived biliary steroid into progestin metabolites. Defined culture and mouse experiments identify hydrogen as an important resource for this conversion. This gives the page a concrete microbial process to assess, but it does not yet establish maintenance of circulating progesterone or hormonal stability. The distinction matters for implementation: generic fibre intake or a named bacterium cannot be presented as a hormone-supporting requirement without evidence connecting that exposure to the conversion and the relevant physiological endpoint.

title: Metabolic-Reproductive Hormone Integration
mission: Enable coordinated integration of insulin and metabolic signalling with reproductive hormone balance.
summary: Metabolic signals can influence reproductive hormone production, rather than merely accompanying it. Insulin experiments in ovarian cells identify one direct connection. In women with PCOS, a low-glycaemic-index dietary pattern improved selected insulin-sensitivity and menstrual-cycle readouts compared with a healthy comparison diet. This supports a contextual dietary-practice route, not a requirement for one isolated food or nutrient. The endocrine response depends on the population and treatment context; improved cyclicity does not establish a uniform change in every reproductive hormone.
dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based glycaemic stability with fermentable substrate support

phenome_relationships.rationale: Insulin sensitivity and metabolic stability interact with reproductive hormone regulation; this PM should be framed as metabolic-endocrine integration rather than a direct ADHD treatment claim.
Metabolic volatility may indirectly influence affective regulation through neuroendocrine and reproductive hormone coupling.
Insulin-linked metabolic signalling and gut ecological context may modulate oestrogen-progesterone balance across feeding and stress cycles.

title: Testosterone Signalling Stability
mission: Maintain androgen receptor signalling so motivation, stamina, and goal-directed effort remain well supported.
summary: Androgen signalling depends partly on the availability of hormones that activate its receptors. Nutritional and sleep conditions can influence this upstream supply, although hormone concentration is not a direct receptor-activity measurement. Small human studies found lower testosterone during zinc restriction and sleep restriction, with repletion findings confined to marginal zinc deficiency. These results support bounded supply and lifestyle relationships. They do not establish that extra zinc increases motivation or that manipulating testosterone is an appropriate goal for adequately nourished people.
dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based; androgen exposure context and life-stage matter

phenome_relationships.rationale: Testosterone signalling has been associated with motivation, effort, behavioural activation and goal-directed behaviour.
Low testosterone states are associated with reduced energy, fatigue and reduced mental stamina, but direct ADHD-specific evidence remains limited.
Androgen signalling may influence mood and emotional regulation through interactions with multiple neural systems.

title: Androgen-Microbiome Regulation
mission: Shape systemic androgen exposure through microbiome-mediated androgen metabolism and recycling.
summary: The gut microbiota can alter androgens within intestinal contents by releasing hormones from conjugated forms. Mouse comparisons and human stool measurements support this local metabolic job. They do not establish how much hormone returns to circulation or changes neural androgen signalling. The relationship also runs in the other direction: hormone exposures can change microbial communities. Keeping these directions separate prevents a generic fibre or microbiome intervention from being treated as an established way to regulate systemic androgen availability.
dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based fermentable substrate support for microbial ecology
